有号鹤者，自不见山中来，于封龙山上再兴书院。其为墨者，而不独授墨学。引学子探格物致知之理，研百工致用之术，所求宏愿，乃为令天下人救天下者也。契丹南下，烽火骤涌，书院师生，为之奈何？此院之志，可得几成？
en:
Dragonbend Mountain has towered since antiquity. Since the Han Dynasty, the tradition of scholarship has flourished within its peaks. Yet amidst the upheavals of the late Tang, the halls of learning fell into neglect, and the voices of recitation fell silent.
Then came Crane from Hidden Mountain to revive the academy upon the heights of Dragonbend Mountain. Though a Mohist, he taught more than the creed of his sect, guiding students in the investigation of things and the practicality of crafts. His grand ambition was to empower all under heaven to be their own saviors. As the Khitans march south and beacon fires ignite the horizon, what fate awaits the academy? Of its founding resolve, how much shall survive the storm?

en:
【Airs of the States · Airs of Gui】

Lamb's Fur

In lamb's fur you roam at ease; In fox's fur you attend court. Do I not think of you? My heart is troubled and sore.
In lamb's fur you wander free; In fox's fur you're in the hall. Do I not think of you? My heart is sad and full of gall.
Lamb's fur shines like grease; In sunlight it gleams bright. Do I not think of you? My heart is filled with fright.

Plain Cap

Can I see the plain cap? The gaunt man looks so thin, My heart is full of care.
Can I see the plain robe? My heart is filled with grief, I long to go with you.
Can I see the plain knee-cover? My heart is tied in knots, I long to be one with you.

zh:
八仙喝了酒，就要过海。铁拐李把拐杖扔进海里，站在上面；吕洞宾踩着宝剑；何仙姑坐着荷花……他们不用船，就能去任何地方。而我们几个骑上了小羊，对它说：“带我们到天上去吧。”
小羊听懂了我们的话，原地蹦了三蹦，后蹄一蹬，嗖的一下蹿上了天。我们攥住羊毛，在白云间穿来穿去，像在海里游泳，低头看去，海离我们很远很远，船小得像蚂蚁一样。
后来下起了雨，云越来越低，我们冲进了海里。一群虾兵蟹将举着叉子冒出来，冲我们大喊：“龙王有令，凡人不得过海！”
我们还没来得及说话，小羊先不干了。它深吸一口气，肚子鼓得圆滚滚的，然后大声地“咩”了一嗓子，头一顶，虾兵蟹将们全被顶飞了！
小羊还嫌不过瘾，撅着蹄子踹了一脚云，散开的云彩正好砸在龙王爷头上。龙王爷气坏了，向我们冲来，小羊一扬蹄子，就带我们飞出了海面！
八仙施展法力，用石块在我们前方组成长桥，小羊撒开蹄子就往桥上跑，哒哒哒哒，跑得比鸟飞得还快。
龙王在我们身后追，小羊一扭头，叼走了龙王爷的叉子，往背上一甩，驮着就跑。
龙王在后面喊：“哎呦我的叉子——”小羊头也不回，“咩咩”大叫着往前。
前面忽然起了大雾，白茫茫的啥也看不见了。雾里冒出一艘大船，船头雕着一条胖乎乎的鱼，灯笼挂了一排，是八仙在为我们引路！
小羊跟着那艘船走，大雾散了，眼前冒出一座山，山上楼阁层层叠叠，仙鹤欢快地叫着，乐声不知从哪儿飘过来。八仙站在山口，笑着等我们，告诉我们那就是蓬莱。
我们进入了八仙的宴席，吃了好多没见过的仙果和仙菜，小羊也得了满满一槽仙草，欢快地打起滚来！
en:
Having partaken in wine, the Eight Immortals set forth to cross the sea. Iron-Crutch Li cast his staff into the waters and stood atop it; Lyu Dongbin rode his flying sword; Immortal Maiden He drifted along upon a lotus bloom. Without need of any boat, they could venture wherever they pleased. As for us, we climbed onto the back of our little goat and said to it, "Take us up to the heavens!" Understanding our words, the little goat bounded three times in place, kicked off with its hind hooves, and shot straight into the sky with a swift whoosh. We gripped its fur tight as we weaved through the white clouds like swimmers in an azure sea. Looking down, the ocean was far, far below, and the great ships looked no bigger than tiny ants.
Before long, rain began to fall. The clouds sank lower and lower until we plunged straight into the sea. A patrol of crustacean guards bristling with tridents rose from the depths, shouting at us, "By order of the Dragon King, no mortal shall cross this sea!" Before we could utter a single word, the little goat took offense. Taking a deep breath until its belly puffed round as a drum, it let out a mighty "Baaah!", lowered its horns, and charged, sending the whole troop of crab and shrimp guards flying in all directions! Still eager for more mischief, the little goat kicked at a cloud with its hind hooves, sending it tumbling squarely onto the Dragon King's head. Furious, the Dragon King charged straight toward us, but with another brisk kick, the little goat carried us soaring right out of the water!
The Eight Immortals conjured their magic, assembling river stones into a long bridge ahead of us. The little goat broke into a wild gallop across the stones, its hooves clattering clip-clop, clip-clop, running even faster than a bird in flight. As the Dragon King gave chase from behind, the little goat whipped its head around, snatched the Dragon King's trident in its teeth, flipped it onto its back, and bolted forward with the prize. The Dragon King wailed from behind, "Hey, my trident!" But the little goat never once looked back, bleating merrily as it bounded ahead.
Suddenly, a thick white mist rose before us, cloaking everything in sight. Out of the haze emerged a grand vessel, its prow carved in the shape of a plump fish and adorned with a gleaming row of lanterns: the Eight Immortals had come to guide our way!
Following closely behind the ship, we watched the fog gently roll away to reveal a majestic mountain. Pavilions and grand towers rose in graceful tiers, celestial cranes called in delight, and ethereal music drifted softly on the breeze. The Eight Immortals stood smiling at the mountain pass, waiting to welcome us and telling us that this was none other than Mount Penglai. We joined the grand banquet of the immortals, feasting on wondrous celestial fruits and delicacies we had never seen before, while our little goat received a trough piled high with divine herbs, happily rolling about in pure delight!
But a prodigy

When Wang Qing left the Well of Heaven, he knelt before the Spring and Autumn Hall for three days and nights. She could not understand his betrayal then: in a world so vast, why was he the one who had to save it? Could he even save it?

Yet in this world, though mountains crumble and allies flee, survival rests on our own strength and the bonds of our comrades. If you must wade into the mire alone, three hundred disciples will still follow and fight by your side.

en:
The Gold Leaf Case, Chapter I 
A gold leaf woven with grass hung from a tree in the west, prompting the rumor that the Gold Leaf Warrior has returned. The body that was also hanging from the tree was identified as Wu, a refugee from the area, with a speculated time of death between eleven and one at night. 
Standing just a little over six feet tall, Wu was short-tempered and violent. It is said that he worked with the Khitan for money, and had a lot of enemies. The victim had several bruises on his body, possibly indicating that he had been in a physical fight with someone before his death. 
(Note: The suspect would have to be someone tall and strong, which were not features of the Gold Leaf Warrior based on past cases. How strange!)

三秒，落座后三秒一定会传来熟悉的啰嗦。
“说了多少回了！不要玩到天黑后回家！”
“就你那三脚猫功夫，遇上无忧帮，被卖去鬼樊楼怎么办！”
“别给老子装死，说你呢，阿如！还有你，阿错！”
“狐狸”阿郑若在，便装模作样地劝劝，“师公，别在门口守着了，下回我看着他们。也是……别让师傅久等不是。”
娘亲每到这时，若是清清嗓，瞧门口瞥两眼，那掌勺的必是臊眉耷眼地贴过来——很好，今日又是万事大吉。

月光依旧，月光下的那些人，却都不见了。
en:
At Zi hour, Feng Ruzhi once again stood by the Yellow River, staring out at the sails fluttering faintly in the moonlit breeze, waiting for the one who had promised to come home.

She remembered. A long, long time ago, when she was still a little kid, there had been someone else standing by the riverbank, arms akimbo, waiting. That figure, chewing on a sprig of foxtail grass, hair tousled like the wind had scruffed it apart, was a little frightening under the moonlight. Back then, A'Cuo had still been timid, unlike herself, who was already bold and brash. Without a second thought, she had grabbed A'Cuo by the collar, barreled past the cook standing at the doorframe, and sat down at the table in one breath.

Three seconds. Within three seconds of sitting down, the jibber-jabber would start.

"How many times do I have to tell you? Do not stay out playing until it's dark!"

"With your half-baked skills, if you run into the Unbound Cavern, you'll end up sold to the Ghost Revelry Hall!"

"Don't you dare play dead! I'm talking to you, A'Ru! You too, A'Cuo!"

If "Fox" A'Zheng was around, he'd strike a pose and try to smooth things over:

"Master Pops, come now, don't stand in the doorway. I'll keep an eye on them next time. It's not good to keep the master waiting, either."

If Mother were to clear her throat and look toward the door, that cook would instantly droop his head and shuffle himself inside. That was the signal for another peaceful night.

The moonlight remained the same. But the people beneath it were gone.
Men Shaoluo
What is going on?!

en: Then there are those who leave the dead to their rest, preferring instead to swindle the living. They forge imitation relics, bury them in the damp earth to manufacture the rot of ages, carve them with false inscriptions, and peddle them in the marketplace to eager, gullible collectors. Fortunately, most of these charlatans are woefully unread, rendering their counterfeits utterly absurd. They will offer up a folding stool and swear it was the seat of the ancient Duke of Zhou, or hawk a paper fan claiming it was held by Confucius himself. Some even forge imperial seals of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, foolishly carving the words "Seal of Emperor Wu," oblivious to the fact that "Wu" was a posthumous title bestowed only after his death. It does not take a master antiquarian to unravel such clumsy lies. A village child reciting his first primers could see right through them.

zh:
【檀弓下第四】

君之适长殇，车三乘；公之庶长殇，车一乘；大夫之适长殇，车一乘。
公之丧，诸达官之长杖。
君于大夫，将葬，吊于宫，及出，命引之，三步则止。如是者三，君退。朝亦如之，哀次亦如之。
五十无车者，不越疆而吊人。
季武子寝疾，𫊸固不说齐衰而入见，曰：斯道也，将亡矣。士唯公门说齐衰。武子曰：不亦善乎！君子表微。及其丧也，曾点倚其门而歌。
大夫吊，当事而至，则辞焉。吊于人，是日不乐。妇人不越疆而吊人。行吊之日，不饮酒食肉焉。吊于葬者，必执引，若从柩及圹，皆执绋。
丧，公吊之，必有拜者，虽朋友州里舍人可也。吊曰：寡君承事。主人曰：临。君遇柩于路，必使人吊之。大夫之丧，庶子不受吊。
妻之昆弟为父后者死，哭之适室，子为主，祖免哭踊，夫入门右，使人立于门外，告来者，狎则入哭父在，哭于妻之室；非为父后者，哭诸异室。
有殡，闻远兄弟之丧，哭于侧室无侧室，哭于门内之右。同国，则往哭之。
子张死，曾子有母之丧，齐衰而往哭之。或曰：齐衰不以吊。曾子曰：我吊也与哉？
有若之丧，悼公吊焉，子游摈，由左。
齐榖王姬之丧，鲁庄公为之大功。或曰：由鲁嫁，故为之服姊妹之服。或曰：外祖母也，故为之服。
晋献公之丧，秦穆公使人吊公子重耳，且曰：寡人闻之，亡国恒于斯，得国恒于斯。虽吾子俨然在忧服之中，丧亦不可久也，时亦不可失也，孺子其图之。以告舅犯，舅犯曰：孺子其辞焉。丧人无宝，仁亲以为宝，父死之谓何？又因以为利，而天下其孰能说之？孺子其辞焉。公子重耳对客曰：君惠吊亡臣重耳，身丧父死，不得与于哭泣之哀，以为君忧。父死之谓何？或敢有他志，以辱君义。稽颡而不拜，哭而起，起而不私。子显以致命于穆公。穆公曰：仁夫，公子重耳！夫稽颡而不拜，则未为后也，故不成拜。哭而起，则爱父也；起而不私，则远利也。
……
en:
【Tan Gong II (Part 4)】

When the eldest son of a ruler dies prematurely, three carriages are used; when the eldest son of a noble by a concubine dies prematurely, one carriage is used; when the eldest son of a high official dies prematurely, one carriage is used.
At the funeral of a noble, all officials in active service support the mourning staff.
When a ruler mourns for a high official, he goes to the ancestral temple to offer condolences before the burial. When the coffin is brought out, he orders the bearers to halt, and they stop after three steps. This is done three times, after which the ruler withdraws. The same is done at the court, and likewise at the place of lamentation.
Those who are fifty years old and have no carriage do not cross the border to offer condolences.
When Ji Wuzi lay ill in bed, Jiao Gu, without taking off his mourning garments of coarse hemp, entered to see him, saying, "This practice is about to be lost. Only at the ruler's gate do scholars remove their mourning garments." Wuzi said, "Is this not excellent! The gentleman reveals what is subtle." At his funeral, Zeng Dian leaned against his gate and sang.
When a high official offers condolences, if he arrives during the funeral rites, he is politely declined. On the day one offers condolences to another, one does not play music. Women do not cross the border to offer condolences. On the day of offering condolences, one does not drink wine or eat meat. When offering condolences at a burial, one must hold the rope pulling the carriage; if following the coffin to the grave, all hold the ropes.
At a funeral, when the ruler offers condolences, there must be someone to respond with the formal bow, even if it be a friend, a fellow countryman, or a lodger. The condolence is expressed: "Our ruler has taken part in the service." The host replies: "We are honored by your presence." If the ruler encounters a coffin on the road, he must send someone to offer condolences. At the funeral of a high official, sons by concubines do not receive condolences.
When the brother of one's wife, who is the heir of his father, dies, one weeps for him in the main chamber. The son acts as the chief mourner, baring his arms and leaping in lamentation. The husband enters from the right side of the gate and has someone stand outside the gate to announce arrivals. If the visitor is familiar, he enters and weeps. If the father is alive, one weeps in the wife's chamber; if the deceased is not the heir of his father, one weeps in a different chamber.
When there is an unburied coffin in the house and one hears of the death of a distant brother, one weeps in the side chamber. If there is no side chamber, one weeps inside the gate on the right. If the deceased is in the same state, one goes to weep at his home.
When Zizhang died, Zengzi, who was in mourning for his mother, went in coarse mourning garments to weep for him. Someone said, "One does not offer condolences in coarse mourning garments." Zengzi said, "Am I offering condolences?"
At the funeral of You Ruo, Duke Dao offered condolences, with Ziyou acting as the usher, standing on the left.
At the funeral of King Ji of Qi, Duke Zhuang of Lu wore the mourning of nine months for her. Some said, "Because she was married from Lu, he wore the mourning appropriate for a sister." Others said, "She was his maternal grandmother, so he wore mourning for her."
At the funeral of Duke Xian of Jin, Duke Mu of Qin sent a messenger to offer condolences to Prince Chong'er, saying, "I have heard that the loss of a state often occurs at such a time, and the gaining of a state also often occurs at such a time. Although you, sir, are solemnly in the midst of mourning, mourning cannot last forever, and the opportunity cannot be lost. Young man, consider this." Chong'er reported this to his uncle Fan, who said, "Young man, decline the offer. The exiled have no treasure; they treasure benevolence and kinship. What does the death of a father mean? To use it for personal gain—who in the world could justify that? Young man, decline the offer." Prince Chong'er replied to the messenger, "Your ruler has graciously offered condolences to the exiled subject Chong'er. In my exile and my father's death, I cannot participate in the lamentations and grief, and this has caused your ruler concern. What does the death of a father mean? How dare I harbor other intentions, to disgrace your ruler's righteousness?" He knocked his head on the ground but did not perform the formal bow, wept as he rose, and after rising did not speak privately with the messenger. Zixian then delivered this message to Duke Mu. Duke Mu said, "How benevolent is Prince Chong'er! Knocking his head without performing the formal bow shows that he does not claim to be the heir, and therefore does not complete the full ceremony. Weeping as he rose shows his love for his father; rising without private speech shows his distance from personal gain."

李祚不知从哪儿翻出这书卷拿与柳青衣。二人对这凝露酿起了兴趣，约好于寅时掩人耳目，偷着去寻这山间清露。日夜交替之时，前路未明，柳青衣一时不察竟然踏空。还没来得及唤出那个令她安心的“祚”字，就见李祚因伸手捞她被裹挟着一道滚下山坡。

幸得一对双生桃花树拦在路中，堪堪接住二人。枝头粉雪中，一点濡湿，仿若山间清露般落在了柳青衣的脸颊上。她循着这触感讶异地转头，却撞见少年眼中满溢的欢喜。
en:
There was once a scroll in the Tang Palace recording some winemaking methods. One section on "Dewcrafted Brew" read: "A hundred and twenty kilograms of glutinous rice, ten taels of yeast, blended with two hundred and forty kilograms of mountain dew. Let it ferment under cloudy skies for seven days, and fine wine shall form."

Li Zuo somehow found this scroll and showed it to Liu Qingyi. The two grew interested in the Dewdrop Wine and agreed to secretly seek mountain dew in the morning. As day turned to night and the path ahead was unclear, Liu Qingyi accidentally missed her step. Before she could call out "Zuo"—the name that always comforted her—she saw Li Zuo grab her and get pulled down the hillside with her.

Miraculously, a pair of twin peach trees broke their fall. Amidst the snowfall of pink petals, a single drop—like mountain dew—landed on Liu Qingyi's cheek. Startled, she turned, only to meet the boy's eyes, brimming with unrestrained joy.

en: The name "Broken Bridge" dates back to the Tang Dynasty, immortalized by Bai Juyi's verse lamenting its rough and desolate moss. In his day, the bridge was likely smothered in wild growth; today, it is veiled by weeping willows, the long causeway draped across the water like a trailing silk ribbon. The landscape has transformed entirely. When the winter snows finally break, the white frost atop the bridge's arch melts first, while the causeway banks remain heavily blanketed. From a distance, the snowline appears abruptly severed, earning the beloved title, "Lingering Snow on the Broken Bridge." Since antiquity, this has been the lake's most bustling crossing. I only fear that one day, buckling beneath the sheer weight of the endless crowds, the bridge might truly break.

好侄儿：
你父亲病逝一事，我们都很伤心，望你节哀，早日振作起来，重整商队。
遥想当年，你父亲带着我们商队的一群兄弟，一遍遍地拜访藤王村,和村民共谋复业之事，一度已经重振了藤王美酒昔日盛名……
可惜，天下不太平，想要重现葡萄园昔日繁华终归是奢望。
你父亲这些年始终不肯荒废玉露台这条赔钱的商路……兄弟们嘴上抱怨，但心里都割舍不下村中的几位守藤老人。
如今你父亲先一步去了，我和你的几位叔叔年纪也大了……我们商量了一晚上，决定采纳大家的意见，以后不再走这条道了。
虽然这些年战乱不断，但天下终会重归太平……届时，藤王之名必将传遍四海！
一定会有那么一天的。
en:
Good nephew,

We're gutted by the news about your father. Mourn him, but then you need to get back on your feet and take charge of the caravan.

I can still picture him, dragging us brothers out to Kingvine Village over and over, trying to get things going with the locals... A damn shame he never saw the Kingvine Wine get its name back.

He was stubborn, your father. Kept that Cleardew Terrace route open all these years, even though it was a money pit. We complained, sure, but none of us had the heart to turn our backs on the old folks still tending the vines there.

Well, he's gone now, and the rest of us aren't getting any younger. We debated all night and we've made a decision—we're done with that route. We can't afford it anymore.

These wars won't last forever. The world will find peace again... And when it does, everyone will know the name Kingvine Wine!

That day is coming. You can bet on it.

Stone Ram Bastion was named after the ancient Shiyang River. The princess built canals and dams to gather Han and Wusun artisans, channeling snowmelt from the mountains, clearing the Jade Pool and Wine Spring.

Mutun came back and destroyed the bastion. Only that broken stele remains, recording the princess's great deeds of yesteryear.

【昭公第十】

元年，春，王正月，公即位。
继正即位，正也。
○叔孙豹会晋赵武、楚公子围、齐国弱、宋向戌、卫齐恶、陈公子招、蔡公孙归生、郑罕虎、许人、曹人于郭。
○三月，取郓。
○夏，秦伯之弟针出奔晋。
诸侯之尊，弟兄不得以属通。其弟云者，亲之也。亲而奔之，恶也。
○六月，丁巳，邾子华卒。
○晋荀吴帅师败狄于大原。
传曰，中国曰大原，夷狄曰大卤，号从中国，名从主人。
○秋，莒去疾自齐入于莒，莒展出奔吴。
○叔弓帅师疆郓田。
疆之为言犹竟也。
○葬邾悼公。
○冬，十有一月，己酉，楚子卷卒。
十楚公子比出奔晋。

二年，春，晋侯使韩起来聘。
○夏，叔弓如晋。
○秋，郑杀其大夫公孙黑。
○冬，公如晋，至河乃复。
耻如晋，故着有疾也。
○季孙宿如晋。
公如晋而不得入，季孙宿如晋而得入，恶季孙宿也。

……
en:
【Duke Zhao, Volume 10】

First year, spring, the king's first month, the Duke ascended the throne.
Succeeding the rightful ruler and ascending the throne is proper.
○Shusun Bao met with Jin's Zhao Wu, Chu's Prince Wei, Qi's Guo Ruo, Song's Xiang Xu, Wei's Qi E, Chen's Prince Zhao, Cai's Gongsun Guisheng, Zheng's Han Hu, Xu's envoy, and Cao's envoy at Guo.
○In the third month, took Yun.
○In summer, Zhen, the younger brother of the Duke of Qin, fled to Jin.
For the honor of the feudal lords, brothers are not communicated with by kinship. The term "his younger brother" indicates closeness. Being close yet fleeing is reprehensible.
○In the sixth month, on Ding Si day, Zhu's ruler Hua died.
○Jin's Xun Wu led troops and defeated the Di at Taiyuan.
The commentary says: In the Central States, it is called Taiyuan; among the barbarians, it is called Dalu. The designation follows the Central States, while the name follows the local ruler.
○In autumn, Ju's Quji entered Ju from Qi, and Ju's Zhan fled to Wu.
○Shu Gong led troops to demarcate the fields of Yun.
"Demarcate" means to establish boundaries.
○Buried Zhu's Duke Dao.
○In winter, in the eleventh month, on Ji You day, Chu's ruler Juan died.
Chu's Prince Bi fled to Jin.

Second year, spring, the Marquis of Jin sent Han Qi on a diplomatic visit.
○In summer, Shu Gong went to Jin.
○In autumn, Zheng executed its high official Gongsun Hei.
○In winter, the Duke went to Jin, reached the Yellow River, and then returned.
Ashamed to go to Jin, thus it was recorded that he was ill.
○Ji Sun Su went to Jin.
The Duke went to Jin but could not enter; Ji Sun Su went to Jin and could enter. This condemns Ji Sun Su.

zh:
【国风·豳风】

七月

七月流火，九月授衣。一之日觱发，二之日栗烈。无衣无褐，何以卒岁。三之日于耜，四之日举趾。同我妇子，馌彼南亩，田畯至喜。
七月流火，九月授衣。春日载阳，有鸣仓庚。女执懿筐，遵彼微行，爰求柔桑。春日迟迟，采蘩祁祁。女心伤悲，殆及公子同归。
七月流火，八月萑苇。蚕月条桑，取彼斧斨，以伐远扬，猗彼女桑。七月鸣鵙，八月载绩。载玄载黄，我朱孔阳，为公子裳。
四月秀葽，五月鸣蜩。八月其获，十月陨萚。一之日于貉，取彼狐狸，为公子裘。二之日其同，载缵武功，言私其豵，献豜于公。
五月斯螽动股，六月莎鸡振羽，七月在野，八月在宇，九月在户，十月蟋蟀入我床下。穹窒熏鼠，塞向墐户。嗟我妇子，曰为改岁，入此室处。
六月食郁及薁，七月亨葵及菽，八月剥枣，十月获稻，为此春酒，以介眉寿。七月食瓜，八月断壶，九月叔苴，采荼薪樗，食我农夫。
九月筑场圃，十月纳禾稼。黍稷重穋，禾麻菽麦。嗟我农夫，我稼既同，上入执宫功。昼尔于茅，宵尔索綯。亟其乘屋，其始播百谷。
二之日凿冰冲冲，三之日纳于凌阴。四之日其蚤，献羔祭韭。九月肃霜，十月涤场。朋酒斯飨，曰杀羔羊。跻彼公堂，称彼兕觥，万寿无疆。

鸱鸮

鸱鸮鸱鸮，既取我子，无毁我室。恩斯勤斯，鬻子之闵斯。
迨天之未阴雨，彻彼桑土，绸缪牖户。今女下民，或敢侮予？
予手拮据，予所捋荼。予所蓄租，予口卒瘏，曰予未有室家。
予羽谯谯，予尾翛翛，予室翘翘。风雨所漂摇，予维音哓哓！
……
en:
【Airs of the States · Bin】

July

In the seventh month the Fire Star declines;
In the ninth month winter clothes are made.
In the eleventh month keen blows the breeze;
In the twelfth month the air is biting cold.
Without warm garments, how can we get through the year?
In the first month we mend the ploughs and shares;
In the second month we start to work afield.
Together with my wife and children,
I take food to those who toil in southern acres,
For the surveyor of the fields is glad.
In the seventh month the Fire Star declines;
In the ninth month winter clothes are made.
In the days of spring, the sun is warm;
Golden orioles begin to sing.
Girls take their deep baskets
And go along the small paths,
Looking for tender mulberry leaves.
The spring days are lengthening;
They gather white southernwood in crowds.
A girl's heart is sick and sad,
For she will soon go with her lord.
In the seventh month the Fire Star declines;
In the eighth month we gather the reeds.
In the silkworm month we strip the mulberry branches
Of their leaves, and take our axes and hatchets,
To lop off those branches that stretch out far,
And pull the tender ones.
In the seventh month the shrikes are heard;
In the eighth month we begin the spinning.
We make dark fabrics and yellow,
Our red being very bright,
To make robes for our young lord.
In the fourth month the grass is in seed;
In the fifth month the cicadas cry.
In the eighth month the harvest is gathered;
In the tenth month the leaves fall.
In the eleventh month we hunt the raccoon,
Take the foxes and wild cats,
To make furs for our young lord.
In the twelfth month we assemble
To continue our practice at arms.
We keep the small boars for ourselves
And offer the big ones to our lord.
In the fifth month the locusts move their legs;
In the sixth month the spinner shakes its wings.
In the seventh month they are in the fields;
In the eighth month they are under the eaves;
In the ninth month they are at the door;
In the tenth month the crickets enter under our beds.
We stop the holes to smoke out the rats,
And close the northern window and plaster the door.
Alas for my wife and children,
They say, "The year is changing,
Let us go into the house."
In the sixth month we eat plums and grapes;
In the seventh month we boil mallows and beans.
In the eighth month we knock down the dates;
In the tenth month we reap the rice.
With it we make the spring wine,
To help our long life.
In the seventh month we eat melons;
In the eighth month we cut the gourds.
In the ninth month we gather the hemp seeds,
Gather the bitter herbs and cut the ailanthus for firewood,
To feed our farmers.
In the ninth month we prepare the threshing floor;
In the tenth month we bring in the harvest.
Millet of both kinds, hemp, beans and wheat.
Alas for us farmers!
When we have gathered in all our crops,
We have to go up to the big house for other work.
In the daytime we gather the thatch,
And at night we twist it into ropes.
We hasten to repair our houses,
For we shall sow the seeds again.
In the twelfth month we cut the ice with repeated blows;
In the first month we store it in the ice-house.
In the second month we offer early sacrifice,
Presenting a lamb and scallions.
In the ninth month it is cold with frost;
In the tenth month we clear the threshing floor.
With two pitchers of wine we feast,
And kill a lamb for the occasion.
We go up into the hall,
Raise the rhinoceros horn cups,
And wish our lord long life, without end.

The Owl

O owl, O owl,
You have taken my young ones,
Do not destroy my nest.
With love and toil
I have reared my young ones.
Before the sky is overcast with rain,
I gather the roots of the mulberry tree,
And mend the window and door of my nest.
Now you people below,
Who dares to insult me?
My hands are all sore,
I gather the reeds and flowers,
I store up the hemp seeds,
My mouth is all sore,
For I have not yet finished my nest.
My feathers are all worn,
My tail is all bare,
My nest is still unsteady,
Shaken by wind and rain,
I can but cry out in distress!
……

zh:
最近，叮当在附近转悠的时候，听见开封府的老捕头提醒新来的，千万要小心那些身披黑袍、腰系葫芦的家伙。这些家伙贼得很，有时只是打个照面，这些人啊就指不定顺走了你什么宝贝。
叮当被吓得连连后退，胸前的铃铛发出清脆的声响。叮当心里一惊，完蛋了，要是那群家伙惦记上它的宝贝铃铛可怎么办！
毕竟，它这宝贝可神了，一动就响，不动就不响。就这种稀世珍宝，一旦被发现，那些大盗能忍得住？
叮当不敢细想，赶紧去问角门里打架最厉害的大耳朵，有没有跟腰系葫芦的人交过"爪"。大耳朵说自己倒是常在角门里见着这些“黑袍子”，但这些人都身手矫健，偶尔还给些吃食，所以大耳朵不想打，也不敢打。
看来最厉害的大耳朵也不是黑袍大盗的对手。
叮当心下一凉，又蹑手蹑脚地找到了金水门街的狗老大——大聪明，嘱咐它赶紧把这消息传出去。让所有狗都拉长耳朵，提高听觉，护好宝贝，全面戒备！
en:
Recently, while wandering nearby, Jingle overheard an old constable from Kaifeng Prefecture warning a new recruit: beware of those in black robes with gourds at their waists. Those fellows are crafty; in just a passing glance, they might lift your precious belongings.
Jingle backs away in fright, his bell chiming brightly. His heart sinks. Oh no. What if those guys set their sights on his precious bell?
After all, his treasure is magical: move, and it rings; still, and it's silent. Such a rare wonder, once discovered, how could those thieves resist?
Jingle doesn't dare think about it. He rushes to ask Big Ears from the Forsaken Quarter, the toughest fighter, if he has ever crossed claws with anyone wearing a gourd. Big Ears says he often sees those "black robes" around the Forsaken Quarter, but they're agile and occasionally toss him food, so he doesn't want to fight them, and he doesn't dare to.
So even the toughest dog is no match for the black-robed thieves.
Jingle's heart chills. He creeps carefully to find Big Smart, the dog boss of Goldwater Street, urging him to spread the word: all dogs must keep their ears perked, guard their treasures, and be on full alert!

en: Silt irrigation was an essential ancient strategy for reclaiming barren, salt-choked land. Farmers would divert the muddy, sediment-heavy waters of the Yellow River directly onto their fields. As the standing water settled, it left behind a thick layer of nutrient-rich silt. This brilliant process naturally washed away toxic salts, deepened the topsoil, and fertilized the earth, eventually transforming poor, alkaline dirt into highly productive farmland. This technique boasts a particularly rich history along the Yellow River in Shandong province.

醉醉的主人是个狂澜小伙子。
不仅自己爱喝酒，还给狗喝。
喝高了就抱着它说：
“来，兄弟，陪我一口。”
于是狗和人就都喝多了。

人喝多了，还看得出。
狗喝多了，没人看得出。
醉醉只是每次都会跑去附近的田里，找那只北边来的狗，问它，要不要和自己去大漠看看。
大漠的月亮圆，美酒烈，沙子软……

醉醉打了个酒嗝，晕晕乎乎地看着对面的大白狗，汪汪地说些狗也听不懂，人也听不懂的话。
en:
Tipsy's master is a young man from Raging Tides.
Not only does he love to drink, but he also lets his dog drink.
When he's had too much, he holds the dog and says:
Come on, brother, have a sip with me.
And so both the dog and the man end up drunk.

When a man is drunk, you can tell.
When a dog is drunk, no one can tell.
Tipsy just runs to the nearby fields every time to find that dog from the north and asks if he wants to go see the great desert.
The desert moon is round, the wine is strong, the sand is soft...

Tipsy let out a drunken hiccup and looked dizzily at the big white dog, barking things that neither dogs nor humans could understand.

zh:
马二第二次经过天街的时候，也是个雨夜。
他推开了酒馆的门。衣裳和背包湿透，手中却没拿伞。
“马二哥？”贾老板有些诧异。“这么晚了怎么又上来了？”
“妹子，来碗酒。”马二的眼睛因为爬山而充血，声音沙哑。“酒肴就不用了。”
贾老板有些担心，但还是端上了一碗酒并几样热乎小菜。
马二没说话，将那碗酒一饮而尽。酒液顺着嘴角流下，滴滴答答掉在桌子上，就像檐外的雨。
“马二哥，怎的，没找到家门？”贾老板故作轻松。
“……没了。”马二低头，把碗底的酒喝尽。
“没了？那边不是挺多人的吗？”贾老板有些摸不着头脑。
“那不是俺的村子。”马二又自己倒了一碗酒。
“俺一路跑，一路跑，还没到地方就闻着香味了。”
“那味儿和俺阿翁的锅气一个样，也和俺做的菜一样。大火爆炒，浓酱香咸……”
“那不家里的味道么是。”贾老板更是糊涂。
“不是。盐田还在，但是以前村里的路都没了。房子也没了。”马二吸了吸鼻子。
“村里的人，看俺就像陌生人。还有人问俺要不要落脚吃饭。”马二摩挲着酒杯。碗里的小菜不再飘起热气。
“俺说俺是老马家的。可没有人记得俺家。他们说起来的马家也不是俺家。俺不是这个村里的人了，”马二似乎下了很大决心，“俺不是青州人咧……不是青州人咧。”他将杯子放下。“本来俺寻思以后常来店坐坐，现在也没机会咧。上次的酒钱，和这次的一并结了吧。”
“恁要去哪？”贾老板蹙了蹙眉。
“恁要不租俺的店？”贾老板眨眨眼。“俺这店在这街上开了好多年，是俺阿爷张罗起来的。但俺没那两把刷子，店里生意也不咋样。”
“恁说恁做饭和乐安浦一个味儿？那正好，俺这店租给你，开个饭馆子咋样？”贾老板环顾四周，“别看俺这店现在冷清，在这街上，只要有手艺，生意差不了！”
“俺……能在这儿开个饭店？”马二似乎有些不敢相信。
“这样恁就又是青州人了，是咱天街上的人。”
en:
It was raining again the night Ma Er returned to Cloudwalk Street.
He pushed open the tavern door. His clothes and pack were plastered to his body, heavy with water, but this time, he carried no umbrella.
"Brother Ma Er?" Boss Jia stared at him in surprise. "What brings you back up the mountain so late?"
"A bowl of wine, sister," he said. His eyes were bloodshot from the climb, his voice reduced to a raw scrape. "Don't bother with the food."
Troubled by his hollow look, Jia ignored his request, bringing out the wine along with a few steaming dishes anyway.
Ma Er didn't say a word. He lifted the bowl and drained it in a single, desperate swallow. The liquor spilled past his lips, dripping onto the wooden table in time with the rain falling from the eaves outside.
"What is it, Brother Ma Er? Couldn't find your front door?" Jia asked, forcing a lightness into her voice to cut the heavy silence.
"...It's gone." Ma Er lowered his head, staring into the empty bowl.
"Gone? But isn't that place bustling these days?"
"It's not my village anymore," he said, pouring himself another drink.
"I ran all the way. Before I even reached the edge of town, I could smell it. It smelled exactly like my grandpa's cooking, exactly like the dishes I make. The smoky breath of the wok, the rich, savory sauces..."
"Isn't that the taste of home, then?" Jia asked, entirely lost.
"No. The salt flats are still there, but the old roads are gone. The houses are gone, too." Ma Er sniffled, his voice thick.
"The people there looked at me like I was a stranger. Some even asked if I was a tourist looking for a bite to eat." He ran a calloused thumb along the rim of his cup. The small dishes sitting between them had long stopped steaming.
"I told them I was from Old Ma's family. But no one remembered us. The 'Old Ma's family' they talked about wasn't mine. I don't belong to that village anymore." He paused, a terrible finality settling over him. "I'm not a Qingzhou man anymore. I'm just not."
He set his cup down. "I thought I'd come back and sit in your tavern from time to time, but I guess that's not happening. Let me pay for the other night, and for tonight, too."
"Where will you go?" Jia's brow furrowed.
Before he could answer, her expression shifted as an idea took hold. "Why don't you rent my place?"
She blinked, her eyes brightening. "This tavern has been on this street for years. My grandfather built it. But I don't have the hands for this work, and business has been slow."
"You said your cooking tastes just like Tranquil Pier? Perfect. I'll lease this shop to you, and you can run it as a restaurant. What do you say?" She gestured around the quiet room. "Don't let the empty tables fool you. Up here on Cloudwalk Street, if you've got the skill, the crowds will come!"
"I... you'd let me open a place here?" Ma Er looked up, the life slowly returning to his eyes.
"That way, you'll be a Qingzhou man again," Jia said, her smile warm and steady.
"You'll be one of us, right here on Cloudwalk Street."

zh:
【哀公第十二】

元年，春，王正月，公即位。
○楚子、陈侯、随侯、许男围蔡。
○鼷鼠食郊牛角，改卜牛。夏，四月，辛巳，郊。
此该郊之变而道之也。于变之中，又有言焉。鼷鼠食郊牛角，改卜牛，志不敬也。郊牛日展斛角而知伤，展道尽矣。郊自正月至于三月，郊之时也。夏四月郊，不时也。五月郊，不时也。夏之始可以承春，以秋之末承春始，盖不可矣。九月用郊，用者，不宜用者也。郊三卜，礼也。四卜，非礼也。五卜，强也。卜免牲者，吉则免之，不吉则否。牛伤，不言伤之者，伤自牛作也，故其辞缓。全曰牲，伤曰牛，未牲曰牛。其牛一也，其所以为牛者异。有变而不郊，故卜免牛也。已牛也，其尚卜免之何也？礼，与其亡也，宁有，尝置之上帝矣，故卜而后免之，不敢专也。卜之不吉，则如之何？不免。安置之？系而待。六月上甲，始庀牲，然后左右之。予之所言者，牲之变也，而曰我一该郊之变而道之何也？我以六月上甲始庀牲，十月上甲始系牲，十一月、十二月牲虽有变，不道也。待正月，然后言牲之变，此乃所以该郊。郊，享道也，贵其时，大其礼，其养牲虽小，不备可也。子不志三月卜郊何也？自正月至于三月，郊之时也。我以十二月下辛卜正月上辛，如不从，则以正月下辛卜二月上辛。如不从，则以二月下辛卜三月上辛。如不从，则不郊矣。
○秋，齐侯、卫侯伐晋。
○冬，仲孙何忌帅师伐邾。

二年，春，王二月，季孙斯、叔孙州仇、仲孙何忌帅师伐邾，取漷东田及沂西田。癸巳，叔孙州仇、仲孙何忌及邾子盟于句绎。
漷东，未尽也。沂西，未尽也。三人伐而二人盟何也？各盟其得也。
○夏，四月，丙子，卫侯元卒。
○滕子来朝。
○晋赵鞅帅师纳卫世子蒯聩于戚。
纳者，内弗受也。帅师而后纳者，有伐也。何用弗受也？以輙不受也，以輙不受父之命，受之王父也。信父而辞王父，则是不尊王父也。其弗受，以尊王父也。
○秋，八月，甲戌，晋赵鞅帅师及郑罕达战于铁。郑师败绩。
○冬，十月，葬卫灵公。
○十有一月，蔡迁于州来。蔡杀其大夫公子驷。

……
en:
【Duke Ai, Twelfth Year】

First year, spring, the king's first month, the duke assumed the throne.
○The Chu Zi, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Sui, and the Earl of Xu besieged Cai.
○A shrew ate the horn of the suburban sacrifice ox, so a new ox was divined for. Summer, fourth month, Xinsi, the suburban sacrifice was held.
This records the anomalies of the suburban sacrifice and explains them. Within the anomalies, there is further commentary. The shrew eating the horn of the suburban sacrifice ox and the subsequent divination for a new ox marks a lack of reverence. The suburban sacrifice ox was examined daily for horn condition, and the injury was discovered, showing that the examination was thorough. The suburban sacrifice from the first month to the third month is the proper time for it. In the fourth month of summer, it was untimely. In the fifth month, it was also untimely. The beginning of summer can follow spring, but the end of autumn following the beginning of spring is not permissible. In the ninth month, the suburban sacrifice was held; "held" implies it should not have been held. Three divinations for the suburban sacrifice are proper. Four divinations are improper. Five divinations are excessive. When divining to exempt the sacrificial animal, if auspicious, it is exempted; if not auspicious, it is not. When the ox was injured, it was not said that it was injured, because the injury came from the ox itself, hence the wording is lenient. An intact animal is called "sacrificial," an injured one is called "ox," and one not yet designated for sacrifice is called "ox." The animal is the same, but the reason for calling it "ox" differs. When there is an anomaly and the suburban sacrifice is not held, divination is done to exempt the ox. Since it was already an ox, why still divine for its exemption? According to ritual, rather than losing it, it is better to keep it; it had been offered to the Supreme God, so after divination it was exempted, not daring to act arbitrarily. If the divination is not auspicious, what then? It is not exempted. Where is it placed? It is tied up and waited for. On the first Jia day of the sixth month, the sacrificial animal is first prepared, and then it is attended to on both sides. What I speak of concerns anomalies in the sacrificial animal, and yet I say I encompass the anomalies of the suburban sacrifice and explain them—why? I begin preparing the sacrificial animal on the first Jia day of the sixth month, and begin tying it up on the first Jia day of the tenth month. In the eleventh and twelfth months, even if there are anomalies with the animal, they are not mentioned. Only after the first month are anomalies in the animal discussed; this is how the suburban sacrifice is encompassed. The suburban sacrifice is a way of offering, valuing timeliness and magnifying its ritual. Though the rearing of the animal may be minor, incompleteness is acceptable. Why does the master not record the divination for the suburban sacrifice in the third month? From the first month to the third month is the proper time for the suburban sacrifice. I divine on the last Xin day of the twelfth month for the first Xin day of the first month; if it is not followed, then I divine on the last Xin day of the first month for the first Xin day of the second month. If it is not followed, then I divine on the last Xin day of the second month for the first Xin day of the third month. If it is not followed, then the suburban sacrifice is not held.
○Autumn, the Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei attacked Jin.
○Winter, Zhongsun Heji led troops to attack Zhu.

Second year, spring, the king's second month, Jisun Si, Shusun Zhouchou, and Zhongsun Heji led troops to attack Zhu, seizing the fields east of Huo and the fields west of Yi. Guisi, Shusun Zhouchou and Zhongsun Heji made a covenant with the Viscount of Zhu at Gouyi.
East of Huo was not fully taken. West of Yi was not fully taken. Why did three men attack but two made the covenant? Each made a covenant over what they had gained.
○Summer, fourth month, Bingzi, Marquis Yuan of Wei died.
○The Viscount of Teng came for an audience.
○Zhao Yang of Jin led troops to escort the heir apparent Kuai Kui of Wei to Qi.
"Escort" means that internally it was not accepted. Leading troops and then escorting implies there was an attack. Why was it not accepted? Because Zhe did not accept it. Because Zhe did not accept his father's command but accepted that of his grandfather. Trusting the father while rejecting the grandfather means not respecting the grandfather. His not accepting was to respect the grandfather.
○Autumn, eighth month, Jiaxu, Zhao Yang of Jin led troops and fought with Han Da of Zheng at Tie. The Zheng army was defeated.
○Winter, tenth month, Duke Ling of Wei was buried.
○In the eleventh month, Cai moved to Zhoulai. Cai killed its high official, Gongzi Si.

zh:
鲍都头前些年救了一只狗，取名叫大海。大海不通水性，不知为何掉进水里，四条腿都在扑腾，叫鲍都头救上了岸。本想救上来便算了，可大海见他要走便呜咽，听得人心里不是滋味。鲍都头说：“我走三步，不，五步，若你能跟上来，我便养你。”话将将落下，便对上大海潮湿的眼睛。
鲍都头从前的日子像一潭平静的水，他在水中，见到无数人为了名利争相去撞浪头，可他只想踏实地过活。后来，每当看到大海被浪潮吓得躲在自己身后时，鲍都头才惊觉，什么名利富贵，其实都比不上大海高兴时摇动的尾巴重要。
en:
A few years back, Captain Bao saved a dog and named him Ocean. Ocean couldn't swim. Somehow he ended up falling into the water, all four legs thrashing helplessly, until Captain Bao pulled him out. Bao meant to leave it at that, but when he turned to go, Ocean whimpered so pitifully that it struck something deep in his heart. Captain Bao said, "I'll walk three steps—no, five. If you keep up, I'll take you in." No sooner were the words out than he met Ocean's damp, pleading eyes.
Captain Bao's days used to be a still pool of water. Within that water, he had watched countless men scramble after fame and fortune, trying to ride the waves, while all he wanted was a simple, honest life. Later, when he saw Ocean cowering behind him, frightened by the tide, Captain Bao came to realize: no measure of fame or fortune could ever outweigh the joyful wag of Ocean's tail.

【国风·王风】

黍离

彼黍离离，彼稷之苗。行迈靡靡，中心摇摇。知我者，谓我心忧；不知我者，谓我何求。悠悠苍天，此何人哉？

君子于役

君子于役，不知其期，曷至哉？鸡栖于埘，日之夕矣，羊牛下来。君子于役，如之何勿思？
君子于役，不日不月，曷其有佸？鸡栖于桀，日之夕矣，羊牛下括。君子于役，苟无饥渴。

君子阳阳

君子阳阳，左执簧，右招我由房，其乐只且。
君子陶陶，左执翿，右招我由敖，其乐只且。

扬之水

扬之水，不流束薪。彼其之子，不与我戍申。怀哉怀哉，曷月予还归哉？
扬之水，不流束楚。彼其之子，不与我戍甫。怀哉怀哉，曷月予还归哉？
扬之水，不流束蒲。彼其之子，不与我戍许。怀哉怀哉，曷月予还归哉？
……
en:
【Airs of the States - Airs of Wang】

Millet Lush

The millet is lush, the millet sprouts grow. My steps are slow, my heart is troubled. Those who know me say my heart is anxious; those who don't know me ask what I seek. Vast, distant heaven, who is this man?
The millet is lush, the millet forms ears. My steps are slow, my heart is drunk. Those who know me say my heart is anxious; those who don't know me ask what I seek. Vast, distant heaven, who is this man?
The millet is lush, the millet bears grain. My steps are slow, my heart is choked. Those who know me say my heart is anxious; those who don't know me ask what I seek. Vast, distant heaven, who is this man?

My Lord is on Duty

My lord is on duty, I know not for how long, when will he return? The roosters roost in their coops, the sun sets in the west, the sheep and cattle come down. My lord is on duty, how can I not think of him?
My lord is on duty, not by days nor months, when will we meet again? The roosters roost on their perches, the sun sets in the west, the sheep and cattle gather. My lord is on duty, may he not suffer hunger or thirst.

My Lord is Joyous

My lord is joyous, holding a reed pipe in his left hand, beckoning me from the chamber with his right, oh how happy we are!
My lord is content, holding a feather banner in his left hand, beckoning me to wander with his right, oh how happy we are!

Flowing Waters

Flowing waters, cannot carry a bundle of firewood. That man, my dear, does not join me in defending Shen. How I miss him, how I miss him! In which month shall I return?
Flowing waters, cannot carry a bundle of thorns. That man, my dear, does not join me in defending Fu. How I miss him, how I miss him! In which month shall I return?
Flowing waters, cannot carry a bundle of rushes. That man, my dear, does not join me in defending Xu. How I miss him, how I miss him! In which month shall I return?

zh: 白雀经阁本是乌护藏经之地。凉州光复后，在张议潮的帮助下，僧人重修经阁，广传佛音。据说此处藏有诸多珍贵经文。其中最为珍贵的乃五卷《白雀经》，系凉州前代高僧以心头血所书。然而， 妄图闯入经阁、修习经书之人均有去无回。自张议潮决定归唐后，此处便出现了於突的踪迹。那些珍贵的经书亦散落无人收管，似是等有缘人到来。
en: Sparrow Sutra Hall was originally Oghuz's scripture repository. After Liangzhou's liberation, monks rebuilt this hall with Zhang Yichao's assistance, spreading Buddhist teachings far and wide. This place reportedly houses many precious texts. The most precious among them are five volumes of Snow Sparrow Scripture, written in heart's blood by Liangzhou's former high monks. However, all who attempted to break into the hall to study these texts never returned. Since Zhang Yichao decided to rejoin the Tang Dynasty, Utuk traces appeared here. Those precious scriptures now lie scattered and unguarded, seemingly awaiting someone destined to find them.

zh:
<信纸有火燎过的痕迹>

晋安寨对战契丹，大败，赵将军降了。契丹人把我们汉军和银鞍契丹直全都关押了，一并收押的还有各族流民、甚至自个儿家的逃兵败将。还不知要怎么处置。
有月娘所绣平安佩，吾必逢凶化吉。

我们这间一共关了五人，既共处一间，又生死同路，倒也算是缘分。故记名于此。
赵石，家住栾城布坊，有母、弟。家中本有营生，为守土而参军。
周富贵，蔚州人，已无亲眷。为报家仇而参军。
斡特剌，契丹人，家在潢水畔，有一弟一妹。被赵将军俘，编入银鞍契丹直。自言无所求，能活便可。
舍朗，奚人，家在狼河畔，有妻。斡特剌转述，他们部族被契丹人征掠，战败为奴，被强征入伍。他不愿意被契丹人驱使，去侵人土地、杀人妻儿，所以做了逃兵。只愿归家与妻偕老。
赵石大哥说，若能逃出，不如大家一起去栾城经营布坊。舍朗说他妻子绣工很好，可以帮忙。她绣工再好，能有月娘好？
不知此刻月娘在做什么？
en:
(The letter bears scorch marks along the edges.)

At Jin'an Fort, we met the Khitans in battle and suffered a crushing defeat. General Zhao surrendered. The Khitans have imprisoned all of us, Han troops and Silver-Saddle Khitan Regiment alike. They have also rounded up refugees of every sort, even deserters and beaten men from their own side. As yet, no one knows what they mean to do with us.
So long as I carry the peace charm Yueniang embroidered for me, I am certain I will survive this calamity.

There are five of us confined here together. Since we share one room and the same road between life and death, that too must count for a kind of fate. So I set down our names here.
Zhao Shi, from Luancheng's cloth workshops. At home he has his mother and a younger brother. His family once had a trade of their own, but he joined the army to defend his home.
Zhou Fugui, of Weizhou. He has no kin left. He joined the army to avenge his family.
Wo Tela, a Khitan from the Huang River. At home he has a younger brother and sister. He was captured by General Zhao and pressed into the Silver-Saddle Khitan Regiment. He says he asks for nothing, only to stay alive.
She Lang, a man of the Xi, from the Wolf River, married. Wo Tela told me that She Lang's tribe was raided by the Khitans, defeated and enslaved, then forced into service. He would not let the Khitans drive him to seize other men's land and kill other men's wives and children, so he deserted. His only wish is to return home and grow old with his wife.
Brother Zhao Shi said that if we ever escape, we should all go to Luancheng together and open a cloth workshop. She Lang said his wife is deft with the needle and could help.
Skilled though she may be, could she truly compare with Yueniang?
I wonder what Yueniang is doing at this very moment.

zh:
郭昕出身华阴郭氏，满门忠烈，伯父郭子仪曾立下赫赫战功，官拜中书令。
当年在长安城，郭昕也是“春风得意马蹄疾，一日看尽长安花”的少年将军。
满腔热血，一心跟着伯父上阵杀敌，重整河山。
永泰元年，郭昕奉命前往巡抚河西、安西。
在长安拜别伯父之时，伯父以断箭为簪，嘱托郭昕，宁折不弯。
郭昕回望这坐曾经锦绣成堆，又遭遇铁蹄踏破的长安城，抱拳，转头，打马向西。 
他未曾想，这一眼便是一辈子。
西北，险呐。
外有强敌，内无援兵。粮饷不继，兵覆甘州。东西阻绝，孤悬绝域。
建中二年，终于盼来了唐廷御诏：
“北庭四镇，统任西夏五十七蕃、十姓部落，国朝已来，相奉率职。自关陇失守，东西阻绝，忠义之徒，泣血相守，慎固封略，奉遵礼教，皆侯伯守将，交修共治之所致也。其将士叙官，可超七资。”
七资，可抵粮草？
七资，可抵兵马？
七资，七资……七资在安西只能算是个短命的盼头儿，挨不过几时，就消散了，可有盼头儿总比没有好。
西北的这数十年，这成千上万条命，多少军民的血与泪。
记不清了，华发满头的郭昕，站在城门口，望着数十白头军。
背后，是冲天的火光，是敌军的千军万马。
万箭如雨，落在身上之时，竟不觉得痛，郭昕只是想起一个人。
那位多年前割袍断义的故友，曾问他，此生可悔？
当时郭昕一字一顿，铿锵有力的说，百死不悔。
可此刻，他好悔呐。悔身败于此，愧对背后这数十白头军。
他再不能守着他此生最眷恋的大唐了。
“大唐，长安……”
无人知道，这是他战死前最后说的话。
郭昕，生于长安，死于龟兹，苦守安西，一生未退。
en:
Guo Xin hailed from the Huayin Guo clan, a family full of loyal martyrs. His uncle, Guo Ziyi, had achieved illustrious military feats, rising to the position of Secretariat Director. 
Back in Chang'an, Guo Xin was also the young general who "galloped his horse joyfully in the spring breeze, viewing all Chang'an's flowers in a single day." 
Filled with fervor, his sole desire was to follow his uncle to the battlefield, slay the enemy, and restore the realm. 
In the first year of the Yongtai era, Guo Xin was ordered to patrol and pacify Hexi and Anxi. 
When bidding farewell to his uncle in Chang'an, his uncle used a broken arrow as a hairpin, entrusting Guo Xin to break rather than bend. 
Guo Xin looked back at Chang'an, this city once piled with splendor, then trampled by iron hooves. He clasped his fists, turned, and rode west.  
He never imagined that this glance would be his last at Chang'an for a lifetime. 
The northwest was a perilous place. 
Enemies loomed outside, and no reinforcements came from within. Grain and pay ran out, and his troops were defeated in Ganzhou. Cut off from east and west, they were stranded in a distant land. 
In the second year of the Jianzhong era, the Tang court's imperial edict finally arrived: 
"The Four Garrisons of the Northern Protectorate, governing the fifty-seven Western Xia tribes and ten surname clans, have since the dynasty's founding served with dedication. After Guanlong fell, east and west severed, the loyal and righteous have defended with blood and tears, cautiously securing the borders, upholding rites and teachings, all achieved through the mutual efforts of marquises, earls, and garrison commanders governing together. The officers and soldiers may be promoted seven ranks." 
Seven ranks, can they replace grain and provisions? 
Seven ranks, can they replace troops and horses? 
Seven ranks… seven ranks… In Anxi, these seven ranks were nothing but a fleeting hope, gone before long. But having hope was better than having none. 
Decades in the northwest, tens of thousands of lives, countless tears and blood of soldiers and civilians. 
He could barely remember. Now with white hair, Guo Xin stood at the city gate, gazing at his dozens of gray-haired soldiers. 
Behind him were soaring flames and tens of thousands of enemy troops. 
Arrows rained down like a storm, but he felt no pain. Guo Xin only thought of one person. 
That old friend from years past, with whom he had severed ties, once asked him, "Do you regret this life?" 
At that time, Guo Xin had replied firmly, word by word: "I would die a hundred deaths and never regret it." 
But now, he regretted it deeply. He regretted failing here, failing these dozens of gray-haired soldiers behind him. 
He could no longer defend the Great Tang, the love of his life. 
"Great Tang… Chang'an…" 
No one knew these were his last words before dying in battle. 
Guo Xin, born in Chang'an, died in Kucha, held Anxi, never retreated.

zh: 宋人爱素食，他们认为荤食味虽美，却总给人富贵粗鄙之感，素食则清雅高洁。假煎肉就是素食中的名菜之一。《山家清供》记载了假煎肉的详细做法，即取瓠与麸薄批，各和以料，煎麸以油，煎瓠以脂，乃熬葱油，入酒共炒。不惟如肉，其味亦无辨者。
en: People in the Song Dynasty favored vegetarian cuisine, believing that while meat might be flavorful, it carried an air of vulgar luxury. Vegetarian dishes, by contrast, conveyed elegance and refinement. One such dish was Fried Mock Meat. As described in Offerings from the Mountain Home, this delicacy is prepared by thinly slicing bottle gourd and gluten, seasoning them separately. Fry seitan in oil and bottle gourd in animal fat, toss both into scallion oil (prepared separately), then stir-fry with rice wine. Though entirely plant-based, the texture and flavor are so convincing that it's nearly indistinguishable from real meat.

en:
Dear Wanderer:
Meow meow meow! Meow meow meow meow meow... meow! Meow meow, meow meow meow! Meow meow, meow meow meow!
Meow, meow meow meow meow. Meow, meow meow meow meow meow. Meow meow meow, meow meow, meow meow meow, meow meow, meow!
Meow meow meow meow, meow meow meow meow. Meow meow meow meow, meow meow meow meow. Meow meow meow meow, meow meow meow meow...
Meow meow meow meow meow meow, meow meow meow meow, meow meow meow meow meow meow!
Many thanks to you and the fine friends you introduced, Boss! I so wish to stay with everyone forever... alright, alright! You there, stop licking my fur! And you, stop nibbling on my tail!
Boss, this place truly is far too lively. A cat, it seems, still needs a bit of quiet solitude now and then. But worry not, boss! After all these days of them chattering around me, even if a cat wanders far and closes its eyes, it will still hear many a familiar meow and chirp, and never again feel at a loss for words!
The spring runs silent, tree shadows fall upon the water. The bright moon startles the magpies, the cool breeze sets the cicadas singing. At Midsummer, scenery is without end...
There will be many more roads to walk, but $T(5053) shall never forget the boss... $T(5053) and the boss are the very best!
-

事情的转机出现在安一飞取了秤要给猫猫们称体重。其他的猫们要么扭扭捏捏，要么窜上跳下，只有小度围着秤，用爪子敲来摸去，好似见了老朋友。
小度的爪子敲了下最小的秤砣，发出清脆的笃笃声。安一飞对着它叫小度，猫咪回它几声喵喵，算是金口松了。
有不喜欢经商的人，说不定有喜欢管度量的猫呢？
en:
Little Measure had no love for books. When An Yifei tried to name it after a book, the scent of ink and paper sent the cat leaping away. For a long time, it was a homeless, nameless wanderer. 
Everything changed when An Yifei brought out a scale to weigh the cats. While the others were shy or restless, Little Measure circled the scale confidently, pawing at it as if greeting an old friend. 
A sharp "tok-tok" rang out as its paw tapped the smallest weight. An called its name—"Little Measure"—and the cat responded with a series of soft meows, breaking its silence at last. 
Some shun the bustle of trade, but perhaps some cats find joy in keeping measure and balance.

en:
Doudou is the most diligent kitten in the palace. Every day, it grooms its fur until not a speck of dust remains.

The palace is huge, and picking a territory to call its own is no easy task. Doudou wandered round and round before settling on a spot. The people here are just as hardworking as it is, rushing about from dawn to night with hardly a moment's rest.

But the place is so big that there are always dirty corners. Right under Doudou's paws, for instance, buckets are piled up in the corner, and the stink makes it scrunch up its nose.

Ever since deciding to live here, Doudou has stood by the doorway every morning, scratching at the soil, determined to bury anything foul underground. Now and then, someone from the Wude guard unit passes by, sees it hard at work, and stops to help clean up.

After all, if you cannot keep one room in order, how can you keep the world in order?

zh:
【八佾第三】

孔子谓季氏：“八佾舞于庭，是可忍也，孰不可忍也？”
三家者以雍彻。子曰：“相维辟公，天子穆穆，奚取于三家之堂？”
子曰：“人而不仁，如礼何？人而不仁，如乐何？”
林放问礼之本。子曰：“大哉问！礼，与其奢也，宁俭；丧，与其易也，宁戚。”
子曰：“夷狄之有君，不如诸夏之亡也。”
季氏旅于泰山。子谓冉有曰：“汝不能救与？”对曰：“不能。子曰：“呜呼，曾谓泰山不如林放乎？”
子曰：“君子无所争，必也射乎！揖让而升，下而饮，其争也君子。”
子夏问曰：“巧笑倩兮，美目盻兮，素以为绚兮，何谓也？”子曰：“绘事后素。”曰：“礼后乎？”子曰：“起予者商也，始可与言诗已矣。”
子曰：“夏礼，吾能言之，杞不足征；殷礼，吾能言之，宋不足征也。文献不足故也，足则吾能征之矣。”
子曰：“禘自既灌而往者，吾不欲观之矣。”
或问禘之说，子曰：“不知也。知其说者之于天下也，其如示诸斯乎。指其掌。”
祭如在，祭神如神在。子曰：“吾不与祭，如不祭。”
王孙贾问曰：“与其媚于奥，宁媚于灶，何谓也？”子曰：“不然。获罪于天，无所祷也。”
子曰：“周监于二代，郁郁乎文哉！吾从周！”
子入太庙，每事问。或曰：“孰谓鄹人之子知礼乎？入太庙，每事问。”子闻之，曰：“是礼也。”
子曰：“射不主皮，为力不同科，古之道也。”
子贡欲去告朔之饩羊。子曰：“赐也，汝爱其羊，我爱其礼。”
子曰：“事君尽礼，人以为谄。”
定公问：“君使臣，臣事君，如之何？”孔子对曰：“君使臣以礼，臣事君以忠。”
子曰：“关雎，乐而不淫，哀而不伤。”
哀公问社于宰我，宰我对曰：“夏后氏以松，殷人以柏，周人以栗，曰使民战栗也。”子闻之，曰：“成事不说，遂事不谏，既往不咎。”
子曰：“管仲之器小哉！”或曰：“管仲俭乎？”曰：“管氏有三归，官事不摄，焉得俭乎？”曰：“然则管仲知礼乎？”曰：“邦君树塞门，管氏亦树塞门。邦君为两君之好，有反坫，管氏亦有反坫。管氏而知礼，孰不知礼？”
子语鲁太师乐，曰：“乐其可知已也：始作，翕如也。从之，纯如也，皎如也，绎如也，以成。”
仪封人请见，曰：“君子之至于斯者，吾未尝不得见也。从者见之，出曰：“二三子何患于丧乎？天下之无道久矣，天将以夫子为木铎。”
子谓韶：“尽美矣，又尽善也。”谓武：“尽美矣，未尽善也。”
子曰：“居上不宽，为礼不敬，临丧不哀，吾何以观之哉？”
en:
【Book 3, Chapter 1: The Eight Rows of Dancers】

Confucius said of the Ji family, "They have the audacity to perform the dance of the eight rows of dancers in their courtyard. If this can be tolerated, what cannot be tolerated?"
The three families of the Meng, Shu, and Ji used the Yong ode during the removal of the sacrificial vessels. The Master said, "Assisting were the princes; the Son of Heaven looked profound and grave. What application can this have in the hall of the three families?"
The Master said, "If a man is not benevolent, what has he to do with the rites? If a man is not benevolent, what has he to do with music?"
Lin Fang asked about the fundamental principles of the rites. The Master said, "A great question indeed! In rites, it is better to be frugal than extravagant. In mourning, it is better to be deeply sorrowful than meticulous in formalities."
The Master said, "The rude tribes of the east and north have their princes and are not like the states of our great land which are without them."
The head of the Ji family was going to sacrifice to the Tai mountain. The Master said to Ran You, "Can you not save him from this?" He answered, "I cannot." The Master said, "Alas! Will you say that the Tai mountain is not as discerning as Lin Fang?"
The Master said, "The superior man has no contentiousness. If it cannot be avoided, let it be in archery! Bowing and yielding to one another, they ascend the hall; descending, they drink. Even in their contention, they are still the superior man."
Zi Xia asked, saying, "What is the meaning of the passage—'The pretty dimples of her artful smile! The well-defined black and white of her eye! The plain ground for the colors?'" The Master said, "The business of laying on the colors follows the preparation of the plain ground." "Ceremonies then are a subsequent thing?" The Master said, "It is Shang who can bring out my meaning. Now I can begin to talk about the odes with him."
The Master said, "I could describe the ceremonies of the Xia dynasty, but Qi cannot sufficiently attest my words. I could describe the ceremonies of the Yin dynasty, but Song cannot sufficiently attest my words. This is because of the insufficiency of their records and wise men. If those were sufficient, I could adduce them in support of my words."
The Master said, "At the great sacrifice, after the pouring out of the libation, I have no wish to look on."
Some one asked the meaning of the great sacrifice. The Master said, "I do not know. He who knew its meaning would find it as easy to govern the kingdom as to look on this"—pointing to his palm.
He sacrificed to the dead, as if they were present. He sacrificed to the spirits, as if the spirits were present. The Master said, "If I am not present at the sacrifice, it is as if I did not sacrifice."
Wang-sun Jia asked, saying, "What is the meaning of the saying, 'It is better to pay court to the furnace than to the southwest corner?'" The Master said, "Not so. He who offends against Heaven has none to whom he can pray."
The Master said, "Zhou had the advantage of viewing the two past dynasties. How complete and elegant are its regulations! I follow Zhou."
The Master, when he entered the grand temple, asked about everything. Some one said, "Who will say that the son of the man of Zou knows the rules of propriety? He has entered the grand temple and asks about everything." The Master heard the remark, and said, "This is a rule of propriety."
The Master said, "In archery it is not going through the leather which is the principal thing; because people's strength is not equal. This was the old way."
Zi Gong wished to do away with the offering of a sheep connected with the inauguration of the first day of each month. The Master said, "Ci, you love the sheep; I love the ceremony."
The Master said, "The full observance of the rules of propriety in serving one's prince is accounted by people to be flattery."
The Duke Ding asked how a prince should employ his ministers, and how ministers should serve their prince. Confucius replied, "A prince should employ his ministers according to the rules of propriety; ministers should serve their prince with faithfulness."
The Master said, "The Guan Ju is expressive of enjoyment without being licentious, and of grief without being hurtfully excessive."
Duke Ai asked Zai Wo about the altars of the spirits of the land. Zai Wo replied, "The Xia sovereigns planted the pine tree about them; the men of the Yin planted the cypress; and the men of the Zhou planted the chestnut tree, meaning thereby to cause the people to be in awe." When the Master heard it, he said, "Things that are done, it is needless to speak about; things that have had their course, it is needless to remonstrate about; things that are past, it is needless to blame."
The Master said, "Small indeed was the capacity of Guan Zhong!" Some one said, "Was Guan Zhong parsimonious?" "Guan had the San Gui, and his officers performed no double duties; how can he be considered parsimonious?" "Then, did Guan Zhong know the rules of propriety?" The Master said, "The princes of states have a screen intercepting the view at their gates. Guan had likewise a screen at his gate. The princes of states, on any friendly meeting between two of them, had a stand on which to place their inverted cups. Guan had also such a stand. If Guan knew the rules of propriety, who does not know them?"
The Master instructing the grand music master of Lu said, "How to play music may be known. At the commencement of the piece, all the parts should sound together. As it proceeds, they should be in harmony while severally distinct and flowing without break, and thus on to the conclusion."
The border warden at Yi requested to be introduced to the Master, saying, "When men of superior virtue have come to this, I have never been denied the privilege of seeing them." The followers of the sage introduced him, and when he came out from the interview, he said, "My friends, why are you distressed by your master's loss of office? The kingdom has long been without the principles of truth and right; Heaven is going to use your master as a bell with its wooden tongue."
The Master said of the Shao that it was perfectly beautiful and also perfectly good. He said of the Wu that it was perfectly beautiful but not perfectly good.
The Master said, "High station filled without indulgent generosity; ceremonies performed without reverence; mourning conducted without sorrow—wherewith should I contemplate such ways?"

佛光顶上，阳光被佛光玉折为虹彩。一位禅师一半僧衣一半劲装，手持禅杖，静立如那诸佛造像中的一尊。 你听闻这位禅师早已易名北上，如今，却在此地意外相逢。禅师面具之下的脸波澜不惊，你只远远听得声如洪钟的询问：小施主，你是想见我的假相，法相，还是真相？……
⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛
禅师并未回答，而是低声颂了句佛号。霎时间，你仿佛看到他身后狂风呼啸，一尊巨大的佛像显露出来。“纵观三相，不如无相。”耳边传来禅师低沉而洪亮的声音。他背后的巨佛像双手合十，风沙隐去了他的身形。待风沙散去，佛光顶上唯有日光彻地，虹彩依然，仿佛禅师从未出现。你不禁怀疑，方才那无相无定之人是否真的折返清河？还是自己这一程入梦又醒，自己产生了幻觉？
en:
Atop Halo Peak, sunlight fractured through the Buddha's Light Jade into drifting rainbow hues. There stood a Chan master, clad half in monk's robes and half in martial garb, Khakkhara staff in hand, as motionless as one of the myriad Buddha statues.
You had heard this master had long since changed his name and journeyed north, yet here, of all places, you unexpectedly crossed paths. His face beneath the mask was entirely unreadable; from afar, you only heard his voice, resonant as a temple bell, asking, "Young patron, do you wish to see my false form, my Dharma form, or my true form?"...

The master gave no answer, but murmured the Buddha's name under his breath. In that instant, howling winds seemed to surge behind him, and the silhouette of a colossal Buddha manifested. "To behold the three forms is not as profound as the formless," the master's low, sonorous voice echoed right beside your ear. Behind him, the great Buddha pressed its palms together, and wind and sand swallowed his form whole. When the wind and sand settled, only sunlight bathed Halo Peak. The rainbows remained unchanged, as if the Chan master had never been there at all. You could not help but wonder whether that formless, unbound man had truly returned to Qinghe. Or perhaps this whole journey had been no more than a dream, leaving you with nothing but a hallucination?

The Art of #ffc89cCloud Hand Fishing#E relies not on rod nor net, but solely on the flow of Qi.

Swimming within this flow, the fish finds unbidden joy and forgets to flee, coming forth of its own accord. The emerald-scaled fish breaks the surface, its glistening scales shining in unison with the rosy dawn glow. Thus it is said: This is no act of fishing. The fish, drawn to the Dao, comes willingly of its own.


Participate in #ffc89cCloud Hand Fishing#E, use different Tai Chi skills to catch Painted Boat exclusive fish, and enjoy an explosive fishing experience! Earn rich rewards based on your score tiers! There is also a Cloud Hand Fishing Leaderboard, so come and strive to be the master fisher!

zh:
她曾经短暂地拥有过奶娘。厚实的皮毛、松软的尾巴，将小小的她包裹得结实。圆月之下，沙漠中凛冽的风刀亦近不了她半分。
沙丘上聚集了许多和奶娘长得一样的生物。它们伸长脖子，此起彼伏地嚎叫着，宣告着此处是它们的领土。
她用稚嫩的嗓音，拼尽全力地应和着，发出了一声响亮的啼哭。

后来她被贺又渠带回了马头村。
她第一次知道，人需要穿皮毛，吃热食；除了活下去，还有其他需要做的事。
贺津看着马头村的人，在井下进进出出，穷尽一生寻求一张图纸上标记的水源。
贺又渠教她像人一样生活，教她人与人之间的约定、人心中的坚持。
她学着做一个人。

可是，风沙的胃口向来大。
沙暴袭来，井下塌方，所有人哭成一团。
她被村人抱在怀中仓皇逃命。沙石重重砸下，隔绝了贺又渠的身影。

她游荡在玉门关时，见过沙子吞噬许多东西。大的小的，死的活的。约定、坚持、人与人……终究还是敌不过风沙。
果然，还是活下去最重要吧？
en:
She once briefly had a wet nurse. Thick fur, a soft tail, wrapped her small body securely. Under the full moon, even the desert's sharp wind-blades could not come near her. 
On the dunes gathered many creatures that looked like her wet nurse. They stretched their necks, howling one after another, proclaiming this place as their territory. 
With a tender voice, straining with all her might, she joined in, letting out a loud wail. 

Later, she was taken back to Horsehelm Village by He Youqu. 
For the first time, she learned that humans need to wear furs, eat warm food; that besides surviving, there are other things one must do. 
He Jin watched the people of Horsehelm Village go in and out of wells, spending their entire lives seeking the water source marked on a single map. 
He Youqu taught her to live like a human, taught her the promises between people, the convictions in people's hearts. 
She learned to be a person. 

But the wind and sand have always had a great appetite. 
A sandstorm struck, the well collapsed, and everyone wept together. 
She was held in a villager's arms as they fled in panic. Sand and stone crashed down heavily, cutting off He Youqu's figure. 

When she wandered by Jade Gate Pass, she had seen sand devour many things. Big and small, dead and alive. Promises, convictions, person to person... in the end, they still could not withstand the wind and sand. 
Surely, survival is the most important thing?

钱塘门外约百步，西子湖畔玉壶园。
昔为钱氏别业，园中有轩名玉壶，畜养珍禽异兽，以供游赏。每值春秋佳日，文人雅集，挥毫题壁，吟咏于亭。身在园中，近揽四时花卉、翠竹摇风；远眺山明水秀、落日渔歌。今则游者往来，携琴载酒，或品茗柳下，或临流照影，抚琴而忘归。湖畔苔痕仍带墨香，庭中奇珍异兽，啼鸣如故。昔年朱衣游赏地，今为青衿雅集所。
en:
Some hundred paces beyond Qiantang Gate, by the shore of West Lake, lies Jadeheart Garden.
Once the private estate of the Qian family, the garden had a pavilion named Jadeheart, where rare birds and strange beasts were kept for visitors to admire. On fine days in spring and autumn, scholars gathered to write poetry on the walls and trade verses in the pavilions. In the garden, one can see flowers of every season and emerald bamboo swaying in the breeze; and in the distance, bright hills and clear waters, and fishermen singing in the sunset. Today, travelers still come with zithers and wine, drinking tea under the willows or watching their reflections in the stream, having such a good time that they forget to leave. The moss by the lake still carries the scent of ink, and the rare creatures in the courtyard cry as they once did. A place once reserved for nobles is now a haven for scholars.

zh:
张泉从来苏蒙学习字回来后，抓着笔，把今天新学的字写给刘娴看。
刘娴不识字，张泉从有点高的椅子上跳下来，丢了笔，抓着她的手，在她手心再写一遍：“娘，先生说这是家字。”
刘娴笑着摸了摸发痒的掌心，这字笔画多，痒也要痒上许久。
张泉跟着她说今日蒙学里的事：“娘，先生还让我们回来想，回来问，家是啥地方，家不就是爹在和娘在的地方嘛，是不是？”
可爹在娘在的时候，刘娴没有家。

这辈子她只有一个家，她的家从十九岁的时候开始，从缩在张家食肆门口的那个雨夜开始。
家是啥样？她都是从张安康身上学到的，张安康又是从他娘身上学到的。
于是刘娴学到：“家是会等人吃饭的地方。”“晚回家的人桌上一定还热着饭菜。”
一条，又一条。
之后她还会学很多很多条。
泉儿出生后，再多学上一条。
“家是有张安康和泉儿的地方，家是要让咱们泉儿过得好的地方。”

他是这样教她的。
他明明是这样教她的，可是怎么不算数了呢，多年后，刘娴看着失火的店铺，闹事的混混，捡起砖，捡起瓦，捡起滚落的食材。
算数的，只是他有两个家，前头一个家，他和他娘的家，后头一个家，他和她的家。
而她只有一个家。

刘娴也知道自己是拦不住他的。
在很久很久之前，她就知道，比起手上有两个馒头的人，手上只有一个馒头的人，是得要低头的，她只是为了这个低头吗？
她的眼睛盯着菜谱上糊了的一小块，那是张安康母亲带回来的菜谱。

张安康看着菜谱做菜的地方，那个江湖上的外来人，看着那个才字的线索。

刘娴的手指怔怔地碰了碰那一小块糊了的地方，那是一位母亲死前的眼泪。
那是一滴来自过去的眼泪。
en:
Zhang Quan returned from Hopewell Academy's literacy class, clutching a brush, eager to show Liu Xian the new character he'd learned that day. 
Liu Xian couldn't read. Zhang Quan jumped down from his slightly-too-high stool, tossed the brush aside, grabbed her hand, and traced the character onto her palm: "Mother, Master said this is the character for 'home'." 
Liu Xian smiled, rubbing her tingling palm. The character had many strokes, so the tingling lingered.
Zhang Quan chattered about his day at school: "Mother, Master told us to think about what 'home' means. Isn't home just where Father and Mother are?" 
But when both parents had been present, Liu Xian had no home.

Her only home in this life began at nineteen, on that rainy night when she huddled at the entrance of Zhang's Eatery. What was a home like? She learned from Zhang Ankang, who had learned from his own mother. 
So Liu Xian learned: "Home is where someone waits to eat with you." "The food on the table stays warm for those who return late." 
One lesson after another.
Then she would learn many, many more. 
After Liquan was born, she added one more.
"Home is where Zhang Ankang and Liquan are. Home is where our Quan can thrive." 

That was what he taught her. 
Yet why did those lessons stop applying years later, as Liu Xian stared at their burning shop, at the rioters, picking up bricks, shattered tiles, scattered ingredients? 
They still applied, only he had two homes. The first one is his home with his mother. The second is his home with her.
She only ever had one.

Liu Xian knew she couldn't stop him.
She'd known long ago that those with one steamed bun must bow to those with two. Was that the only reason she yielded?
Her gaze fixed on a smudged corner of the recipe book, the one Zhang Ankang's mother had left behind.

Zhang Ankang had once cooked from that book. Now, an outsider in the jianghu studied it for clues about the "Cai" character. 

Liu Xian's fingers absently brushed the stain, a mother's final tear. 
A drop of grief from the past.

Foreman Shi was up late checking inventory last night, so I should make him a rainbow lantern. That way he'll feel a bit more lively when he's counting stock after dark, and when he has a moment to spare, he can even loosen up with a few steps in its colorful glow.

The old foreman has been ordering everyone around nonstop lately, and everyone's ears are paying the price. I should make him a sound-recording box. Then he can talk all he likes, and no one else will have to hear a word of it.

Zi Yuan is always saying she wants to see the world beyond the mountain, so the little bird carrier still needs a few more adjustments... There's no way it can fly across Gasping Cliff, but maybe it could whip up a whirlwind and blow her over instead. I just hope she doesn't grow too tall before then.

Cai Yin loves her drink, but she's always worried a cup too many will muddle her sums. I'll build a "Slumber-Buster Mechanism": whenever her head goes fuzzy, it'll dump a jug of "Sweet Slumber" right over her. That way she can drink and keep the books at once. I'll just have to swap her ledgers for waterproof ones.

...

So much to do. Mirkvale really can't manage without me!
Kang Tao

zh:
昔年命途多舛，郁不得志。不得已避入山间，苦乏庸烦，或与汝闲涂数笔，聊为驱闷尔。
今世事陡转，机缘已至，出山入世，青云在望。天意怜我，与我金桃，风云助我，全我夙愿！此去中原，宗师论剑、华堂共酒，鲜衣怒马，畅快平生，方不负我卅年蹉跎、一身胆略矣！
夫人之相知，贵合其天性。 明珠美玉、凤凰良木，此谓相配也。尔描花绘鸟，市井之人。吾幼学逐鹿之术，少入将相庙堂。或有低徊，不过一时之遇，岂可久与杂匠嬉戏哉？
此番相别，非吾寡义。鸿鹄冲天，无暇回望梁下燕。蛟龙入海，腾波何顾池中鱼。旧日戏言，尽付逝水。汝自守陋室，吾自逐青云。言尽于此，不复再白。
——方白
en:
Hardship and stifled ambition forced me to retreat to the mountains and a life of dull frustration. In those times, a few idle strokes of the brush with you served as a modest diversion from my gloom. 
Now, opportunity has arrived, with success within reach. The Golden Peach comes to fulfill my deepest wish. On this journey to the Central Plains, I shall cross swords with masters, share wine in splendid halls, and ride in glory, my heart at last at ease. 
True kinship between souls is rooted in a harmony of nature. I have since childhood pursued the art of statecraft. Whatever setbacks I may have faced were but fleeting; how could I linger forever among humble artisans? 
This parting, then, is no failure of loyalty on my part. A dragon plunging into the sea spares no glance for the fish in the pond. The idle words of old dissolve into flowing waters. I have said all there is to say, and will not speak again. 
Fang Bai

遇见敌手，只需三招，即可战胜！首先，请对方先手，当对方落子时即刻摄星拿月偷之！可怜的对手以为自己抢占先机，谁承想呢反而是我多了一枚棋子。其次，世人掌握太极之术者众多，可将乾坤挪移搬上棋盘的只有我！趁对手不备，将其棋盘上所有棋子变成我的，快哉！最后，若遇实在无法战胜之人，只需在棋盘上轻轻拍上一掌，并大喊一声“我不玩了”即可破局。
en:
They say defeat comes from being one move short. That missing move is none other than this very move of mine!
The older I grow, the less I can rely on my memory. So I have gathered the secret arts of a lifetime's study of Go into a single volume. It is my precious treasure, and must never fall into another's hands.
When faced with a worthy opponent, three moves are all it takes to win. First, let the other player take the opening move. The moment the opponent places a stone, use Celestial Seize to steal it away! The poor fool thinks he has claimed the advantage, never imagining that I am the one who ends up with an extra stone. Second, many in this world may know the art of Tai Chi, but I alone can bring Qiankun Shift onto the Go board! Catch your opponent off guard and turn all the stones on the board into your own. What joy! Last, if you should meet someone you truly cannot defeat, simply give the board a light slap and shout, "I play no further!" That alone is enough to break the deadlock.

家里的生意越来越好，可叛逆的少年厌倦了这样的日子。而且，王团花这个名字真是太难听了，他最讨厌别人“王团花”“王团花”的叫，他要去一个没人知道他名字的地方。于是，他逃家了。

很快，这位性喜天然的少年就在山里迷了路，闯入了一个老和尚的隐居之所。王团花发现，这老和尚看着不起眼，实则深藏不露，书画更是一绝，便缠着他教自己。后来，每隔一段时间，王团花就想法子逃家来找老和尚。他的确是有天分的，三五年间，便将老和尚的本领学去了七七八八，竟然连如何隐匿气息都学会了。渐渐地，王团花擅书擅画的名号在蜀中传扬开来。
en:
In Chengdu Prefecture of the Shu Kingdom, there lived a renowned brocade family headed by Lord Wang. Fond of circular patterns, he named his son Wang Tuanhua. As a teenager, Wang Tuanhua revealed a unique talent: no matter how damaged the fabric, he could always find a way to restore it using unconventional methods.

Business thrived, but the rebellious youth grew restless. Worse, he loathed his name, "Wang Tuanhua, Wang Tuanhua", a constant mockery in his ears. He longed to vanish where no one knew him. So he fled. 

His nature-driven wanderings soon led him astray in the mountains, stumbling upon a hermitage where an unassuming old monk lived. Wang Tuanhua discovered the monk was a master of calligraphy and painting, and pestered him for lessons. Thereafter, he escaped home periodically to study. Gifted and driven, within three to five years, he mastered seven or eight out of ten of the monk's skills, even learning to mask his presence. Gradually, his fame as a prodigy in art spread throughout Shu.

zh:
萧誉默默地清扫着柴房前的落叶，几位弟子聚在不远处，毫不避讳地对着他指指点点。
“这就是那个自称狂刀门第一人的萧誉？怎么跑来住柴房了？”
“你不知道？此人不知练了什么邪功，走岔了真气，如今已是个废人！”
“我就说，一个无父无母的野种，进了我狂刀门才修习多久就那样厉害，原来是走了邪路了！我呸！丢我狂刀门的脸。”
萧誉冷冷望向那几位弟子，昔日打遍门中上下的威势仍在，吓得那几名宵小立时闭嘴。他正欲低头继续手中活计，又一不速之客声音响起：
“哼，断牙恶犬，还在此处虚张声势，欺凌同门？”
却道来者是谁？正是狂刀门大师兄宋白书。几名宵小见大师兄到此，赶忙上前，极尽谄媚之辞。萧誉不为所动，仍只清扫落叶。
宋白书冷哼一声：“见大师兄至，还不行礼？”
萧誉冷漠对答：“你我皆为门中弟子，并无上下之别。况且我已被门中除名，为何要向你行礼？”
说时迟那时快，宋白书如一道疾电，掠过身边几人，一掌攥住萧誉的脸，顺势将其首重重按在地上。萧誉此时已无还手之力，被掼摔在地，顿时七窍出血，好不渗人。
“你也配和我说道理？废人？”
宋白书收回手，嫌弃地用白手帕擦了擦，而后用脚顺势踩住萧誉的头，如同他真的只是路边一条野犬。
萧誉本就重伤在身，此时气息更加微弱，嘴巴一开一合，似有话要说。宋白书饶有兴致，俯身将耳凑近。却见萧誉只狠狠将一口血水啐了宋白书一个满面，而后张狂大笑。
宋白书大怒，正要干脆了断了萧誉性命，一道倩影赶忙冲进院落，将萧誉护在身后。来人正是掌门之女王熏儿，方才去为萧誉买药出门，一时不在，竟令萧誉险遭毒手。
“小师妹，此人悖逆之徒，何必护着他！”
王熏儿扶起萧誉，明眸含怒：“我与萧誉有婚约在身，大师兄却这样伤他。若再不离开此地，休怪熏儿手下无情！”
宋白书脸色难看：“掌门已取消那婚约，你何必还待在这废人身边？我这就去求掌门，将你许配于我！”
宋白书还要再言，却见王熏儿已将手伸向腰间长剑，一股凝然杀意已锁定在他身上。他只得服软，假意要走，却忽然出手，就要将王熏儿击晕。好在萧誉功力已无，眼力却在，及时出声提醒，王熏儿才堪堪避过。
宋白书也不再隐藏：“熏儿，此逆徒擅改狂刀之法，还将其外传！杀他乃掌门之令，你何必执迷？”
萧誉眉头皱起，他何时做过这样的事？王熏儿却不管那许多，抓起萧誉之手，便直往后山而逃。狂刀门中也不再掩藏杀萧誉之意，追兵一时蜂拥。王熏儿独木难支，且战且退，及至后山崖边。
追兵皆不愿伤了掌门之女，都有留手，但刀剑无眼，王熏儿身上还是多出了几处剑伤。萧誉身上之伤，更不知几何。狂风烈烈，萧誉染血衣袍随风鼓动，猎猎作响。他望着王熏儿，难掩自责心痛之意。
“且送至此处吧。”
还不待王熏儿反应，萧誉已一跃而下。临死之前，他想明白了一切。原来他经脉尽断亦是掌门之意，他以诚相待，向掌门指出了狂刀门刀法中的欠缺之处，竟反招来杀身之祸。
狂刀门配不上他萧誉，若有来生，必让那故步自封的掌门，见识何为真正的武技！
————————欲知后事如何，且听下回分解——————————
en:
Xiao Yu was silently sweeping the leaves outside the wooden shack, while nearby, a few disciples huddled, pointing and snickering without the slightest pretense of privacy.
"So this is the 'top blade' of our sect? Look at him now, reduced to a woodshed servant."
"Haven't you heard? He dabbled in some dark arts and backfired his Qi. Now? He's nothing but a spent husk!"
"I knew it. A low-born stray like him reaching those heights? Must be some crooked trickery. Bah! A total disgrace to the Fierce Blade name."
Xiao Yu shot them a cold glance, and even now, the weight of his former name was enough to shut them up. Just as he bent down to keep sweeping, a voice cut in from behind.
"Hmph. A toothless cur, still barking to scare the juniors?"
It was Song Baishu, the senior disciple. The spineless lot rushed to Song's side, showering him with sycophantic praise. Xiao Yu ignored them all and kept sweeping.
Song Baishu sneered. "Your Senior Brother is here. Where is your salute?"
Xiao Yu replied flatly, without even looking up. "We are both disciples, and I've been struck from the scrolls. Why should I bow to you?"
In the blink of an eye, Song Baishu blurred forward like a bolt of lightning. He clamped a hand over Xiao's face and slammed his head into the dirt. Xiao Yu, already too weak to fight back, hit the dirt hard. Blood seeped from every orifice. A brutal sight.
"You think you're in any position to lecture me? You pathetic cripple!"
Song pulled back, wiping his fingers with a white handkerchief in feigned disgust. Then he ground his boot into Xiao's head as if he were nothing but a stray dog.
Xiao was barely holding on. His breath grew even shallower. His lips quivered as if struggling to force out a final word. Curious, Song leaned in closer. Bad move. Xiao spat a mouthful of blood right in his face, followed by a roar of defiant laughter.
Song lost it. He was about to end Xiao right then and there when a girl rushed into the courtyard and threw herself in front of him. It was Wang Xun'er, the Sect Master's daughter. She'd just gotten medicine for Xiao.
"Junior Sister, the man is a renegade. Why shield him?"
Wang helped Xiao to his feet, fury burning in her eyes. "Xiao Yu and I are betrothed. And this is how you treat my fiancé, Senior Brother? Leave now, or do not blame me if my blade shows no mercy!"
Song's face darkened. "The Master has annulled that marriage pact! Why cling to this shell of a man? I shall petition Master to grant your hand to me instead!"
He was about to keep pushing when he noticed Wang's hand moving toward the sword at her waist, and the killing intent suddenly locked onto him. Forced to yield, he feigned retreat, only to whirl around with a sudden strike, aiming to knock Xun'er senseless. Though his powers are gone, Xiao Yu's eyes remain keen. He shouted a warning just in time, and Wang barely managed to dodge.
Song stopped holding back. "Xun'er, enough! This traitor corrupted our sacred styles and leaked them to outsiders. His execution is Master's direct command!"
Xiao furrowed his brow. When had he ever committed such a crime? But Wang didn't care. She grabbed his hand and bolted toward the back mountain. The Sect's intent was now bared for all to see. A tide of pursuers swarmed the mountain paths. Outnumbered and overwhelmed, Xun'er fought a desperate retreat toward the edge of a cliff.
The pursuers didn't want to risk hurting the Sect Master's daughter, so they held back, but blades had no eyes. Xun'er was soon trailing blood from several shallow gashes. A fierce wind whipped around them, Xiao's blood-soaked robes snapping in the gusts. He looked at Wang, guilt and anguish written all over his face.
"This is far enough."
Before she could utter a word, Xiao flung himself into the abyss. In that final moment, everything clicked into place. His shattered meridians were no accident; it was the Master's design. His honesty in pointing out the flaws of their style had been his own death warrant.
The Fierce Blade Sect was never worthy of him. If fate granted him another life, he would show that stagnant old Master the meaning of true mastery!
To find out what happens next, stay tuned for the next episode.

今岁粮饷，我托王大哥一起带回去。家中一切辛苦爹和月娘帮忙看顾，等开春战事少了，我定能回家看看！

李景行 字

en:
Father,

It has been two years since I marched north with the army. All is well with me. I only do not know whether your health is sound, and whether Yueniang and Xia'er are both well.

Last year I came under General Zhao Dejun's command. Thanks to the few characters I learned from you in childhood, and with the help of the brothers in the ranks, I was promoted to the post of unit leader. But Father, do not worry. The men under General Zhao are all seasoned soldiers. I have heard there is even a troop of foreign cavalry, all Khitan riders on silver saddles, fighting for the Han. Most days it is not my turn to go into battle. Whenever I have the chance, I learn a little more riding and archery from them. I will take good care of myself.

I have asked Brother Wang to bring home this year's pay and grain stipend for me. I must trouble you and Yueniang to look after things at home for a little while longer. Once spring comes and the fighting eases, I shall surely be able to come home and see you.

Li Jingxing

世间哪有这般人？樊楼交不出人，他就自己四处找。醉花阴们也不阻拦，不外是笑着问一句：公子，还在寻觅知音呀？

en:
Master Zhong is a regular at Revelry Hall and a favored guest there. Lately, however, he has taken to muttering to himself, endlessly carrying on about #Ya mysterious dancer#E, insisting it's the soulmate who has captured his heart at first sight, demanding that Revelry Hall produce that person at once.
As if anyone like that could be conjured up. Since the Revelry Hall could offer no such person, he set out to search for them himself. The maidens of Velvet Shade did nothing to stop him; they only smiled and teased, "Still hunting for your soulmate, Master Zhong?"
With his heart in his throat and a stubborn breath caught in his chest, Master Zhong swore he would find this person no matter what. He dashed up and down the tower more than a dozen times before at last finding the little room where he had caught that dazzling glimpse. The door, it turned out, had been hidden behind a folding screen all along. No wonder he had searched in vain!
Overjoyed, he bypassed the screen and hurried inside, only to find the room empty.
Why was there only a chessboard left behind? The pieces had been put away; there was no telling if a player had yet to arrive, or if a game had just ended and they had already departed.
