en: On the night of the Lantern Festival, the city stacks countless lanterns layer upon layer, raising a towering, luminous peak known as the "Mountain of the Turtle." The displays feature an endless, dizzying array of shapes and styles, from frameless silk globes to glowing riverboats, each a marvel of craftsmanship vying for the eye. Yet, the true masterpieces are the fish lanterns. Crafted with startling realism, they are suspended high above the bustling avenues. As twilight falls and the first wicks are kindled, the streets awaken with joyous clamor. Above, the scattered lanterns hang low across the dark like a river of stars. Caught in the night breeze, the fish lanterns sway and ripple, appearing to swim through the Milky Way itself, chasing the light and snapping at glowing pearls. To stand beneath them is to wander deep into the Dragon King's crystal palace beneath the sea.

Xiang loves Grit Cakes. Even dogs turn their noses up at them, but that camel eats them with gusto.
It's a pity. I won't be going back.
Kind stranger, I stashed away a bunch of Grit Cakes. Afraid I won't get the chance to give them to him.

zh:
本人胡树叶，年廿七未婚，心悦同村小雁。本人殚精竭智，得悦女五法，录之如下：

其一，好男儿肩头能跑马，故每日扛石锁练"担山式"。肩宽二尺五，方为大丈夫！

其二，本人欲自明日起，晨起空腹将胡饼吊于眉前一尺，吸气收腹后徐徐啃食，此法虽类驴驹嗅草，然苦练三月，必得腹肌八块！

其三，腿长秘诀在胫不在股！本人特制"昆仑奴增高履"，鞋底填三层硝制牛筋。袍子下摆裁宽三寸，必无人能察。

其四，腱肉在精不在多，七分劲三分仙，此谓男儿骨，女儿劫。我这般筋肉流畅的英伟男子，莫及那粗豪野汉，如何与我比肩？

其五，制香方：蜀椒三颗、番荷五叶、鲜胡桃青皮，渍酒三宿。沐浴后焚此香，可祛汗臭。香风袭人，何愁小雁不中意于我？

无心点火处，芳心自然燃。

莫及莽夫，只知苦练腱子肉，怎知男子须修风仪？小雁芳心，必属胡某！
en:
I'm Hu Shuye, madly in love with Xiaoyan from my village. After much effort, I've mastered five secrets to win her heart:

First, a real man carries strength on his shoulders. Only with shoulders over two and a half feet wide can a man truly stand proud.

Second, starting tomorrow, I'll hang a flatbread a foot in front of my face each morning on an empty stomach, tighten my core, and slowly nibble it down. Three months in, I'll have washboard abs.

Third, long legs come from strong shins, not thighs. I made special shoes with triple-layered ox tendon soles. I also widened my robe hems by a few inches.

Fourth, it's quality over bulk: strength is 70% power, 30% grace. That's what makes a man truly impressive.

Fifth, my secret incense, which is Sichuan pepper, wild ginger leaves, and fresh walnut peels soaked in wine, banishes sweat odor and leaves an intoxicating fragrance when burned after a bath. How could Xiaoyan possibly resist?

zh:
多年后，洪水再次夺走了土地的生机。浊水蔓延又褪去，烈日把淤泥晒得干硬。饥饿和死亡再次攫取了“人”的尊严。
阿娘却破天荒地蒸了两个白面馍馍，塞进了千里烛的手中。不管阿弟如何哭闹，阿娘和阿爷都只把馍馍给她吃。
那是千里烛吃过最好吃的东西。她舍不得吃，把其中一个塞到了怀里。同时，她的头上被戴了草环。
“以后，你自己学着乖点吧。”“疼了也别喊，听话。”
怀里的馍馍还没有凉透，千里烛就被人牵走了。她看到，爷娘牵了另外的一个女孩回家。她以为爷娘认错了自己，拼命哭喊挣扎。可爷娘再也没回头看她一眼。
直到很多年后，她才明白，自己的不幸里又藏了多少幸运。
卖儿鬻女，易子而食。饥饿与死亡，模糊了人和牲畜的边界。
买下她的老翁把宰猪刀磨了又磨，终是叹了口气。他丢下刀，拿起了破碗与竹杖，拉着她向西去。
老翁带着千里烛涉过溪河。千里烛害怕地不敢下脚。老翁板着脸，凶狠地催促她一步一步走。
冰凉浑浊的水再次漫过她的脚背，小腿，腰间，胸口……千里烛害怕了，努力控制着摇晃的孱弱躯体。可她伸手一抓却发现，老翁的手一直默默护在身后。
en:
Years later, floods once again stole the land's vitality. Murky waters spread and receded; the scorching sun baked the mud into hardness. Hunger and death once more stripped people of their dignity. 
Yet, for the first time ever, Mother steamed two white-flour buns and pressed them into Celestial Candle's hands. No matter how her little brother cried and fussed, Mother and Father only gave the buns to her. 
They were the most delicious things Celestial Candle had ever eaten. She couldn't bear to eat them both and tucked one into her clothes. At the same time, a wreath of grass was placed on her head. 
"From now on, learn to behave on your own." "If it hurts, don't cry out. Be obedient." 
Before the bun hidden in her clothes had even cooled, Celestial Candle was led away. She watched as her parents took another girl home. Thinking they had mistaken her for someone else, she cried and struggled desperately. But her parents never looked back. 
It was only many years later that she understood just how much luck was hidden within her misfortune. 
Selling children, trading sons to eat—hunger and death blurred the line between human and beast. 
The old man who bought her sharpened his butcher's knife again and again, then finally sighed. He dropped the knife, picked up a broken bowl and a bamboo staff, and led her west. 
The old man led Celestial Candle across the creek. She was too afraid to take a step. With a stern face, he harshly urged her forward, one careful move at a time. 
Once again, the icy, murky water rose over her feet, then her calves, her waist, her chest... Terrified, she struggled to steady her trembling, fragile body. But as she reached out, her hand found the old man's—quietly hovering just behind her, guarding her all along.

It is to cultivate with them, and one day, we will ascend to the immortal realm together." As the Daoist grew old and was nearing the end of his life, he suddenly had a dream. In the dream, the mountain spirit transformed into a form and scolded him for being unfair, only being kind to the fish and leaving him behind. The mountain spirit promised to take him to the immortal realm. Upon waking, the Daoist went into the mountains and gathered all the spirits he had seen in his dream. zh:
河水浑浊，裹着断枝和死畜的尸体。千年渡的人都挤在高坡上，望着洪水淹没低处的房屋。
杨义深心里害怕极了，估摸着这一次是凶多吉少，恨自己来错了地方。
直到洪水褪去半日后，他才敢颤颤巍巍下到地面。
他看见那些被冲来的鱼在浅洼里扑腾，鳃一张一合，拼命喘着气。
多像啊，这鱼和自己多像啊。
就算每一口呼吸都带着死亡的腥气，却还是挣扎着活下去。
杨义深惊觉，这必是神女给他的启示。
发水了，长腿的牲畜跑不掉，人跑不掉，唯有鱼能活。
鱼之所以不死，全是神女的恩惠。
人们若是吃了鱼，一定也能沾点神女的福气，在水里活下来！
杨义深把心一横，从那天起，他在这支起了神女赏还给他的小鱼摊。
这样似乎就可以说服自己，当初他权衡片刻便任由不慎跌倒的小女儿落在洪水里……只是为了今时今日，自己还能匀旁人一尾鱼、让更多人活下去。
en:
The river ran the color of mud, choked with snapped branches and bloated carcasses. The residents of Millennium Crossing crowded the higher grounds, watching as the flood swallowed the houses below, one roof at a time.
Fear gnawed straight through Yang Yishen. He was afraid that things would end very badly for him this time, and cursed himself for ever coming here.
Only when the waters had receded for half a day did he dare climb back down, legs shaking.
That was when he saw them... the fish. They were hurled inland by the flood and thrashed in shallow hollows. Their gills flared and collapsed as they struggled desperately to breathe.
They looked just like him. Exactly like him.
Every breath tasted of rot and death, yet they still struggle to survive.
The thought struck him with terrifying clarity: this was the Goddess's message!
When the flood came, even long-legged beasts couldn't flee, and neither could people. Only fish endured.
It could only be by the grace of the Goddess.
If people ate fish, surely some fragment of that blessing would cling to them as well and allow them to survive in the water!
Yang Yishen steeled himself. From that day on, he set up a small fish stall once more. This one, he told himself, is a gift returned by the Goddess.
Believing this made it easier. Easier to tell himself that when his little daughter slipped and fell, when he hesitated for just a heartbeat and let the flood take her... It wasn't abandonment. It was so that today, he could hand fish to someone else, and keep more people alive.

她的相公是个粗人，却格外珍惜她。她说话轻声细语的，稍微开些玩笑，便会红了脸。她心细得很，他有个什么不舒服，都逃不过她的眼睛，热了有凉水，冷了有棉衣，他是普通人，却被她照顾得像是个了不得的人。
他不会说话，只想给她最好的生活，他不想她一到冬天就满手的冻疮，他想赚大钱，让她也做一做有钱人家的奶奶。

听了人家说唐钱要涨，他就弄了不少唐钱，可是钱到手还没焐热，便跌得让人害怕。
跌成这样，或许不会跌了，人家说，这时候就该咬咬牙，再兑些才是。
于是他真的咬咬牙，又兑了一些，可是那唐钱不仅没有涨，反而跌得更厉害了。
他不敢说，骗她家里啥也正常，勒紧了裤腰带，还是给她好的穿的用的，可身子却渐渐怄出了暗疾。
唐钱收缴令绷断了他的最后一根弦。
没有钱了，一分都没了，周氏却查出了有孕，那是他们的孩子，他只得找进了灰坑……听闻人市，能卖米肉。

他最终没能见到他们的孩子，孩子长大后，会更像自己，还是娘子呢？希望会更像她吧……她生得那样好看。
他也没听见她的哭声，没能听见她在他的坟前发誓，要不惜一切代价，让他们的孩子长大。
如果他能听见就好了，他多想擦干她的泪水，让她别那样勉强。
en:
"Little white chicken, scratching the ground. Our family's married a flower-faced aunt! Quick of tongue, deft of hand, two big scissors clacking grand. Left cuts peonies fair, right trims sacred herbs rare. Upon the herbs, two geese take flight, flapping wings across the Yellow River bright..."
Firecrackers popped as children clapped and sang, while Lady Zhou, veiled in red, married the sweetheart she'd loved since childhood. 

She dreamed of a plump baby boy, to raise him well, to watch him one day join the singing children at another's wedding.
Her husband was a rough man, but tender with her. She spoke softly, blushing at the mildest jest, and noticed every flicker of his discomfort. When he was hot, she fetched cold water. When he was cold, she sewed warm clothes. He was ordinary, but she made him feel like a king.
He lacked eloquence but vowed to give her the best life. He hated seeing her hands frostbitten in winter and dreamed of striking it rich, letting her live like a noble lady. 

When rumors spread that Tang Coins would rise in value, he invested heavily, only to watch their worth plummet.
"They can't fall further," people said. "Now's the time to grit your teeth and buy more." 
So he gritted his teeth and exchanged more money for Tang Coins, but instead of rising, their value plummeted even further.
He lied to her about their finances, tightening their belts while still spoiling her, but the stress festered into a silent illness.
The Tang Coin Confiscation policy snapped his last thread of hope. Ruined and penniless, with Lady Zhou newly pregnant, he went to the Ash Pit... where the Human Market traded in rice-meat.

He never saw their child. Would the baby look more like him or his wife? He hoped for her beauty. 
He never heard her sobs, never heard her vow over his grave to raise their child at any cost.
If only he could have wiped her tears and told her not to suffer alone.

Granny Turtle checked her Treasure Basin once again. Lately, a lot more coins have appeared inside it.
She asked around, and people told her they were Song Coins.
Oh... then these are good coins. With Song Coins, she could buy Yingying a new pair of shoes. The girl ran and skipped everywhere, and her shoes were all worn through... She could save a little for the eldest, too. No, no, the eldest hadn't come home yet, but the youngest had.
The youngest was a good child, always coming and going in a whirlwind. When that fierce-looking man barged in, it was the youngest who stood right in front of her and Yingying.
Granny Turtle calculated in her head. The coins from the Treasure Basin, these Song Coins, could buy so many things: flatbreads, steamed buns, rolls, noodles... The youngest would never have to live on thin gruel again. Ah, yes, the wheat had been harvested too. She should save a little toward buying land for both Yingying and the youngest.
But she couldn't just save it all. If the youngest came back, she ought to buy...
#YZheng's fried cakes... one... maybe three... make it five! She had heard of some saying like, "five sons passing the exams," or something similar. These days everyone wants an auspicious number, and the youngest should have one, too.#E

执于全而拙于思，偏于幽微而无大局。尽录其类机枢百年，无需多析，义理流变，已自现尔。
然水，变化之物，非拘于一时一处。不为则已，为，则算四时，划方圆，联万里，安八荒。
昔者禹之功，疏天下水而留法万代。至于今人，尽得先贤之智，又有机关术为助，不立旷古之业，则万卷经书、岂不枉读？可效之矣！

A Critique on the "Illustrated Evolution of Mohist Hydraulic Systems":

It is obsessed with completeness but clumsy in thought, biased toward the minute while lacking a grand vision. It exhaustively records a century's worth of mechanisms, rendering further analysis unnecessary, for the evolution of its principles has already laid itself bare.
Yet water is a thing of constant change; it cannot be confined to a single time or place. If one does not act, so be it. But if one must act, one must calculate the four seasons, delineate the square and the circle, connect ten thousand miles, and secure the eight desolate corners of the realm.
In antiquity, Yu the Great dredged the world's waters and left behind methods for ten thousand generations. As for us men of today, having inherited the wisdom of the sages and possessing the aid of mechanical arts, if we fail to establish an unprecedented legacy, have we not read our myriad scrolls in vain? We must rise and emulate his greatness!

zh:
小笼包
开封小笼包又称灌汤包，源于东京的灌汤馒头，东京七十二家正店之一的“王楼”制售的名为“山洞梅花包子”，号称“东京第一”。不过这些都是写给文人和游客看的。真要吃小笼包，还是得去找家正儿八经的本地小摊先端碗小米汤，在低矮的小桌旁找个缝儿和大爷大妈大叔大嫂们挤一挤一起坐下，再去要一屉热气腾腾的小笼包来。小米汤要等凉一点顺着边儿吸溜着喝，不然太热了烫嘴，太凉了香味儿少了汤也凝固了。在等小米汤凉的间隙，就可以研究着吃小笼包了。和那些每一口滋味儿都一样，可以呼噜呼噜往嘴里倒的饭菜不同，小笼包可是早点摊中最精致的了。它里头的汤汁滚烫鲜香，若是一口咬的大了，少不得狠狠挨一记烫。咬的少了呢，又变成汤汁，肉馅，薄皮分开吃，那就没意思了。所以吃小笼包是个技术活儿，非得吃多了吃熟练了才吃的痛快。小米汤未必是街头公认最好的搭头，但汤喝的太咸便影响品尝包子的味道，豆腐脑又太轻薄，唯有小米汤近乎无味但又有香味，喝进口扎扎实实有颗粒感压着舌头，这样一口有实感的汤反而更能衬出小笼包的皮之薄，肉馅之香，汤汁之美。至于为什么不是大米汤……或是因为开封那条街上只有卖小米汤的。真有别的汤也可以配来试试，说不得有新发现。
en:
15. Xiaolongbao

Kaifeng xiaolongbao, also called soup dumplings, trace their roots back to broth-filled buns from the Eastern Capital, Kaifeng. People say that among the city's seventy-two famous restaurants, Wanglou once sold "Cave Blossom Buns," crowned "Kaifeng's finest."

But that's for scholars to write down and tourists to repeat.

If you really want xiaolongbao, find a proper local stall. Order a bowl of millet soup first, squeeze into a gap at one of those low tables, and sit shoulder to shoulder with the locals. Then ask for a steaming basket of dumplings.

Let the millet soup cool a little and sip it from the rim. Too hot and it burns. Too cool and the aroma fades, and the soup starts to set.

While you wait, get ready for the real work. Unlike breakfast foods that taste the same in every bite and can be wolfed down without thinking, xiaolongbao is the most delicate thing on the stall's menu. The soup inside is scalding and fragrant. Bite too big and you'll pay for it. Bite too small and the soup, filling, and thin skin fall apart into separate mouthfuls, and that's no fun at all.

Xiaolongbao takes practice. Eat enough of them, and you'll finally learn how to enjoy them properly.

Millet soup might not be everyone's first choice, but anything too salty dulls the dumplings, and tofu pudding is too light. Millet soup is nearly plain yet still fragrant, with little grains that press against your tongue. That solid, honest sip makes the dumplings feel even thinner-skinned, meatier, and more beautiful.

As for why it's millet and not rice, maybe it's just because that street only sells millet soup. Still, if you spot another soup, try it. You might discover something new.

zh:
捕鸟这么多年，怪鸟见过不少，怪人见得也多。可那年遇见的那个画师，至今想起来，还觉得尤其邪乎。
渭西这带荒得很，偏偏野鸟扎堆，好下网。那天我一网下去，逮住只金鸟——叫金鸟，其实就是毛色亮些、叫声脆点，卖得上价。正解着绳结，一抬头，看见个画师立在几步外，直勾勾盯着我网里那鸟。
我当是生意上门，赶紧招呼：“买只玩玩？金鸟，稀罕货！”
为讨个好意头，我还翻出肚里那点墨水挂了个典故：“这金鸟爱啄金桃，吉祥长寿！”
他眼睛倏地亮了，却不是为这兆头：“金桃？”
“对对对……金桃嘛，也有人叫黄桃，甜得很！”
他摇摇头，哦，那这不是我要寻的鸟。
我问他：您要寻什么鸟？我捕鸟二十年，天上飞的地上跑的，没我不认识的！
“我听说有心有执念、未肯消散的英魂所化的金鸟——”
“啊？”
“他们从狮子的身躯里飞出。”
——得，是个疯子！
我忍着笑说：几十年这儿就是一片平野。您上别处寻去吧。
兵荒马乱的年头，人找鸟不是为了果腹就是为了换钱，谁扯什么“英魂”？
可他却自顾自念叨：这里该有狮子，石的。
“有石狮在，有金鸟栖。等到某一日……它终于被人知道了，便会从石狮口中飞出，冲天而去。”
“这百里平野，土堆都少见，哪来的石狮子？”我忍不住打断。
“那这里便该画一个。”
我摇摇头转身要去收别的网。没成想他竟还是叫住我，掏出钱买了这鸟。
我愣愣接了钱，看他小心翼翼捧出那只金鸟，理了理羽毛，一扬手——
那鸟儿扑棱棱飞走了。
嘿！真是个怪人。
en:
I've trapped birds for years, seeing my share of weird wings and even weirder folk. But that painter I met back then... even now, the memory of him feels straight-up eerie.
Out west by the Wei, the land's barren but wild birds gather in flocks. One day, I caught a golden bird. As I was tying it up, I noticed a painter staring intently at it just a few steps away.
I figured he was a customer and hollered over, "Care for a pet? A Golden Bird. A rare find!"
His eyes lit up, but not for that. "Golden peaches?"
"Right... Golden Peaches! Some folk just call 'em yellow peaches. Sweet as honey!"
He shook his head. "I'm looking for the Golden Birds born of restless souls, valiant spirits who refuse to fade. They take flight from the bellies of lions."
He even believed that golden birds roost where there's a stone lion.
But that plain barely had hills, not to mention a stone lion. Then he decided to paint one here, and later bought the bird from me. To my surprise, he just gently held it, straightened its feathers, and with a flick, the bird flew away.

zh: 黄沙漫天，行路多艰。你行走于玉门关外的无垠沙海之中。口干舌燥之际，你来到一处沙丘的阴凉之处，发现了一口枯井。这口井宽可容人。你还记得这里。你曾帮助马头村的挖井人取回井下的油灯。此刻，井中传来隐隐的水声与人声。你决定…… ⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛ 你沿着水道来到一处临时搭建的落脚点。这里的人们向你自豪地讲述着马头村的过往，讲述着安西军饮马地的雄壮，讲述着几代挖井人的努力，还讲述了一位游侠的相助……你明知这是一场梦，但你仍相信，只要那盏油灯还在，井下就永远会清泉常涌，人的希望便永不枯竭。问渠哪得清如许，唯有万代执灯来。
en:
Yellow sand fills the sky, and the journey is arduous. You press on through the endless sea of dunes beyond Jade Gate Pass. Parched and faint with thirst, you come to the shaded side of a dune, where you find an old, dry well. The well is wide enough for a person to descend. You remember this place. Once, you helped the well-digger of Horsehelm Village recover an oil lamp from the depths below. At this moment, the faint murmur of water and human voices echoes from within the well. You decide to...
Following the underground watercourse, you come upon a makeshift refuge. The people here speak to you with pride of Horsehelm Village's past, of the might of the Anxi Army's watering grounds, of the generations of well-diggers' efforts, and of the help once given by a wanderer... You know this is only a dream, yet you still believe that as long as that oil lamp burns, clear spring water will forever flow beneath, and human hope will never run dry. "How does the water remain so clear? Only because, through countless generations, lamp-bearers have come."

Qi Sheng was helping her older brother with frontline supplies when she came across a green-robed young officer. He moved his pieces with calm confidence, clearly in control, while his opponent scratched his head in frustration, sweating and hesitating before finally conceding defeat. Qi Sheng's eyes drifted over the board, and her competitive streak kicked in. "Wait!" She called out sharply, and took over for the defeated player. After more than twenty moves, Qi Sheng was finally checkmated, her expression shifting with surprise—she hadn't lost a game in years. True to her word, she looked the man over, raised an eyebrow, and asked, "Are you married?"

zh:
某日午后，怀月气冲冲跑回张府，拖了柄快和她一般高的陌刀，扭头就走。
廊下的淮深见状，伸腿一拦，目光扫过她脸上的几块青紫：“拿它做什么？”
“杀人！”
“姓李的嘴不干净！说我能识字就够了，学人读书给谁看！”
“我倒要让他瞧瞧，张怀月不仅读得了书，还举得起刀！”
“走。”淮深没再多问一句，抄过刀往肩上一扛，干脆利落。仿佛阿姊去杀人，他递刀都嫌慢。
本就候着怀月的索靖也丢下书，紧随其后，不发一言，目光却不离怀月，总想替她接下沉甸甸的刀。捧着块大石头归来的张球，正好撞见三人杀气腾腾地往外冲，此刻他也顾不上学什么刻碑了，忙不迭跟了出去。
就这样，淮深扛刀在前，大步流星，领着几人风风火火直奔李家。

那李家小子见了淮深，不自觉后退半步，嘴上却不肯输。
“男人婆搬救兵了？哟，是没爹要的张淮深啊！万年老二索靖也来凑数？还有个没用的球！哈哈，一帮废——”
淮深的拳风比话快，结结实实砸在他脸上。旁边几人扑上来帮忙，却被索靖挡得死死的。
怀月也顾不得其他，挥舞着刀就要杀。可怜张球，既想帮又想劝，推搡间，脑袋不知挨了谁的一棍子……
一时间尘土飞扬，棍棒交击，只听得哭爹喊娘，哀告求饶之声。
张球老实地交待了前后原委，听罢，张议潮无奈地叹了口气。
但在李家人面前，他少不得要责罚几句，于是叫孩子们回家好好反省，不许再惹事端。
夜半时分，四个小小的身影，不约而同溜上了城墙。
他们并排而坐，掰着圆圆的胡饼，望着圆圆的月亮，月华洗去一身尘灰。
“我说，你们几个手也太慢了！该多揍他几拳才解气！”
“拳脚无眼，我可是在护着你。”“嘁！”
说起白日的事，几人笑个不停，笑声散入夜风，越飘越远，直到被风雪埋没。
淮深枕着胳膊望天，任由雪落在脸上，身侧的打闹声入耳，却教他无比安心。
这一夜，距离张议潮束甲归唐，尚有二十一载，距离淮深执掌归义军，亦有二十一载。
淮深病重，怀月兵围节度使府，更是四十四载光阴之后。
此刻，他们只是四个不谙世事的天真少年，坐在高高的城墙上，同食一块胡饼，共望一轮月亮。
en:
One afternoon, Huaiyue ran back to the Zhang Mansion in a rage, dragged a Mo Blade almost as tall as herself, and turned to leave. 
Huaishen, standing under the corridor, stretched out his leg to stop her. His eyes glanced at the bruises on her face: "What are you going to do with it?" 
"Kill someone!" 
"That Li fellow's mouth is foul! He said it's enough that I can read, who am I studying to show off for!" 
"I'll make him see that Zhang Huaiyue not only can read, but can also wield a blade!" 
"Let's go." Without another word, Huaichen took the saber and slung it over his shoulder, clean and decisive. As if if his elder sister were going to kill someone, he'd be too slow just handing her the blade. 
Suo Jing, who had been waiting for Huaiyue anyway, also dropped his book and followed closely, saying nothing, yet his gaze never left Huaiyue, always wanting to take the heavy blade for her. Zhang Qiu, returning with a large rock in his arms, happened to run into the three of them charging out with murderous intent. At that moment, he forgot all about learning stone-carving and hurriedly followed them out. 
Just like that, Huaishen led the way with the sword on his shoulder, striding forward, and the group rushed to the Li Mansion in a fury. 

That Li lad, upon seeing Huaishen, involuntarily took half a step back, but his mouth refused to yield. 
"The tomboy brought reinforcements? Oh, it's Zhang Huaishen, the fatherless boy! And Suo Jing, the eternal second place, here to make up the numbers? And that useless Qiu! Haha, a bunch of losers..." 
Huaishen's fist was faster than words, landing solidly on his face. Several others nearby rushed to help, but were blocked firmly by Suo Jing. 
Huaiyue, disregarding all else, brandished the blade, ready to strike. Poor Zhang Qiu, wanting both to help and to mediate, got shoved around, and his head took a blow from someone's club... 
For a moment, dust flew, clubs clashed, and the sounds of crying for parents and begging for mercy filled the air. 
Zhang Qiu honestly explained the whole story. Hearing it, Zhang Yichao sighed helplessly. 
But in front of the Li family, he had to scold them a bit, so he told the children to go home and reflect, and not to cause any more trouble. 
At midnight, four small figures slipped onto the city wall as if by agreement. 
They sat side by side, breaking round pancake, gazing at the round moon, letting the moonlight wash away the dust and grime. 
"I say, you guys were way too slow! Should've punched him a few more times to really vent!" 
"Fists and feet have no eyes, I was protecting you." "Hmph!" 
When they talked about what happened during the day, the four laughed endlessly. Their laughter drifted into the night wind, growing farther and farther until it was swallowed by the snowstorm. 
Huaishen pillowed his arms and looked up at the sky, letting the snow fall on his face. The noise of frolicking beside him entered his ears, bringing him immense peace of mind. 
On this night, there were still twenty-one years until Zhang Yichao put on his armor and returned to the Tang Dynasty, and twenty-one years until Huaishen took command of the Guiyi Army. 
It would be another forty-four years before Huaishen fell seriously ill, and Huaiyue besieged the Governor's Residence with troops. 
At this moment, they were just four innocent teenagers, unfamiliar with the ways of the world. Sitting on the high city wall, they shared a single sesame seed cake and gazed at the same moon.

zh:
【乡饮酒礼第四】

乡饮酒之礼。主人就先生而谋宾、介。主人戒宾，宾拜辱；主人答拜，乃请宾。宾礼辞，许。主人再拜，宾答拜。主人退，宾拜辱。介亦如之。
乃席宾、主人、介、众宾之席，皆不属焉。尊两壶于房户间，斯禁，有玄酒，在西。设篚于禁南，东肆，加二勺于两壶。设洗于阼阶东南，南北以堂深，东西当东荣。水在洗东，篚在洗西，南肆。
羹定，主人速宾，宾拜辱，主人答拜。还，宾拜辱。介亦如之。宾及众宾皆从之。主人一相迎于门外，再拜宾，宾答拜；拜介，介答拜；揖众宾。主人揖，先入。宾厌介，入门左；介厌众宾，入；众宾皆入门左；北上。主人与宾三揖，至于阶，三让。主人升，宾升。主人阼阶上当楣北面再拜。宾西阶上当楣北面答拜。
主人坐取爵于篚，降洗。宾降。主人坐奠爵于阶前，辞。宾对。主人坐取爵，兴，适洗，南面坐，奠爵于篚下，盥洗，宾进东，北面辞洗。主人坐奠爵于篚，兴对。宾复位，当西序，东面。主人坐取爵，沃洗者西北面。卒洗，主人壹揖，壹让。升。宾拜洗。主人坐奠爵，遂拜。降盥。宾降，主人辞；宾对，复位，当西序。卒盥，揖让升。宾西阶上疑立。主人坐取爵，实之宾之席前，西北面献宾。宾西阶上拜，主人少退。宾进受爵，以复位。主人阼阶上拜送爵，宾少退。荐脯醢。宾升席，自西方。乃设折俎。主人阼阶东疑立。宾坐，左执爵，祭脯醢，奠爵于荐西，兴；右手取肺，却左手执本，坐，弗缭，右绝末以祭，尚左手，哜之，兴；加于俎，坐梲手，遂祭酒，兴；席末坐，啐酒，降席，坐奠爵，拜，告旨，执爵兴。主人阼阶上答拜。宾西阶上北面坐，卒爵，兴；坐奠爵，遂拜，执爵兴。主人阼阶上答拜。
宾降洗，主人降。宾坐奠爵，兴辞，主人对。宾坐取爵，适洗南，北面。主人阼阶东，南面辞洗。宾坐奠爵于篚，兴对。主人复阼阶东，西面。宾东北面盥，坐取爵，卒洗，揖让如初，升。主人拜洗。宾答拜，兴，降盥，如主人礼。宾实爵主人之席前，东南面酢主人。主人阼阶上拜，宾少退。主人进受爵，复位，宾西阶上拜送爵。荐脯醢。主人升席自北方。设折俎。祭如宾礼，不告旨。自席前适阼阶上，北面坐卒爵，兴，坐奠爵，遂拜，执爵兴。宾西阶上答拜。主人坐奠爵于序端，阼阶上北面再拜崇酒。宾西阶上答拜。
……
en:
【The Fourth Rite of District Drinking】

In the rite of district drinking, the host consults with the Master regarding the guests and the assistant. The host warns the guest, who bows in acknowledgment of the honor; the host returns the bow, then invites the guest. The guest politely declines, then accepts. The host bows twice, and the guest returns the bow. The host withdraws, and the guest bows in acknowledgment of the honor. The same is done for the assistant.
Then the seats for the guest, host, assistant, and all the guests are arranged, none of them connected. Two pots of wine are placed between the door and the window of the chamber, on a stand, with dark wine on the west side. A basket is set south of the stand, facing east, with two ladles added to the two pots. A basin is set southeast of the eastern steps, its north-south position determined by the depth of the hall, and its east-west position aligned with the eastern eave. Water is placed east of the basin, and the basket is west of the basin, facing south.
When the meat is cooked, the host hastens to invite the guest, who bows in acknowledgment of the honor; the host returns the bow. Upon returning, the guest bows in acknowledgment of the honor. The same is done for the assistant. The guest and all the other guests follow him. The host, with one attendant, welcomes them outside the gate, bows twice to the guest, who returns the bow; bows to the assistant, who returns the bow; and salutes the other guests. The host salutes and enters first. The guest yields to the assistant and enters through the left side of the gate; the assistant yields to the other guests and enters; all the other guests enter through the left side of the gate, facing north in order. The host and the guest exchange three salutes, and when they reach the steps, they yield three times. The host ascends, and the guest ascends. The host, on the eastern steps, facing north under the ridge beam, bows twice. The guest, on the western steps, facing north under the ridge beam, returns the bow.
The host sits, takes the goblet from the basket, and descends to wash it. The guest descends. The host sits, places the goblet before the steps, and declines. The guest responds. The host sits, takes the goblet, rises, approaches the basin, sits facing south, places the goblet beneath the basket, and washes his hands. The guest advances eastward, facing north, and declines the washing. The host sits, places the goblet in the basket, rises, and responds. The guest returns to his position, facing east by the western wall. The host sits, takes the goblet, and the one who pours the water faces northwest. When the washing is finished, the host makes one salute and one yielding. They ascend. The guest bows for the washing. The host sits, places the goblet, and then bows. He descends to wash his hands. The guest descends, and the host declines; the guest responds and returns to his position by the western wall. When the washing is finished, they salute, yield, and ascend. The guest stands upright on the western steps. The host sits, takes the goblet, fills it, and presents it before the guest's seat, facing northwest, offering it to the guest. The guest bows on the western steps, and the host withdraws slightly. The guest advances, receives the goblet, and returns to his position. The host bows on the eastern steps, sending off the goblet, and the guest withdraws slightly. Dried meat and pickled vegetables are presented. The guest ascends to his seat from the west. Then the divided meat on the stand is set out. The host stands upright east of the eastern steps. The guest sits, holds the goblet with his left hand, offers the dried meat and pickled vegetables, places the goblet west of the offerings, rises; with his right hand takes the lung, with his left hand turned back holding the root, sits, without twisting, cuts off the end with his right hand to offer, raises his left hand, tastes it, rises; places it on the stand, sits, wipes his hands, then offers the wine, rises; at the end of his seat, sits, sips the wine, descends from the seat, sits, places the goblet, bows, declares the wine excellent, takes the goblet, and rises. The host, on the eastern steps, returns the bow. The guest, on the western steps, sits facing north, drains the goblet, rises; sits, places the goblet, then bows, takes the goblet, and rises. The host, on the eastern steps, returns the bow.
The guest descends to wash, and the host descends. The guest sits, places the goblet, rises to decline, and the host responds. The guest sits, takes the goblet, approaches south of the basin, facing north. The host, east of the eastern steps, facing south, declines the washing. The guest sits, places the goblet in the basket, rises, and responds. The host returns east of the eastern steps, facing west. The guest, facing northeast, washes his hands, sits, takes the goblet, and when the washing is finished, salutes and yields as before, and ascends. The host bows for the washing. The guest returns the bow, rises, descends to wash his hands, as in the host's ritual. The guest fills the goblet before the host's seat, facing southeast, to toast the host. The host bows on the eastern steps, and the guest withdraws slightly. The host advances, receives the goblet, returns to his position, and the guest bows on the western steps, sending off the goblet. Dried meat and pickled vegetables are presented. The host ascends to his seat from the north. The divided meat on the stand is set out. He offers as in the guest's ritual, but does not declare the wine excellent. From before his seat, he approaches the eastern steps, sits facing north, drains the goblet, rises, sits, places the goblet, then bows, takes the goblet, and rises. The guest, on the western steps, returns the bow. The host sits, places the goblet at the end of the eastern wall, and on the eastern steps, facing north, bows twice in honor of the wine. The guest, on the western steps, returns the bow.
……

zh:
张家食肆的招牌挂上过，被闹事的砸下来过，又被找人翻新过，兜兜转转总算立住了脚。
去取家里新招牌这天，张安康七岁，不高，刚到他娘腰间。
他跟着娘跨过街，路过升平桥，那些高头大马都比他的人更高，街上的店铺里都摆着他没见过的稀奇玩意，他被娘拉着，绕着那些高头大马、繁华锦绣的店铺走，娘拉走了他的人和手，他的眼睛却离不开那些。
他一步三回头地到了木匠铺子，木锯子木刨子呼啦啦地叫，木屑子满天满地飞。
他娘蹲下来瞧新招牌，他坐在一边的凳子上四处望，瞧招牌也瞧他娘。

那块崭新的招牌可大，张家食肆四个字也大，显得他娘更瘦更小，头上用了好些年的破木钗子在他面前晃，化在木屑里，像是木匠铺子里，漫天飞的木屑子里的一小块。
他没忍住看了好久，比在来的路上，看那些高头大马和锦绣店铺更久。
他想起店里往来的客人常说——让他娘找个依靠，起码能给她买些新钗子。
张安康想，新钗子是怎么样的呢。
十岁的张安康明白了。
新钗子是街上的高头大马，是店里的稀奇玩意，是木匠铺里巨大的新招牌，是一眼就能让人瞧见的好东西，不会化在漫天木屑子里头。
有了这个东西，娘就变成了过得好的人，有依靠的人，不会受世上闲言碎语的人。

回去的路上，他跨过街，路过升平桥，高头大马依旧比他人高，店铺里依旧摆着他没见过的稀奇玩意，他看着娘头上的木钗子，再之后他的眼睛盯着一家店，他看见人流往来，里头有着许多漂亮的钗子首饰。
那店里的人拉着客人：“咱们金氏头面——”
他被娘狠狠一拽：“看路，混小子！”
en:
The Zhang family's restaurant sign had been hung, smashed by troublemakers, refurbished, and finally stabilized after many twists. 
On the day they went to collect the new sign, Zhang Ankang was seven years old, only reaching his mother's waist.
He followed her across the street, past Harmonic Span. The towering horses loomed taller than him. The shops displayed wonders he'd never seen. His mother pulled him along, steering him clear of the bustling crowds and lavish storefronts, but though she dragged his body forward, his eyes lingered behind.
At the carpenter's workshop, saws and planes screeched, wood shavings swirling in the air.
His mother crouched to inspect the new sign, while he sat on a stool, looking around, at the sign, and at her.

The freshly carved sign was huge, the characters for "Zhang's Eatery" bold and imposing, making his mother seem even thinner, even smaller. Her old wooden hairpin, worn for years, swayed before his eyes, blending into the flurry of wood shavings, just another tiny speck in the storm of sawdust.
He stared longer than he had at the horses and fancy shops on the way here.
He remembered the customers at the eatery often saying to his mother: "Find yourself a supporter, at least then you could afford a new hairpin.
Zhang Ankang wondered: "What would a new hairpin look like?"
By ten, he understood.
A new hairpin was like the tall horses on the street, the exotic treasures in the shops, the grand new signboard in the carpenter's workshop. It was something bright and unmistakable, something that wouldn't disappear into a cloud of sawdust.
With it, his mother would become someone who "lived well", someone with backing, someone spared from the world's gossip.

On the way back, crossing Harmonic Span again, the horses still loomed over him, the shops still overflowed with strange, nameless wonders. His gaze shifted from his mother's wooden hairpin to a jewelry shop, where customers streamed in and out, and glittering hair ornaments lined the displays.
A shopkeeper called out, "Jin's Jewelry here..."
His mother yanked him roughly, "Watch where you're going, you scamp!"

zh:
前些日子又有不少村民下井后病倒了，她爹也在其中，她为这事连着数日水米未进，人也变得憔悴消瘦，我虽焦心，一时也不知道能帮上什么忙。
……
她对那些会唱歌的鸟儿喜欢得紧，也许我该抓一只送给她，说不定能解了她眉头的愁意。
……
我原以为抓鸟比挖井容易，却差点被半路杀出的鹰叨了胳膊。回村后我把鸟儿给了她，她果真欢喜得很，一直追问着是哪里得来的，我不知该如何开口，只好诓她说是碰巧抓到的……
……
她父亲的病愈发重了，听说商队有药可医，只是他们家实在拿不出值钱的物件来抵。领头的人倒对我抓的鸟儿颇感兴趣，愿用药换这稀罕东西。她看向我的时候，我立马开口连声答应了。这本就是属于她的东西，我有何不允呢？
……
商队离去时，她哭红了眼，一直站在村口远望，直到车马的足迹消失在风沙里。我知道她是舍不得那鸟儿，一时说不出宽慰的话，只好立下誓言，她虽没了鸟儿的陪伴，但我会一直守在她身侧，必不弃她。
en:
Recently, many villagers fell ill after going down the well, and her father among them. She hasn't eaten or drunk anything in days, growing pale and thin. I'm worried sick, but I don't know what I can do.
...
She loves those singing birds. Maybe I should catch one for her. It might take her mind off things.
...
I thought catching a bird would be easier than digging a well, but I nearly got my arm clawed by an eagle that came out of nowhere. When I gave her the bird back in the village, she lit up, asking over and over where I'd found it. I couldn't bring myself to tell her the truth, so I said I'd just stumbled across it...
...
Her father's condition worsened. Word was that a merchant caravan had medicine that could help, but her family had nothing of value to trade. The caravan leader, though, took a real interest in my bird, and said he'd swap medicine for it. When she looked at me, I didn't hesitate. The bird was hers anyway. How could I refuse?
...
When the caravan left, she stood at the village entrance with red-rimmed eyes, watching until the dust settled and the tracks disappeared. I knew she was heartbroken over the bird. I couldn't find the right words, so I made her a promise: she might not have the bird anymore, but I'd stay by her side. Always.

zh:
墨山道有内外门之别，入内门则探渊索珠，为千年计；入外门则专工其器，为万民益。
常人谓：“盖以天赋为别？内门为大才，外门为小才。”余思之非也。
周广顺中，有一漠姓外门弟子。与诸长老以机括之术对战，连下三城而不败，人皆叹服。
其人机括，重实效而形制粗野，原为内门所鄙。
经此一战，其声名大噪，粗野之风，竟一时风靡，门人竞相以机关粗陋为傲。
时至今日，旧事渐隐，独此风不坠。
en:
The Mohist Hill distinguishes between inner and outer disciples. Becoming inner disciples means probing the depths, planning for millennia, while being outer disciples means specializing in crafting tools for the benefit of all people.
To many, "Is the distinction based on innate talent? Inner disciples for great talent, outer disciples for lesser talent." I think differently.
An outer disciple surnamed Mo, in a contest of mechanical devices against several elders, won three consecutive rounds undefeated, earning everyone's admiration.
His mechanisms emphasized practicality but were wild in form, originally looked down upon by the inner disciples.
After this contest, his fame soared. This rough, unrefined style actually became fashionable for a time, with disciples competing to take pride in the crude appearance of their mechanisms.
To this day, the old story has gradually faded, but this style alone has not fallen out of use.

zh:
十七岁那年，我救了一个汉人回来，他叫陈怀卿，听了“长生仙人”的传说，来寻解毒的方子。
我讨厌这个称呼，我是相貌与常人不同，不是仙人，我也没有一声大吼震碎毒虫，我只是跟着阿婆学过怎么驱使它们。
陈怀卿讲了外面很多的趣事，我听得很快活，原来村子之外不但有江湖，还有庙学，有佛堂，有我从没见过的节日。但阿婆拦住了我，说外面的人心毒，见了会烂眼睛，她走江湖炼长生虫的时候见过，因此瞎了。
陈怀卿临走的时候，讲了江湖人相互下毒的事，他说一定要拿到解毒的方子救家里人，我心软了，偷了阿婆的方子，藏在灯里给了他。
他捧着灯出了寨子，我望着他的背影，灯光在鹿食林的雾里像一只扑腾的火毒蝶。
后来，我听说他在外自称“长生仙人弟子”，但他从不与我通消息，也没回来道谢。
阿婆骂我不知道人心险恶，说这就是外边人心的模样，你对他们好，你得不到回报。
这年生辰，阿婆将蟾王交给了我，说蟾王体内藏着长生虫，许多人都想得到它。阿婆还说，要是她不在了，长生虫能保全我和大家的性命，但这虫一旦用了，就回不去了。
en:
When I was seventeen, I saved a Han man named Chen Huaiqing. He had followed the whispers of the Immortal of Longevity, seeking an antidote.
I despise that title. I'm no immortal, just look different from the folk here. And I certainly can't "shatter venomous swarms with a single roar." I'd learned only from Granny how to command them, not conquer them.
Chen Huaiqing told me stories of the world beyond—of the jianghu, of temples and shrines, of festivals I'd never heard of. I listened eagerly, but Granny warned me: "Outsiders' hearts are poison. One look, and your eyes will rot." She'd seen it herself in her youth, back when she roamed the martial world refining the Longevity Parasite. That's how she'd gone blind.
Before he left, Chen Huaiqing spoke of the jianghu's endless poison feuds. "I need that antidote to save my family," he pleaded. My heart softened. I stole Granny's formula, hid it inside a lamp, and gave it to him.
As he left the village, I watched his silhouette fade into the mists of Deerforage Grove. The lamp's glow flickered like a struggling dying moth. Later, I heard he'd proclaimed himself a "Disciple of the Immortal of Longevity". Yet he never sent word, never returned to thank me.
Granny scolded me. "You know nothing of men's hearts. This is their nature. Kindness goes unrewarded."
That year, for my birthday, she entrusted me with the Toad King. "The Everlasting Parasite stays within," she said. "Many covet it. If I'm gone, it will protect you all. But once used, there's no turning back."

若要学子们为藏书馆评出一位风雅之最，当选者或非双元也，非十相也，实乃小狗才子是也。
才子生得一身墨色，身姿优雅纤长，如同将文津馆衣装贴身穿住了一般。有人作揖，它也抬起一只前爪，学着拱一拱。有人念诗，它便安静听着，偶尔眨眨眼，仿佛在说听得懂。有回一位老先生咳嗽了一声，才子竟叼着自己的水碗走过去，轻轻放在老先生脚边。
老先生愣了半天，摸着它的头说：“有礼了，有礼了。”才子轻摇尾巴，依旧风度端方。
然而前些日子，闯入馆中挑战双元的江湖客大大扰乱了学堂秩序，才子本是个文人，这下也怒了。一向不紧不慢的才子竟呲牙咆哮起来，以一狗之力将一众草莽尽数吓退。
众人欣慰道，这下才子更像文津馆的狗狗了。小狗之吼，怎么不是一种雄辩之才？
en:
If the scholars were asked to name the most refined soul in the Archives, the title would belong neither to the Twin Mavens nor the Ten Sages, but to the little dog, Prodigy.
Prodigy boasts a coat as black as ink and a sleek, graceful frame, as though it were tailored into the scholarly robes of the Inkbound Order. When someone offers a formal bow, it raises a front paw and mimics the salute. When someone recites poetry, it listens quietly, blinking now and then as if it understands every word. Once, when an elderly master coughed, Prodigy picked up its own water bowl and gently set it down by the master's feet.
Stunned for a moment, the old master patted its head and chuckled, "Most polite of you, little one." Prodigy merely gave a gentle wag of its tail, keeping its dignified composure.
Yet not long ago, a band of martial ruffians barged in to challenge the Twin Mavens, throwing the academy into chaos. Gentle as Prodigy was, the scholar within it was stirred to fury. The usually placid hound bared its teeth and let out a fierce roar, driving off the entire mob on its own.
Everyone smiled with pride, remarking that Prodigy was now a true Inkbound Order dog. After all, is a hound's fierce bark not its own form of eloquence?

Nor does she desire to be anyone's master. With wolves, she is a companion day and night, an inseparable family. Beasts have never sought to tame—yet men always try to tame the wild.

zh:
佛光顶上，阳光被佛光玉折为虹彩。一位禅师一半僧衣一半劲装，手持禅杖，静立如那诸佛造像中的一尊。 你听闻这位禅师早已易名北上，如今，却在此地意外相逢。禅师面具之下的脸波澜不惊，你只远远听得声如洪钟的询问：小施主，你是想见我的假相，法相，还是真相？……
#Y假相。你想起那些北去的义士，想起他们抛却的姓名与身份，耳边想起了萧萧风声。你希望他以假相示人，将真相留于功成归来之日。#E
禅师并未回答，而是低声颂了句佛号。霎时间，你仿佛看到他身后狂风呼啸，一尊巨大的佛像显露出来。“纵观三相，不如无相。”耳边传来禅师低沉而洪亮的声音。他背后的巨佛像双手合十，风沙隐去了他的身形。待风沙散去，佛光顶上唯有日光彻地，虹彩依然，仿佛禅师从未出现。你不禁怀疑，方才那无相无定之人是否真的折返清河？还是自己这一程入梦又醒，自己产生了幻觉？
en:
Atop Halo Peak, sunlight fractured through the Buddha's Light Jade into drifting rainbow hues. There stood a Chan master, clad half in monk's robes and half in martial garb, Khakkhara staff in hand, as motionless as one of the myriad Buddha statues.
You had heard this master had long since changed his name and journeyed north, yet here, of all places, you unexpectedly crossed paths. His face beneath the mask was entirely unreadable; from afar, you only heard his voice, resonant as a temple bell, asking, "Young patron, do you wish to see my false form, my Dharma form, or my true form?"...
#YFalse form. Your thought drifts back to the righteous souls who journeyed north, leaving behind their names and identities, as the bleak wind echoes in your ears. You hope he will face the world in his false form, saving his true form for the day he returns in triumph.#E
The master gave no answer, but murmured the Buddha's name under his breath. In that instant, howling winds seemed to surge behind him, and the silhouette of a colossal Buddha manifested. "To behold the three forms is not as profound as the formless," the master's low, sonorous voice echoed right beside your ear. Behind him, the great Buddha pressed its palms together, and wind and sand swallowed his form whole. When the wind and sand settled, only sunlight bathed Halo Peak. The rainbows remained unchanged, as if the Chan master had never been there at all. You could not help but wonder whether that formless, unbound man had truly returned to Qinghe. Or perhaps this whole journey had been no more than a dream, leaving you with nothing but a hallucination?
Jade Within the Body

昔有五百猕猴，游行林中。俱至大树下，树下有井，井中有月影现。
时猕猴主见是月影，语诸伴曰：“月今日死，落于井中，当共出之，莫令世间长夜暗冥。”
共作议言：云何能出？时猕猴主言：我知出法。我捉树枝，汝捉我尾。展转相连，乃可出之。时诸猕猴，即如主语，展转相捉。树弱枝折，一切猕猴堕井水中。
en:
Once there were five hundred macaques wandering through the forest. Together they came to a great tree. Beneath the tree was a well, and in the well appeared the reflection of the moon.
When the macaque chief saw the moon's reflection, he said to the others:
"The moon has fallen into the well and perished. We must rescue it together and not let the world be plunged into endless darkness."
The macaques discussed it among themselves, saying, "How can we get it out?"
Then the macaque chief said, "I know a way. I will grab hold of the tree branch, and you will grab my tail. Then each of you can hold on to the next, one after another. That way we can pull it out."
So the macaques did exactly as their chief said, each clutching the next in turn. But the branch was too weak and snapped, and all the macaques fell into the well.

月影摇曳，夜宴无休，金樽玉盏，满座衣香。笙歌沸处，画阁千重，金钗扶醉归。世人皆慕此楼之盛，以为极乐尽在于此。却不知极乐之外，另有极乐。灯火阑珊处，笙歌或又起。
en:
Verdant Tavern stands where the lake meets the hills, overlooking the boundless green waters. The beams are carved, the rails painted red. The songs of oarsmen and the calls of the causeway mix beneath the tavern, making it the finest sightseeing spot for travelers. When first built, it rose splendid and grand, completed in but a few days, becoming the crowning view of the lakeshore.
When the decree on the wine monopoly was enacted, Verdant Tavern alone was granted the official license—only here could the government-brewed wine be bought.
Moonlight sways, and the night's feasting never ceases; golden cups and jade goblets fill every seat, and the fragrance of fine robes lingers. Where the sheng and song rise, painted chambers stretch a thousandfold, and golden hairpins sway as ladies return home drunk. All the world admires the splendor of this place, believing that ultimate bliss is found here. Yet they know not that beyond this bliss lies another. Where the lanterns grow faint and few, the sheng and song may yet rise again.

菜馍
有人说中原人的早点全是油炸之物，这还是要辟谣澄清的。菜馍就是中原人早餐时重要的一道以菜为主，没用到油炸的面点。若要解释菜馍，得先解释烙馍。菜馍便是擀两张没烙的烙馍，先铺一张作为床单，在上面放满时令的蔬菜——春天吃荠菜，菠菜，韭菜多些，夏天能见到苋菜和荆芥来客串，秋冬季节因着要清点这一年的收获，更是什么都有。最后将另一张薄而柔软的大面饼像被子一样盖在上面，放在热腾腾的床板上静静等待，让一年四季的菜叶和滋味都在这一床大被下做个好梦。
en:
6. Vegetable Flatbread

Some people claim Central Plains breakfasts are all deep-fried. Let's set the record straight. Vegetable flatbread is a staple that puts vegetables front and center, with no frying involved.

To explain it, you first need to know luomo, a thin flatbread cooked on a hot griddle. For vegetable flatbread, you roll out two sheets before they're cooked.

Lay one down like a bedsheet and pile on seasonal greens. In spring, you'll see shepherd's purse, spinach, and chives. In summer, amaranth and schizonepeta join the mix. Come autumn and winter, when the harvest gets tallied up, almost anything can go in.

Then you cover it with the second soft sheet like a quilt and set it on the hot griddle to wait, while the flavors of all four seasons fall asleep together under one big blanket.

The moon will rise, the moon will set. At home a treasure basin is kept. 
Don't cry, my dear, just close your eyes. While you sleep, treasures multiply. 
Heavy eyes and dreams so deep. Rest now, my child, drift off to sleep. 
When morning stars outshine the blue, you'll wake to find your dreams come true. 
(A marginal note, seemingly not by the songwriter):
"Though striving for verses even an old crone can understand, they lack the piercing power to move hearts. While polishing these lines, I suddenly recalled Nie Yizhong's "Ode to Peasant Families". Setting its verses to song, they strangely harmonize with the melody. This must be fate—let me blend them into one composition." 
In February, they sell fresh silk still on the reel;
In May, new grain is sold before the mill. 
A plaster for today's wound, but they carve out a piece of heart—
Treating the surface, yet tearing out the very core. 
Oh, that the sovereign's heart might turn to a candle of light— 
The moon refuses to light feasts of silk-clad lords,
But shines on hovels where refugees cower.

“宗贤哥，家主当真传讯说“万事齐备，所谋将成”？”
“好！真好！阿爹和阿姊的牺牲，总算没有白费。流寇与赵宋欠我们的血债与公道，终是能向他们一一讨还！”
——报仇？报什么仇？你正想着，他们又提到了要提防今日闯进来的江湖人。
“为了以防万一，这几日祠堂的钥匙，还是宗贤哥带着更为稳妥。”
“便如此吧。咳咳... 我先回库房，稍后众人再自行离去。”
——是白天听到的男声！接着，随着开门与关门的声音，方才嘈杂的集会声逐渐低了下来。
en:
The villagers' voices become clearer once the rooftop is removed: 
"Brother Zongxian, did the family head really send word that 'all is prepared, and the plan will succeed'?" 
"Great! Father and sister's sacrifices have not been in vain. The debts of blood and justice owed to us by the bandits and the Song court will finally be repaid!" 
—Revenge? What revenge? As you're wondering, they caution about the wanderer who has intruded earlier. 
"Just in case, it's best to have Brother Zongxian hold the key over the next few days." 
"Agreed. *coughs* I'll head back to the storeroom first. The others shall leave shortly on their own." 
It's the same male voice you've heard earlier that day. Then, with the creak of doors opening and closing, the once boisterous gathering gradually falls silent.

而一眨眼，大鹅飞走了，少东家却没影了。
大伙正愣神，有人遥遥瞧见熟悉的衣角一闪而过。于是揉腰的揉腰，捶腿的捶腿，各自散了。
而若仔细瞧，会发现他们的嘴角都带着笑——有那位在，少东家呀，丢不了！
en:
Even seven or eight days after Spring Festival's Eve, the adults in Heaven's Pier were still rubbing their backs and groaning now and then.
That was all because of what happened at the reunion dinner. The Young Master made a grab for a jug of wine and somehow ended up riding a big white goose all over the courtyard.
The adults ran after him laughing and shouting, tripping over each other, bumping into each other, and finally collapsing in a heap.
Then in the blink of an eye, the goose was gone, and so was the boy.
Everyone stopped short. Then someone caught sight of a familiar edge of clothing in the distance. After that, people went back to rubbing sore backs and pounding their legs, and everyone went their separate ways.
But if you looked closely, they were all smiling. With that person there, the Young Master would be perfectly safe!

一日寒香寻路过一野村，见路边一人躺在驴背上姿势怪异，忍不住多看了几眼。那人没睁眼却好似有所感应一般，开口说道：“你这命格倒是特殊。”

寒香寻私下张望确认无人，才知眼前这人的确是在和自己说话。
“这荒郊野岭的，能骗几个钱？”
“哈哈，年柱见劫煞，日柱见孤辰。若命局有此二神入命，此命犯天煞孤星。”
“天煞孤星又如何？”
“当无父无母，家破人亡。凡有夫妻，则夫妻死，若有儿女，则儿女苦。”

“……”想不到此人还有点本事，竟能道出她前半生这些倒灶事。寒香寻只觉得可笑，难道从前种种，只是因为自己的命吗？

“老娘命不好早就知道了，要你个鬼道士戳人心窝？”
“非也，非你的命。此命格乃是男命，应是你的至亲。你不过是被波及。”
“我，我的至亲？哦，你说那个天杀的。”寒香寻想起她那卖妻卖子女的亲爹，恨意又涌上心头。
“是耶非耶……”那道人没再多说，驾着身下的毛驴就走远了，只留寒香寻还站在原地。
en:
One day, as Han Xiangxun traveled through a remote village, her eyes were drawn to a figure lying awkwardly on a donkey by the roadside. Intrigued, she stopped and took a second glance. The man, though his eyes were closed, seemed to sense her presence and spoke, "Your fate is quite unusual."

Han Xiangxun scanned the area, ensuring there was no one else around, and then realized he was speaking directly to her.
"Out here in the wilderness, what could you possibly swindle me out of?" The man chuckled softly, then continued, 
"Your year pillar shows calamity, your day pillar shows loneliness. When these two stars align in one's fate, that person is marked by the doomed loner."
"Doomed loner? So what then?"
"A doomed loner lives without parents, without kin. Marry, and your spouse will die; have children, and they will suffer."

Silence hung in the air as Han Xiangxun took in his words. He had indeed revealed all those misfortunes in the first half of her life. A bitter laugh escaped her lips. Was it just fate that had shaped all the misfortune in her life?

"I've long known my life's a mess. Don't need some damned priest rubbing salt in the wound!"
"No, no, it's not because of you. This fate belongs to a man, someone very close to you. You, however, are merely caught in the ripple of it."
"Someone... close to me?" Han Xiangxun's mind raced, her anger and hatred flaring as she remembered her father who had sold his wife and children without a second thought.
"It is him, and also not..." The man fell silent, urging his donkey forward, leaving Han Xiangxun standing there.

zh:
游侠亲启：
岁序更替，雪融春至。值此新岁，老朽敬祝游侠佳节安康。
此番提笔，实是被福、禄、寿那三个娃娃缠得紧，非闹着要给少侠写信。老规矩，童言无忌，她们说一句，老朽便如实代录一句。
小福：老山！这墨汁闻着怎么甜甜的，能吃吗？……哎呀！这句别记上去！
小寿：大个子，你去哪儿威风啦？我们都在这儿巴巴地等着你呢！
……娃娃们七嘴八舌，老朽落笔都要跟不上了。罢了，还是言简意赅，替她们把正事说了吧。
新春已至，汴京城里火树银花，好生热闹。杂耍的、唱戏的、卖时令糕点的，应有尽有。娃娃们想请少侠去逛逛，顺道将这些市井烟火、满城春色，都收录进册子里。待到来日想起这过年的乐趣，便翻开看看。“贺新岁，录嘉时”……这般雅事，老朽也颇为期待呢。
小禄：哎哎！我还没说完呢！老山快记下——游侠走南闯北见多识广，眼神肯定最好使了！等你把册子填得满满当当，别忘了拿给我们看，我们仨可是凑了“小惊喜”要送给你呢！

#Y参与春节活动「录嘉时」，游历汴京，记录年俗风物，完成「新春岁时记」即可解锁更多奖励。#E
en:
Dear Wanderer,
As the seasons turn and the snow gives way to spring, I wish you peace and health in this new year.
I take up my brush today because those three little ones, Fu, Lu, and Shou, have been pestering me relentlessly to write to you. As is the rule, children speak their hearts, and I shall record their words as faithfully as they fall.
Little Fu: Laoshan! This ink smells so sweet, can I eat it? ...Oh no! Don't you dare write that down!
Little Shou: Big friend, where have you been showing off lately? We've been waiting here for you forever!
...The children are chattering all at once; my brush can hardly keep pace. Enough, let me be brief and speak of the matter at hand.
Spring is here, and Kaifeng is ablaze with festive lanterns and flowers. The streets are full of acrobats, opera performers, seasonal sweets, and all the bustle of the holiday season. The children wish for you to wander the streets and capture the bustle of life and the city's spring beauty within your album. "To record the good times of the New Year"... Such an elegant pursuit is something even I look forward to.
Little Lu: Hey! I'm not done! Laoshan, write this: Wanderer, you've been everywhere and seen it all, so you must have the sharpest eyes! Once you've filled that album to the brim, don't forget to bring it back and show us. The three of us have also prepared a little surprise for you!

#YParticipate in the "Good Times Record" event. Explore Kaifeng, document customs and scenery, and complete the "Springtide Chronicle" to unlock rewards.#E

朔风卷起旌旗，远处狼烟未散。

那一次出征的前夜，恩师郭怀烈造访张淮深的营帐，师徒无言对坐良久，天地间唯余瀚海风鸣。

三更将尽时，郭怀烈还是忍不住问出了那个问题：“此战之险，非患寇强，惟患庙堂掣肘……若是不归，该当如何？”
“夫战者，义不可辞。若身死，万勿怀恨，万勿复仇，万勿究底。”张淮深举起酒葫一饮而尽，“凡战者当如是，纵殁他故，亦当如是。”

数十年后，风沙磨尽碑碣，凉州依旧白雪如银。百岁有余的郭怀烈又听到了那晚同样的风鸣。
葫中日月葬我，何必青山埋骨。
恍然间，他似乎又看到了那个策马的少年，依然是风华正茂的模样。
en:
The north wind rolls the banners; distant beacon smoke still lingers. 

The night before that campaign, mentor Guo Huailie visited Zhang Huaishen's tent. They sat in silence, only the desert wind between them. 

Near midnight, Guo finally asked: "The danger of this battle lies not in enemy strength, but in court interference... If you don't return, what then?" 
"Warriors cannot refuse duty. If I die, hold no hatred, seek no revenge, dig no deeper." Zhang Huaishen drank from his gourd. "Every soldier should face death so—even if fallen by other means." 

Decades later, wind and sand have worn the stele, but Liangzhou's snow remains silver. Centenarian Guo Huailie hears the same wind from that night. 
The sun and moon in a gourd can bury me—why need green hills for bones? 
Suddenly, he saw that youthful rider again, forever in his prime.

zh:
“长安大道横九天……逛了一整天，名不虚传。不过你带我来这儿干嘛？安记胡饼……我看这胡饼店平平无奇，也没什么了不起嘛？” 
“就说你笨。你不是来找长安精怪的？你去大街上能找到啥？还是得往这种地方来。” 
诚如所言，这处街巷没有显贵豪宅，不见胡姬酒肆，说是城里最平凡的角落也不为过。那些惊才绝艳的才子佳人，引人遐思的传奇，应该都与此处无关吧。 
少女指向不远处的院落：“我儿时住在此地。旁边就是观音婆婆的家。” 
观音婆婆是这街里小有名气的人物。据说观音婆婆本姓曹，年轻时貌美如观音，为寻亲从凉州归乡。观音婆婆虽失明，却颇受人敬重，皆因她精通佛法，至今还隔三差五有书铺店家或僧尼登门，请观音婆婆帮忙翻译和校对梵文经书。街坊们私下里都在传，说观音婆婆该是有些神通在身上。不然，她怎么跋涉过千里大漠的？观音婆婆有个店面，叫安记胡饼铺子，里面设了一面题壁，说是若诗写得好便免了餐钱。有好奇的妇人打听过这铺子怎么姓安，那时婆婆只说是她心上人的铺子。只是这么多年过去，大家还没见过哪个姓安的男人来宣称这铺子是他的。 
“听来是位佛缘深厚的才女……可这又如何？跟我要找的长安精怪可不相干。” 
“你别急啊。你就不好奇，观音婆婆那个姓安的心上人是谁？” 
“能是谁。又一个抛家弃子的臭男人呗。” 
“诶诶，别急呀。我越长大越觉着，我小时候可能无意中撞见过婆婆的心上人……你想，婆婆是有神通傍身的观音，她的心上人……说不得并非凡人。” 
“啊！你是说……精怪！快，快讲讲！” 
“我儿时有次在上元灯节迷路，进了一个黑漆漆的小巷子，我看不见路，蹲下大哭起来。你说怪不怪，明明是灯节，那巷子里却黑的什么都看不见……现在想来，应该是被妖怪施了障眼法了。” 
“有道理……” 
“然后，我突然听见有人喊我。我一抬头，看见了来找我的观音婆婆。她背后有好大一轮月亮……那巷子黑的就像化不开的墨，灯的光照不进来，可月亮的光却照得进来。巷子里到处都是黑的，只有婆婆身边被月光照着……婆婆走到哪儿，月光就照到哪儿。就像是，单照她一个人似的。” 
少女说着，回想起小时候观音送她出巷子，找到了她的父母。跟着父母道过谢后，她心有所感，忍不住回头看了一眼。月光下，依稀有一个人影，陪在观音婆婆身边。她眨了眨眼又去看，那人又消失了。 
  
“观音婆婆，你有神通吗？”黑漆漆的巷子里，小女孩瘪着嘴要哭不哭地牵着观音的手往前走去。 
“有的。”清亮的月光下，观音对她笑了。 
“我的神通啊，可以把月亮叫到身边来。” 
今夕何夕，得见此月。 
今夕有客，可赐光明。 
她早已拥有。
en:
"Chang'an's great avenues span the nine heavens… We've been wandering all day, it lives up to its reputation. But why did you bring me here? An's Pancakes… This pancake shop looks ordinary, nothing special."  
"That's because you're dumb. Weren't you looking for Chang'an's spirits and oddities? What could you find on the main streets? You have to come to places like this."  
As stated, this street had no grand mansions of the nobility, no foreign style wine shops with dancing girls, one could say it was the most ordinary corner of the city. Those dazzlingly talented scholars and beauties, those legends that sparked imagination, likely had nothing to do with this place.  
The young girl pointed to a courtyard not far away, "I lived here as a child. Next door is Granny Goddess of Mercy's house."  
Granny Goddess of Mercy was a somewhat famous figure in this street. It was said her original surname was Cao, and in her youth she was as beautiful as Goddess of Mercy. She returned to her hometown from Liangzhou to search for family. Though blind, Granny Goddess of Mercy was highly respected because she was well-versed in Buddhist teachings. Even now, bookstore owners or monks and nuns would visit every so often, asking Granny Goddess of Mercy to help translate and proofread Sanskrit scriptures. The neighbors privately spread rumors that Granny Goddess of Mercy must possess some divine powers. Otherwise, how could she have traversed a thousand miles of desert? Granny Goddess of Mercy had a shop called An's Pancakes, which featured an inscription wall, it was said that if you wrote a good poem, your meal was free. Curious women had inquired why the shop bore the surname An. At that time, Granny only said it was her beloved's shop. But after all these years, no one had ever seen a man surnamed An come to claim the shop as his.  
"Sounds like a talented woman with deep Buddhist connections… But so what? This has nothing to do with the Chang'an spirits I'm looking for."  
"Don't rush. Aren't you curious about who Granny Goddess of Mercy's beloved, surnamed An, is?"  
"Who could it be? Just another rotten man who abandoned his family."  
"Hey, hey, don't be hasty. The older I get, the more I feel that as a child I might have accidentally encountered Granny's beloved… Think about it, Granny is Goddess of Mercy with divine powers. Her beloved… might not be an ordinary person."  
"Ah! You mean… a spirit! Quick, tell me more!"  
"Once as a child during the Lantern Festival, I got lost and entered a pitch-black alley. I couldn't see the way, so I crouched down and cried. Isn't it strange? It was the Lantern Festival, yet that alley was so dark you couldn't see anything… Thinking back now, it was probably an illusion cast by a monster."  
"Makes sense…"  
"Then, I suddenly heard someone call me. I looked up and saw Granny Goddess of Mercy coming to find me. Behind her was a huge moon… The alley was dark like ink that wouldn't dissolve, the lantern light couldn't penetrate, but the moonlight could. Everywhere in the alley was dark, except around Granny, who was bathed in moonlight… Wherever Granny walked, the moonlight shone. It was as if it shone on her alone."  
The young girl spoke, recalling how Goddess of Mercy led her out of the alley as a child and found her parents. After thanking them with her parents, sensing something, she couldn't help but glance back. In the moonlight, there was a faint figure accompanying Granny Goddess of Mercy. She blinked and looked again, and the person disappeared.  
  
"Granny Goddess of Mercy, do you have divine powers?" In the pitch-black alley, the little girl, pouting on the verge of tears, held Goddess of Mercy's hand as they walked forward.  
"Yes, I do." Under the clear moonlight, Goddess of Mercy smiled at her.  
"My divine power… can call the moon to my side."  
What night is tonight, that I may see this moon?  
Let the moonlight shine upon the beholder.
She had long possessed it.

Upon reaching Discipleship Level 7, further Master Points earned will be converted into Peach-Plum Blossoms. These blossoms can be used to upgrade the effects and counter levels of the "A Wanderer's Solitude" Hero Title and "Noble Spirit" Badge.

Xue Chou of Kaifeng, a man of mixed Hu and Han descent, was born with an unknown original name. In his youth, he apprenticed under Old Man Xue, mastering miraculous arts: treading on fire and blades, transplanting melons and wells, conjuring clouds and mists at will, and shaping mountains and rivers from thin air—feats that left onlookers in awe. Chou was renowned for his cunning. He assisted Ghostlight Market Elder and Dao Lord Zhu Yousheng in founding the Nine Mortal Ways to resist the Khitan forces, winning great prestige among the people for his strategic acumen.
After Zhu Yousheng's death and as his disciples came of age, Xue Chou retired to oversee the Oil Umbrella faction. He often performed illusionary acts in the Fairgrounds, gaining renown for his craft. When envoys from various states converged on the capital, the Emperor wished to stage a performance to showcase imperial might and entrusted the task to Chou.
If later generations of jianghu practitioners are destined to meet him, they may seek his trace at the Beast Reverie Stage in the Fairgrounds—perhaps they will find what they seek.

演武玩法中，最多可使用20支箭矢，治疗效果降低70%。进入战斗一段时间后，玩家伤害将获得提升且治疗效果将进一步下降。在#Y无治疗流派#E的对局中全队共获得一次复活机会。队友倒下15秒内，在其阵亡位置10米范围内可将其复活。被复活的队友将获得20%外功攻击提升，持续20秒。在#Y有治疗流派#E的对局中，武学明川药典感知技千金朝玉仅可使用1次，心法君臣药六重效果不受此限制。#Y小队面板上的复活次数显示未计入“君臣药”六重效果带来的额外次数#E。

场景机制：雪天战场处于极寒环境，#Y火属性伤害降低50%#E，影响神龙吐火、流星坠火、火箭。

玩家的技能大多都可以以卸势应对，破防奇术不仅不会被卸势，在命中处于防御或在释放卸势技能的目标时，反而有更好的效果，但其可以被任意技能打断。玩法中释放卸势会消耗耐力，而处决命中时会回复耐力。

玩家的各类技能（包括奇术和蓄力技）能够打断轻重击，而反过来则不行。解控技能清风霁月可在受击或控制状态下使用，活用可以有效扭转劣势。

移动端与PC端为独立的匹配池。组队参与玩法时，匹配逻辑遵循以下规则：系统将检测队伍内所有成员的设备类型。一旦检测到存在PC端设备，该队伍会被纳入PC端匹配队列。若玩家在移动端匹配成功后出现跨平台顶号等异常行为，则该玩家后续匹配被归入PC端队列。

在限定时间内，率先击败对方全部玩家的一方获胜，若倒计时结束未分胜负，按以下优先级依次判定：
1.存活玩家数量更多的一方获胜；
2.若存活玩家数量相同，则总伤害量更高一方获胜；
3.若总伤害量相同，则总治疗量更高一方获胜。
en:
3v3 Arena is a fair competitive mode where combat attributes are balanced. All character attributes are normalized. Gear sets and Arena Attunement effects are customizable. Mystic Skills are at Tier 6 Rank 20, and Inner Ways are at Tier 6. All general Arena Talents for the current season are unlocked. Food and Talisman effects are inactive.

Matching Rules: A team can have a maximum of 2 players using the same martial art and 1 player using healing martial arts.

In 3v3 Arena, a maximum of 20 arrows can be used, and healing effects are reduced by 70%. After a certain duration in combat, damage increases and healing further decreases. Teams #Ywithout a healer#E receive one revival attempt. Fallen teammates can be revived within 10m of their death location within 15s. Revived players gain a 20% Physical Attack bonus for 20s. In matches with #Yhealers#E, Panacea Fan's perception skill: Resurrection can only be used once. Tier 6 effect of Royal Remedy is not affected by this limit. #YResurrection counts on the team panel do not include extra counts from the Tier 6 Royal Remedy effect#E.

Scene Mechanism: Snowy battlefields are extremely cold. #YFire damage is reduced by 50%#E for Dragon's Breath, Flaming Meteor, and Flaming Arrow.

Most skills can be countered with Deflect. Defense-breaking Mystic Skills cannot be deflected and deal enhanced damage to targets using Defense or Deflect, but can be interrupted by any skill. Using Deflect costs Endurance, while landing an Execution restores it. Player skills (including Mystic and Charged) can interrupt Light/Heavy Attacks, but not vice versa. Use Break Control Skills like Serene Breeze to escape control effects.

Mobile and PC players queue separately. In team queue, if any member is using a PC, the entire team enters the PC matchmaking pool. Players showing abnormal cross-platform behavior (e.g., account takeover) on mobile will be moved to the PC queue.

Win by eliminating all opponents. If time expires, victory is decided by:
1. Surviving players
2. Total damage
3. Total healing.

zh:
少年终究还是离开了，带着很多很多捞月网。
纤阿女知道少年要去做什么。她明白，她的哥哥，心肠比水中的月亮更温柔，更纯粹。
但她也担心，担心自己看到的未来：那个温柔的哥哥最后会失去月华的祝福，在沙海中衰朽逝去。

于是纤阿女也启程了。她许诺，一定会把少年带回来。
她没有说出自己在月华里看到的画面。那是她心里的秘密。
她本就是带着奇迹出生的人。她是从残月逆向而生的人，最终将以新月的样子死去。
只是她不知道能不能超越奇迹，打破哥哥既定的命运。

她走着，念着。渴了，便掬一捧清泉，饿了，便捞一轮明月。
直到她的容颜越发年轻。
有时她也害怕，害怕自己也像哥哥那样，永远回不到月光深处。
但她没有停下自己的脚步。
她并非囿于儿女私情，亦知晓自己与众不同的宿命。
可如果月光宣告了世间众人的定数，又为何让自己得以一见？
既然得见，便去超越。
en:
The boy left in the end, taking many, many moon-catching nets with him. 
Xian'a knew what he intended to do. She understood her brother—his heart was gentler, purer than the moon in the water. 
But she was also afraid, haunted by the future she had seen: that gentle brother, stripped of the moon's blessing, withering and dying in the sea of sand. 

So, Xian'a set out as well. She vowed to bring the boy back. 
She did not speak of the visions she had seen in the moonlight. That was her secret. 
She was born from a miracle, born from a waning moon in reverse, destined to die as a new crescent. 
She just didn't know if she could surpass that miracle and break her brother's preordained fate. 

She walked, she chanted. When thirsty, she cupped a handful of clear spring water; when hungry, she scooped up a moon. 
Until her face grew younger still. 
Sometimes she, too, was afraid—afraid that like her brother, she might never return to the heart of the moonlight. 
But she did not stop. 
She was not bound by mere sentiment, and she knew her destiny was different from others. 
But if the moonlight proclaimed the fixed fate of all, why had she been allowed to see? 
Since she had seen, she would surpass it.

zh:
【说卦】

昔者圣人之作《易》也，幽赞于神明而生蓍，参天两地而倚数，观变于阴阳而立卦，发挥于刚柔而生爻，和顺于道德而理于义，穷理尽性，以至于命。

昔者圣人之作《易》也，将以顺性命之理。是以立天之道，曰阴与阳；立地之道，曰柔与刚；立人之道，曰仁与义。兼三才而两之，故易六画而成卦。分阴分阳，迭用柔刚，故易六位而成章。

天地定位，山泽通气，雷风相薄，水火不相射，八卦相错。数往者顺，知来者逆，是故易逆数也。

雷以动之，风以散之，雨以润之，日以烜之，艮以止之，兑以说之，乾以君之，坤以藏之。

帝出乎震，齐乎巽，相见乎离，致役乎坤，说言乎兑，战乎乾，劳乎坎，成言乎艮。万物出乎震，震，东方也。齐乎巽，巽，东南也。齐也者，言万物之絜齐也。离也者，明也。万物皆相见，南方之卦也。圣人南面而听天下，向明而治，盖耴诸此也。坤也者，地也。万物皆致养焉，故曰：致役乎坤。兑，正秋也，万物之所说也，故曰：说言乎兑。战乎乾。乾，西北之卦也，言阴阳相薄也。坎者，水也，正北方之卦也，劳卦也，万物之所归也，故曰：劳乎坎。艮，东北之卦也，万物之所成终而所成始也，故曰：成言乎艮。

神也者，妙万物而为言者也。动万物者莫疾乎风，燥万物者莫熯乎火，说万物者莫说乎泽，润万物者莫润乎水，终万物始万物者莫盛乎艮。故水火相逮，雷风不相悖，山泽通气，然后能变化，既成万物也。

乾，健也。坤，顺也。震，动也。巽，入也。坎，陷也。离，丽也。艮，止也。兑，说也。
乾为马。坤为牛。震为龙。巽为鸡。坎为豕。离为雉。艮为狗。兑为羊。
乾为首。坤为腹。震为足。巽为股。坎为耳。离为目。艮为手。兑为口。
……
en:
【Shuo Gua】

In ancient times, when the sages created the *Yi* (Book of Changes), they subtly assisted the spirits and deities, and thus the yarrow stalks came into being. They established the numbers by referencing Heaven and Earth in their proportions of three and two, observed changes in yin and yang to establish the hexagrams, and activated the firm and yielding to generate the lines. They harmonized with virtue and the Dao, and ordered things according to righteousness, exhausting principle and fully realizing nature, thereby reaching destiny.

In ancient times, when the sages created the *Yi*, it was to follow the principles of nature and destiny. Therefore, they established the Dao of Heaven, calling it yin and yang; the Dao of Earth, calling it yielding and firm; and the Dao of Humanity, calling it benevolence and righteousness. Combining the Three Powers and doubling them, thus the six lines of the *Yi* form a hexagram. Dividing into yin and yang, alternately using the yielding and firm, thus the six positions complete the pattern.

Heaven and Earth establish their positions, Mountain and Lake interpenetrate their vital forces, Thunder and Wind stir each other, Water and Fire do not oppose each other, and the Eight Trigrams interweave. Counting the past is forward, knowing the future is backward; therefore, the *Yi* counts backward.

Thunder moves them, Wind disperses them, Rain moistens them, the Day illuminates them, Gen stops them, Dui delights them, Qian rules them, and Kun stores them.

The Emperor emerges in Zhen, is aligned in Xun, appears in Li, labors in Kun, speaks joyfully in Dui, contends in Qian, toils in Kan, and completes in Gen. All things emerge in Zhen, for Zhen is the East. They are aligned in Xun, for Xun is the Southeast. "Aligned" speaks of the orderly arrangement of all things. Li is Light; all things become visible there, and it is the trigram of the South. The sage faces South to hear the world, governing toward the light—this is derived from this. Kun is Earth; all things are nourished there, hence it is said: "Labor in Kun." Dui is the height of Autumn, the delight of all things, hence it is said: "Speak joyfully in Dui." Contend in Qian—Qian is the trigram of the Northwest, speaking of the clash of yin and yang. Kan is Water, the trigram of the true North, the trigram of toil, where all things return, hence it is said: "Toil in Kan." Gen is the trigram of the Northeast, where all things reach their end and their beginning, hence it is said: "Complete in Gen."

The spirits are that which mysteriously accomplishes all things. Nothing moves all things faster than Wind, nothing dries all things more than Fire, nothing delights all things more than the Lake, nothing moistens all things more than Water, and nothing brings all things to their end and beginning more than Gen. Thus Water and Fire aid each other, Thunder and Wind do not oppose each other, and Mountain and Lake interpenetrate their vital forces—only then can transformation occur, completing all things.

Qian is strength. Kun is compliance. Zhen is movement. Xun is penetration. Kan is the pit. Li is attachment. Gen is stillness. Dui is joy.
Qian is the Horse. Kun is the Ox. Zhen is the Dragon. Xun is the Rooster. Kan is the Pig. Li is the Pheasant. Gen is the Dog. Dui is the Sheep.
Qian is the Head. Kun is the Belly. Zhen is the Foot. Xun is the Thigh. Kan is the Ear. Li is the Eye. Gen is the Hand. Dui is the Mouth.
……

Because Masseur has a unique secret technique: massaging, which no other cat or dog can do. Whenever the soldiers are exhausted, Masseur proactively pounces onto their shoulders or leans against their backs, using his paws to press on their sore spots. After every session, the soldiers' fatigue eases. Then, Masseur quickly jumps behind someone else to continue.
Massaging one after another, Masseur handles such small scenes with calm and ease.

zh:
天不收从没想过自己能养大两个孩子。
那可是，两个孩子啊孩子！
不是小花小草，不是小猫小狗，哪里是随便养养就可以的。
一旦决心养了就没有回头路，一辈子都要绑在一起。不仅要管吃喝拉撒、还要教本事、讲道理，教的不好还不行，万一成了为害乡里的恶霸……
所以一开始，天不收压根没想将这两个家伙收为徒弟。
但那个年纪小的男孩脸烂得不成样子，一直哭一直哭，女孩又抓着天不收衣角不放，眼睛水汪汪地看他。
……
算了算了。
“从今往后，你就叫窦豆豆，你就叫姚药药，听懂了吗？”

要说豆豆为什么叫豆豆，药药为什么叫药药，天不收是很有讲究的。
虽然乍一听像是个玩笑。
首先，豆豆总是一副很悲伤的样子，那便给他三个逗，日后定然笑哈哈。
再来，药药小时身体不好，那便多带点药，日子好过得平安顺遂。
这取名的法子虽土，但确实有用。豆豆和药药的确如他心愿那样长大了。
天不收虽不信佛，但每每念及此，都忍不住在心里谢一声阿弥陀佛。
药药再无病痛，长成了心里不装事儿、成天嘻嘻哈哈的样子。而豆豆也不再成天愁眉苦脸，有时也像个寻常孩子那样笑，还很有孝心，只是……
只是，太有孝心了。天不收叹息一声，小小的心里装了那么多事，要是能活得轻松一些就好了。

关于如何养孩子这事，天不收着实费了不少心思。
要说最头疼的，便是如何止小儿夜哭。
夜哭这种事，一个孩子已经很头疼了，不要说天不收家里还有两个。
两个一起，跟比赛似的，越哭越起劲，半宿不停歇。
每当此时，夜半人静，举目无助，住在不羡仙半山、远离人烟的天不收深切地体会到了，何谓高处不胜寒。

后来，天不收为了解决这事，甚至低下头去找那个讨厌的江无浪取经。
求问江大侠是如何哄孩子的？
江无浪似笑非笑。
我家的从不夜哭。
……
江无浪果然讨厌。
所幸，天不收后来经过无数的摸索，总算找到了一个法子。
那便是……讲笑话。
其实讲得不怎么样，常人听了完全笑不出来，只觉得冷得要命。
但每一次都能哄住药药和豆豆。
天不收很得意，而药药和豆豆，则会在他得意的时候互相对视一眼，然后继续默契地哈哈大笑。
en:
Unfated Tian never planned to raise two children.
Two children!
Not flowers or grass, not cats or dogs. You can't just half-heartedly raise kids.
Once you take them in, there's no turning back. You're tied together for life. You have to feed them, teach them skills, and drill morals into them. And if you do a bad job? Well, what if they grow up to be neighborhood tyrants?
So at first, Unfated Tian had no intention of taking these two in as disciples.
But the younger boy's face was a ruined mess, tears streaming endlessly, while the girl clung to Unfated Tian's sleeve, her eyes wide and pleading....
Fine, fine.
"From now on, you're Doudou, and you're Yao Yaoyao. Understood?"

As for why "Doudou" and "Yaoyao"? Unfated Tian put serious thought into it. Even if it sounded like a joke.
First, Doudou always looked so sorrowful. So he gave him three "dous" (to tease), ensuring he'd grow up laughing.
Second, Yaoyao was sickly as a child. So he loaded her name with "yao" (medicine), hoping she'd stay healthy.
Corny? Maybe. But it worked. Against all odds, Doudou and Yaoyao grew up just as he'd wished.
Unfated Tian wasn't a Buddhist, but whenever he thought about it, he couldn't help muttering a silent Amitabha.
Yaoyao shed her ailments, becoming a carefree girl who laughed at everything. Doudou, too, stopped moping like a little rain cloud. He even smiled sometimes, a proper, childlike grin, and was fiercely filial. Yet...Too filial, Unfated Tian sighed. That tiny heart carried too much weight. If only he'd learn to live lightly.

Unfated Tian poured his soul into figuring child-rearing out.
The worst challenge? Stopping nighttime crying.
One wailing child is bad enough. Unfated Tian had two in one house.
And they'd compete. One would start, the other would escalate, a duet of misery lasting half the night.
In those moments, alone on his remote mountain in Blissful Retreat, far from human noise, Unfated Tian truly understood the phrase: "It's lonely at the top."

Desperate, he even swallowed his pride to ask that insufferable Jiang Wulang for advice.
Great Hero Jiang, how do you soothe a child at night?
Jiang Wulang smirked.
Mine never cries....Jiang Wulang is the worst.
Luckily, through trial and error, Unfated Tian discovered a solution:
Telling jokes. Terrible jokes. 
The kind that'd make normal people shiver from sheer awkwardness.
But without fail, they silenced Yaoyao and Doudou.
Unfated Tian preened at his genius. Meanwhile, the kids would exchange a glance and burst into exaggerated laughter, playing along every time.
I suppose...
Zheng Tianchen

“这会儿赶着上滹沱河去，两位大人可是那军中的贵人？我只听闻那将军帐里，总坐着几位了不得的幕僚，出谋划策平定天下。二位可也是那厉害的人？只消动动手指，往那舆图上一点，咱这些百姓的好日子就来了。”
——言多易失，知多……易死。
“瞧我这多嘴的毛病……晓得，晓得，我不问了。”
“我就是心里憋着团雾，想求高人指点指点：这天下一趟趟地乱，仗一场场地打，究竟图个什么呢？”
“打赢了，三两天又换个皇帝。打输了，白搭进去好多人命。反反复复，来回折腾，又能有什么结果？”
——此战，不在输赢。

不在输赢，而在破局。战有胜败，朝有更替……唯有先破，方能后立。
en:
"Rushing to the Hutuo River at this hour... are you two lords important figures in the army? I have heard that great advisors sit in the General's tent, planning to stabilize the realm. Are you two just as skilled? Just a flick of a finger on a map, and a good life comes to us commoners."
"Too many words invite loss. Too much knowledge... invites death."
"Look at my big mouth... I understand, I won't ask."
"I just have a mystery in my heart and want a master to guide me: the world turns to chaos time and again, and battle after battle is fought. What is it all for?"
"If you win, the Emperor changes in a few days. If you lose, so many lives are wasted for nothing. Over and over, back and forth... what is the point?"
"This battle is not about winning or losing."

Not about winning or losing, but about breaking the deadlock. Dynasties change and battles are won or lost... but only through destruction can something new be built.

zh:
小友见谅，本该早点与你通书信，只是我这两日昏睡不醒，眼下神思稍清，才能提笔。唉，此事说来实在惭愧……
前几日晓晓嫌饭菜腻味，不肯好好吃饭，我便想着寻些新鲜食材来换换口味，于是一时兴起，提着菜篮往山野间去了。
走到一处峭壁时，忽见一株异草，叶泛淡金，籽若珠玉，还散发着阵阵清香。我一心以为此物可以入馔，便摘取少许尝了尝，谁料顷刻间天旋地转，再睁眼，我已身在缥缈浮云之上了。
更奇的是，墨子竟站在我眼前，同我说起他周游列国时所尝百味——楚椒之辛、齐盐之醇、宋菘之甘……言谈间我与他好似故交，恍然未觉光阴飞逝。
直到晓晓哭着把我叫醒，我才知道自己已经足足昏睡两日。害她忧心奔走，是我这个做父亲的太不尽职了。
可是小友，此番虽然凶险，朴某却得以在梦中与先贤坐而论味，这算不算是……因祸得福呢？
en:
Forgive me, my young friend. I should have written sooner, but I have been in a deep slumber these past two days. My mind has only just cleared enough to write. Honestly, the matter is truly shameful to admit...
A few days ago, Xiaoxiao complained that the food was too heavy. Hoping to find some fresh ingredients to change her palate, I headed into the wilderness with a basket on a whim.
Near a steep cliff, I chanced upon a strange herb. Its leaves had a faint golden sheen, its seeds resembled pearls and jade, and it wafted a clear fragrance. Mistaking it for an edible ingredient, I picked a little to taste. To my surprise, the world immediately spun around me, and when I opened my eyes next, I was standing amidst ethereal clouds.
Even more bizarrely, Mozi himself stood in front of me, speaking of the myriad flavors he had tasted while wandering the states: the sharp heat of Chu pepper, the mellow richness of Qi salt, the sweetness of Song greens... We talked as if we were old friends, entirely oblivious to the fleeting passage of time.
It wasn't until Xiaoxiao woke me up in tears that I realized I had been unconscious for two full days. Causing her such frantic worry was deeply irresponsible of me as her father.
Still, my young friend, dangerous as it was, I did get the chance to sit and talk about culinary delights with one of the great sages of old. Would you call that... a blessing in disguise?

zh:

它喜欢谁，就舔谁。于是八哥的羽毛经常湿漉漉的。

八哥的主人是个铜头怪人，谷里叮叮当当的音乐声，听说就是铜头怪人搞出来的。
小七也喜欢他，毕竟从名字来看，小七、小八，应该是一窝的。

那天，小七正专心致志地给八哥鸟“洗头”，铜头怪人恰好进门。
八哥鸟的半个身子，已经消失在了狗嘴里，小八吓得头差点都掉在地上，大喊一声：“松口！”

小七被这声吓了一跳，嘴一张，八哥鸟就扑腾着飞了出来，稳稳落在了小七头顶。
它歪着脑袋，学着怪人的腔调，清脆地叫了一声：“松口！”

小八愣了一下，然后哈哈大笑。

小七不懂他为什么一惊一乍。它只是摇着尾巴，听着谷里传来的叮当声，蹭了蹭怪人的裤腿，又抬头看了看头顶上的鸟。真好，喜欢的都在身边。
en:
Seven's favorite thing isn't a bone; it's a mynah bird.
Whoever he likes, he licks. So the mynah's feathers are often damp.

The mynah's owner is a copper-headed eccentric. The ding-ding-dang-dang music echoing in the valley is, it's said, made by this Copper-Head Man.
Seven likes him, too. After all, judging by the names, Seven and Xiaoba, they should be from the same litter.

That day, Seven was intently giving the mynah bird a "head wash" when the Copper-Head man happened to walk in.
Half of the mynah bird's body had already disappeared into the dog's mouth. Xiaoba (the man) was so scared his head nearly fell off. He shouted, "Let go!"

Startled by the shout, Seven's mouth opened, and the mynah bird fluttered out, landing steadily on top of Seven's head.
It tilted its head, imitating the man's tone, and chirped crisply: "Let go!"

Xiaoba was stunned for a second, then burst into laughter.

前些时日，老朽随府尹大人巡查蒙学，见学堂里的娃娃们一个个正襟危坐，埋首书卷，连我等走近了都未曾察觉。
老朽心下好奇，是何等妙文，能让这些上蹿下跳的娃娃们如此专心？一问才知，他们手中所读，竟是你前些时日所赠。
老朽又问，这些书好在何处？娃娃们七嘴八舌，老朽这才知道，原来你竟为每个孩子都择了不同的书，实在是费心了。而听闻老朽与你相熟，他们都央着我，定要代他们向你道声谢。
只是，真要问他们想说什么，这群小家伙却面露羞赧，讷讷而止了。最后，老朽想了个法子，让他们把想说的话都诉诸笔端，一并封在信里了。至于写了什么，老朽绝未偷看！
对了，娃娃们还托我转交几幅画作，说是读了书卷后的有感而发。他们都说，游侠你是他们见过最有眼光的人，定能欣赏他们的大作。
哈哈，看来往后若再有与孩子们打交道的差事，找游侠准是没错了。
<IMAGE id='im1' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/68ce3ebf0344181869c1ddfaaJT4M6ZM06' size='1896*1336' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
<IMAGE id='im2' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/68ce3eea1bc13e1c8515e545p8TiViY906' size='1500*2211' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
en:
Dear Wanderer,

The other day, I accompanied the Prefect on an inspection of the village school. The children sat straight at their desks, noses buried in scrolls, so absorbed they didn't even notice us draw near.
Curious what could hold their attention so completely, I asked. Turns out, they were reading the very books you gifted them not long ago.
I inquired further: what made these books so special? The little ones burst into chatter, and that's when I learned you had chosen a different book for each child. What thoughtfulness.
When they heard I knew you, they begged me to pass along their thanks.
But when I asked what they wanted to say, shyness took over, and words failed them. So I suggested they write it down instead. Their letters are enclosed. And no, I did not peek!
Oh, and they also asked me to send you a few drawings. Inspired, they said, by your books. They all agreed you're the most discerning person they've ever met, and that you'd surely appreciate their masterpieces.
Seems to me, whenever there's a task involving children, you're the one to call.
