zh:
马二第一次来到天街上是个夜晚，天上下着大雨。
山上风大，雨脚倾斜，就算打了伞，背包和衣裳也全都湿透了。
他推开了一间小酒馆的门。年轻的贾老板被闯入屋内的雨汽吓了一跳。
“喝啥？”没见过这么晚爬山上来的，贾老板停下收拾的手。
“妹子，随便给俺来一碗酒就行，再端几个酒肴，要热乎的。”马二局促地擦了擦手上的水，又退回门外，把布鞋在石头上蹭了又蹭。
“坐吧。没事，还没收拾呢。”
三碗黄汤下肚，马二畅然地舒了口气。
“俺打听下妹子，东边，最东边有个村子靠海……咋样现在？“马二的语气突然有些怯生生。
“乐安浦？挺好的地方，俺们店的小曼儿还上那块吃饭了前几天。”贾老板又给他添了一碗酒。“咋个，你也嫌俺店里这酒肴不合胃口？非要吃那边的菜？”
“不是，不是，俺是青州人，从外面回来咧！”马二的喉头泛起了酒气，就连眼睛也蒸腾。
“俺叫马二，以前就是……现在叫啥？乐安浦？是那儿的人！那几年发大水，俺阿翁带着俺逃难咧。”马二顿了顿。“阿爷阿娘叫大水冲走了，俺阿翁带着俺，在外面做饭店生意，前几天也走了。俺说，要带着阿翁回家看看。”
“俺还记得，从前村口有一大片一大片的盐田，俺时常去撒丫子玩。还在水边抓螃蟹……”
“退潮了那礁石缝里头都是鱼啊虾啊，还有会跳的泥猴儿鱼咧！俺阿翁说，那种鱼以后会变成龙，飞到海里头去！”
这个打开话匣满脸幸福的汉子，此刻仿佛又变成了海边的少年。
“妹子，结账。今晚俺就动身下山，明天晌午头就能到……”
“都是老乡，客气啥。这顿俺请了。以后常来。”贾老板笑了笑。
“马二哥，欢迎回家。”
马二的脸红扑扑的，酒意乡情让他的血脉升温。
他应了一声，撑开伞，向山下跑去。
记忆里那盐花璀璨的小渔村，正逐渐在雨幕中清晰。
马二跑起来，如同小时候，迎着黄昏，奔向家门。
en:
The night Ma Er first arrived at Cloudwalk Street, the rain was coming down in sheets.
Up on the mountain, the fierce wind drove the rain sideways, blowing so hard that an umbrella was useless. His clothes and pack were drenched.
He pushed open the door to a small tavern. The sudden, violent gust of stormy air startled the young Boss Jia.
"What can I get you?" she asked, pausing her sweeping. She hadn't expected anyone to brave the mountain path this late.
"Just a bowl of wine, sister, whatever you have. And a few hot dishes, if you don't mind." Suddenly self-conscious, Ma Er hastily wiped his dripping hands and stepped back outside to scrape the mud from his cloth shoes against the stone step.
"Come on in. Sit down. Don't worry about it. I haven't cleaned up yet anyway."
Three bowls of yellow wine later, Ma Er let out a long, contented sigh.
"Let me ask you something, sister," he began, his voice dropping to a shy timbre. "Out east... the furthest east along the coast, there's a village. How is it doing these days?"
"Tranquil Pier? It's a lovely place. My helper, Lass, was just down there on an errand a few days ago." She poured him another bowl. "Why? Are my bar snacks not hitting the spot? Craving the food down there?"
"No, no, it's not that. I'm actually from Qingzhou, just making my way back." The alcohol caught in his throat, and a sudden heat brought tears to his eyes.
"My name is Ma Er. I used to live in... what did you call it? Tranquil Pier? That's where I'm from. Years ago, there was a terrible flood, and my grandpa took me away to escape it." He paused, swallowing hard. "The flood took my parents. Grandpa and I survived by running a small eatery in another town, but he passed away a few days ago. I told him I'd bring him back home to see it one last time."
"I still remember the sprawling salt flats right at the edge of the village. I used to run wild out there barefoot, catching crabs by the water..."
"When the tide went out, the rocks were teeming with fish and shrimp, and those little mudskippers that hop across the sand! My grandpa used to tell me that one day, those mudskippers would turn into dragons and soar into the deep sea!"
As the rugged man poured out his memories, his face glowed with a profound joy. For a fleeting moment, he was no longer a weary traveler, but that carefree boy by the sea.
"Sister, let me settle the bill. I'm heading down the mountain tonight. I should make it there by noon tomorrow."
"We're from the same hometown. There's no need for that. This one's on me. Just come back and visit sometime." Jia offered a gentle smile.
"Welcome home, Brother Ma Er."
Ma Er's face flushed, his blood warmed as much by the wine as by the fierce, sudden rush of belonging.
He called out a rough thanks, snapped his umbrella open, and began the descent into the storm.
Through the heavy curtain of rain, the memory of that little fishing village with its glittering sea salt bloomed bright and clear in his mind.
Ma Er ran, just as he had as a boy, chasing the twilight, sprinting all the way home.

zh:
什么财神，原也是人。
原也是街坊四邻交口称赞的本分商贩，本着姓名里一个“真”字起早贪黑讨生活，可惜向来只知劝自己知足，却不知高门的大人们永不知餍足。
未央城倾轧，史真一朝失去所有，在尘土里几经生死，史真才明白了许多“早该明白”的道理——
你不赚钱，自有人要赚，你欲人活，人却只欲你死。
未央城的一块玉玦，使得史真拥有了从头再来的机会，他改“真”为“鸩”，从此成为温无痕手中的一招狠棋。逐温无缺出城后，他以为自己能成为未央城的上宾，可温无痕的眼里，纵使是浑身镀金，他也不过是一只招人厌倦的蟾蜍。
凭什么温家人天生是财神？我偏不信。
凭着这句话和未央城的独门武学，他最终得到了江湖上最为神秘的那位“楼主”的青睐。
从此以后，他不再是江南史真，也不再是未央城史鸩，他是开封府的史大人，是绣金楼的玄林掌司，更是……万人拥戴、万人恐惧的——黑财神。
en:
What god of wealth? He is just a man.
Once, he was a vendor. Living up to his first name "Zhen", he was honest and humble, praised by every neighbor. He rose early, worked late, and taught himself to be content, but he'd never known that those in high places were never content.
When the cruel competition began in Weiyang City, Shi Zhen lost everything overnight. Dragged through dust and death, he came to understand what he should've known all along:
If you don't make money, someone else will. If you wish others well, they may still wish you dead.
A jade pendant from Weiyang gave him a second chance. The name was still "Zhen", but the meaning had soured, and virtue curdled into malice. From that day, he became a ruthless piece in Wen Wuhen's game. After casting Wen Wuque out of the city, he thought he earned his place among the powerful. But in Wen's eyes, even covered in gold, he was nothing more than a toad—gaudy, repulsive, disposable.
Who decided that the Wen family was to be a god of wealth by birthright? He spat on the very idea.
Fueled by that defiance and armed with Weiyang's secret martial arts, he finally caught the eye of the most elusive figure in the martial world.
From that moment on, he was no longer Shi Zhen of Jiangnan. No longer Shi Zhen of Weiyang. He is now Lord Shi of Kaifeng Prefecture. He is the Aureate Pavilion's Grand Steward. Above all... he is the God of Avarice, feared by thousands, and worshipped by more.

zh:
张阿满从小就手抖。
他拿不住爹娘给的银钱，拿不住朋友给的蜜饯。只要往他手里一塞，准咕噜噜地掉下来。
旁边的人就乐，张阿满也跟着乐。
当见到那个女子的时候，他不乐了。张阿满第一次痛恨自己这个毛病。
张阿满递出花束，花朵哗啦啦撒了一地；给她带去的糖饼，连着瓷碗摔在地上。晶莹的糖霜沾到她的裙摆，羞得张阿满手抖得停不下来。
女子也乐，咯咯笑着掏出一个小针盒。纤纤玉手拿出几根针，又让张阿满闭了眼。
那针轻轻扎进张阿满的手，他却不觉疼痛。针尖刺得他酥酥麻麻的，一路酥进心里。
针拔了出来，女子身上的香气也离了张阿满三步之外。
他好似做了场幻梦。梦醒来了，他的手也好了。
en:
Zhang A'man's hands had always trembled.
As a child, he couldn't hold the coins his parents gave him, nor catch the candied treats his friends tossed his way. Anything placed in his palm would inevitably slip free and roll across the ground.
People laughed. Zhang A'man laughed with them.
Then he met her, and the laughter stopped. For the first time, he loathed his affliction.
The bouquet he offered fell apart at her feet. The sugar cakes he carried shattered along with the bowl. Crystals of white glaze splashed onto the hem of her skirt, and shame sent his trembling completely out of control.
She laughed instead. With a soft chuckle, she took out a small needle case. With slender, jade-like fingers, she drew a few silver needles and told him to close his eyes.
The needle tips pricked his hand, light, painless. A tingling warmth spread from his fingertips, all the way into his chest.
When the needles were gone, she had already stepped back, her faint fragrance lingering in the air.
It felt like a dream. When he woke, his hands were steady.
So this is your flower boat, miss?

大侠近来可好？写这封信，是想给你报个喜。多亏你先前帮忙，我才有了支起摊子的本钱，在开封南郊的麦香集里寻了个落脚处。当初从家里出来时，哪敢想有今日……

不过今年老家的天儿有些邪乎……又是旱又是涝的没断过，八成会影响收成……希望地里可千万争气点。
<IMAGE id='im1' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/6937d9ff99a801cef19883d1aMopacRH07' size='1810*2704' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
en:
Dear Wanderer,

How are you? I write with glad tidings. Thanks to your help, I've set up my stall at the Wheatwind Bazaar in Kaifeng Suburbs-South. When I left home, I never dreamed such a day…
Grandfather always said gratitude must be more than words. So I've sent my savings back to Fuping, my hometown, to lease five mu of persimmon groves in your name. Grandfather and the villagers tend them. He insisted on having the old painter paint them for you. I can already imagine the fiery red blaze!
But the weather's been cruel this year, drought and flood by turns. The harvest would likely suffer… May the land prove worthy.

zh:
鬼樊楼的姑娘们常说，这楼里啊，有个吃人的屋子。活的人走着进去，出来时却只剩尸骨。
所以姑娘们战战兢兢，日夜都照着主事的吩咐做事。她们从不去想，不去谈，更无力关心，里边到底有什么。
只有个送饭的小厮知道。那暗房里啊，其实关了个姑娘。

那姑娘衣衫褴褛，容颜半毁，失了神志。所有闯入她视线的人，都会被她斩于刀下。
但还有些时候，那姑娘会陷入长久的沉默。然后她开始哼唱歌谣。那歌声断断续续，如泣如诉。
像是暗夜里摇摇欲坠的花朵。风吹过，雨打过。根茎已毁，叶脉已断，但那盛开的花蕊里，还藏着一点点的红。
让人听了，忍不住生出怜悯。

但也止步于怜悯。
人要活下去，就只能忽视、忘却，那些被吃掉的人。
en:
The girls of Ghost Revelry Hall often whispered about the "devouring room" hidden within its walls, a place where the living walked in, and only bones came out.
So they obeyed the overseers with trembling diligence, never daring to wonder, speak of, or question what lay inside.
Only a young pageboy knows the truth: the dark chamber holds a girl.

She is tattered, half-scarred, and deranged. Anyone who meets her gaze falls to her blade.
Yet in rare moments, the girl would lapse into silence, then begin humming a fractured lullaby. The melody came in gasps and whispers, a wounded sound that hung in the air like blood in water.
Like a flower trembling in the dead of night, battered by wind, broken by rain, its roots rotted and veins severed... yet deep within its crumbling petals, a stubborn crimson still clings.
It made listeners ache with pity.

But pity changed nothing.
To survive here, one learned to turn away. To forget the devoured.
B-Beautiful... my beauty, I'm home...

zh: 回家后，杜巧兰便和毛乙商量着，给天佑请个厉害些的下棋师傅。毛乙找到了刘爷爷。但刘爷爷称，他们这些老头子，早已经不是天佑的对手，要真想栽培天佑，还得去找城里有名的棋手。杜巧兰便又巴巴的跑去城里，但城里的著名棋手打量了一圈毛天佑，摇了摇头。他称天外有天，毛天佑确有天赋，但没受过正经的训练，又过了最佳的启蒙年纪，他不收。若非要学嘛，也不是不行，但是这价钱嘛……夫妻俩愁坏了，整日里唉声叹气，直怪自己没本事，连累了儿子。天佑见父母愁苦，思考了半天后同他们二人说，自己有法子了。他求着父亲给自己做了张棋桌，就摆在家门口的大街上。他跟爹娘说，每一个过路人，都可以是他的师傅。每个人教他一招，十个人便能教会他十招。等他学会了一百招，他再去城里找师傅。兴许那时候，师傅看在他努力又上进的份上，就收了他呢。
en: Back home, Du Qiaolan discussed the matter with Mao Yi—they had to find a proper chess teacher for Tianyou. Mao Yi turned to Elderly Liu, hoping the old man could take the boy under his wing. But Elderly Liu simply shook his head with a smile. "He's already beyond what we old men can offer," he said. "If you truly want to nurture him, you'll need someone from the city—a real master." With hope rekindled, Du Qiaolan made her way to the city, asking around for reputable chess players. However, when one of the renowned chess players examined Mao Tianyou, he shook his head and declined. He confirmed Tianyou's talent, but chess is a deep rabbit hole—there's always someone better out there. Without formal training, and starting this late, the road will be hard. Not impossible, but difficult and the cost will be high. The couple was devastated, sighing night after night and blaming themselves for not being wealthy enough to give their son the opportunity he deserved. Tianyou saw it all. After thinking quietly for some time, he came to them with a plan: he asked his father to make him a humble chess table and set it up just outside their front door, right in the middle of the street. "Everyone who passes by could be my teacher," he said. "If each one teaches me a single strategy, then after learning a hundred strategies, I'll go back to the city. Maybe then, a master will see how hard I've worked and be willing to teach me."

【祭统第二十五】

凡治人之道，莫急于礼。礼有五经，莫重于祭。夫祭者，非物自外至者也，自中出生于心也；心怵而奉之以礼。是故，唯贤者能尽祭之义。贤者之祭也，必受其福。非世所谓福也。福者，备也；备者，百顺之名也。无所不顺者，谓之备。言：内尽于己，而外顺于道也。忠臣以事其君，孝子以事其亲，其本一也。上则顺于鬼神，外则顺于君长，内则以孝于亲。如此之谓备。唯贤者能备，能备然后能祭。是故，贤者之祭也：致其诚信与其忠敬，奉之以物，道之以礼，安之以乐，参之以时。明荐之而已矣。不求其为。此孝子之心也。祭者，所以追养继孝也。孝者畜也。顺于道不逆于伦，是之谓畜。是故，孝子之事亲也，有三道焉：生则养，没则丧，丧毕则祭。养则观其顺也，丧则观其哀也，祭则观其敬而时也。尽此三道者，孝子之行也。既内自尽，又外求助，昏礼是也。故国君取夫人之辞曰：“请君之玉女与寡人共有敝邑，事宗庙社稷。”此求助之本也。夫祭也者，必夫妇亲之，所以备外内之官也；官备则具备。水草之菹，陆产之醢，小物备矣；三牲之俎，八簋之实，美物备矣；昆虫之异，草木之实，阴阳之物备矣。凡天之所生，地之所长，茍可荐者，莫不咸在，示尽物也。外则尽物，内则尽志，此祭之心也。是故，天子亲耕于南郊，以共齐盛；王后蚕于北郊，以共纯服。诸侯耕于东郊，亦以共齐盛；夫人蚕于北郊，以共冕服。天子诸侯非莫耕也，王后夫人非莫蚕也，身致其诚信，诚信之谓尽，尽之谓敬，敬尽然后可以事神明，此祭之道也。及时将祭，君子乃齐。齐之为言齐也。齐不齐以致齐者也。是以君子非有大事也，非有恭敬也，则不齐。不齐则于物无防也，嗜欲无止也。及其将齐也，防其邪物，讫其嗜欲，耳不听乐。故记曰：“齐者不乐”，言不敢散其志也。心不茍虑，必依于道；手足不茍动，必依于礼。是故君子之齐也，专致其精明之德也。故散齐七日以定之，致齐三日以齐之。定之之谓齐。齐者精明之至也，然后可以交于神明也。是故，先期旬有一日，宫宰宿夫人，夫人亦散齐七日，致齐三日。君致齐于外，夫人致齐于内，然后会于大庙。君纯冕立于阼，夫人副袆立于东房。君执圭瓒祼尸，大宗执璋瓒亚祼。及迎牲，君执纼，卿大夫从士执刍。宗妇执盎从夫人荐涚水。君执鸾刀羞哜，夫人荐豆，此之谓夫妇亲之。
……
en:
【Sacrificial System, Chapter 25】

Of all methods for governing people, none is more urgent than ritual. Among the five categories of ritual, none is more important than sacrifice. Sacrifice is not something that comes from outside; it originates from within the heart. When the heart is moved, it is expressed through ritual. Therefore, only the worthy can fully realize the meaning of sacrifice. When the worthy offer sacrifice, they surely receive blessings—but not what the world commonly calls blessings. Blessing means completeness; completeness means being in accord with all things. To be without anything that is not in accord is called completeness. This means: inwardly, one exhausts oneself; outwardly, one follows the Dao. A loyal minister serves his ruler, a filial son serves his parents—the foundation is the same. Above, one accords with ghosts and spirits; outwardly, one accords with rulers and elders; inwardly, one is filial to one's parents. This is what is called completeness. Only the worthy can achieve completeness, and only after achieving completeness can they offer sacrifice. Therefore, when the worthy offer sacrifice: they bring forth their sincerity and their loyalty and reverence, they present offerings with things, they guide with ritual, they soothe with music, they coordinate with the seasons. They present their offerings clearly and purely, without seeking any return. This is the heart of a filial son. Sacrifice is the means by which one continues the nourishment and extends the filial piety of the past. Filial piety is accumulation. To accord with the Dao and not go against proper relationships—this is called accumulation. Therefore, a filial son's service to his parents has three ways: while they live, he nourishes them; when they die, he mourns them; after mourning, he sacrifices to them. Nourishment is observed through obedience, mourning through grief, and sacrifice through reverence and timeliness. To fulfill these three ways completely is the conduct of a filial son. Having inwardly exhausted oneself, one also seeks help from outside—this is the marriage rite. Thus, when a ruler takes a wife, his words are: "Please, may your Jade Lady share with me my humble state, to serve the ancestral temple and the altars of state." This is the foundation of seeking help. As for sacrifice, it must be personally conducted by husband and wife, so as to complete the offices of both inner and outer; when the offices are complete, the offerings are complete. Pickled vegetables from water plants, sauces from land products—the small items are all provided; the three animals on the stands, the contents of the eight vessels—the fine items are all provided; the unusual insects, the fruits of plants and trees, the products of yin and yang—all are provided. Whatever Heaven produces and Earth nourishes, if it can be offered, is all present, showing the exhaustion of things. Outwardly, one exhausts things; inwardly, one exhausts one's will—this is the heart of sacrifice. Therefore, the Emperor personally plows in the southern suburb to supply the grain for offerings; the Queen raises silkworms in the northern suburb to supply the pure garments. The feudal lords plow in the eastern suburb, also to supply the grain for offerings; their Ladies raise silkworms in the northern suburb to supply the ceremonial robes. It is not that the Emperor and lords cannot plow themselves, nor that the Queen and Ladies cannot raise silkworms themselves—they personally manifest their sincerity and trustworthiness. Sincerity and trustworthiness are called exhaustion; exhaustion is called reverence. Only after reverence and exhaustion can one serve the spirits and deities—this is the way of sacrifice. When the time for sacrifice approaches, the ruler undergoes purification. Purification means alignment. One aligns what is not aligned in order to achieve alignment. Therefore, the ruler does not undergo purification except for great affairs or matters of reverence. Without purification, there is no guarding against things, and desires are not restrained. But when about to purify, one guards against deviant things, restrains desires, and does not listen to music. Thus the records say: "One who purifies does not enjoy music," meaning one dares not scatter one's will. The mind does not casually deliberate but must rely on the Dao; the hands and feet do not casually move but must rely on ritual. Therefore, when the ruler purifies, he concentrates on achieving his quality of clarity and refinement. Thus, he disperses and purifies for seven days to settle himself, and concentrates and purifies for three days to align himself. Settling oneself is called purification. Purification is the utmost clarity and refinement, and only then can one commune with the spirits and deities. Therefore, eleven days before the sacrifice, the palace steward prepares the Lady, and the Lady also disperses and purifies for seven days and concentrates and purifies for three days. The ruler purifies outside, the Lady purifies inside, and then they meet in the Grand Ancestral Temple. The ruler, in pure ceremonial cap, stands at the eastern steps; the Lady, in her adorned robe and headdress, stands in the eastern chamber. The ruler holds the jade ladle and pours the libation for the personator; the Grand Officer holds the jade ladle and performs the second libation. When welcoming the victim, the ruler holds the rope, the ministers and officers follow, and the officers hold the fodder. The clan women hold the vessels and follow the Lady as she presents the clear water. The ruler holds the bell-knife and presents the roasted meat, and the Lady presents the dishes of offerings—this is what is meant by husband and wife personally conducting the sacrifice.
……

zh:
悬泉驿书库最后一阶的烛火刚刚熄灭。洪钰短暂地适应了一下黑暗，随即掏出火折子，点燃了手里的灯笼。映入眼帘的，是藏于四面壁龛内的简牍。汉隶清晰，韦编未散。
这是自汉武扬鞭时就留下的竹简，是悬泉驿还叫“悬泉置”之时就留下的记录。洪钰摩挲过累累案牍，选中一卷，轻轻展开捆扎的绢带。
“甘露二年二月庚申朔丙戌，鱼离置啬夫禹移县泉置，遣佐光持传马十匹，为冯夫人柱，廪穬麦小卅二石七斗，又茭廿五石二钧。”
冯夫人？那是西汉时解忧公主的侍女，游走于乌孙与大汉之间的奇女子。洪钰读过汉书，知晓这位女子的胆色。她也来过悬泉驿？
不知从哪儿出来一阵风，扬起案牍上的尘沙。灯笼昏黄的灯光映在尘幕上，洪钰迷了眼，似乎看到了一位乌发长裾的女子行行复止，在悬泉置的客房内轻轻叹了一口气。
眼前昏黄的灯光晕染了四壁。洪钰发现自己竟站在今天刚打扫出来的客房中。周围的侍者垂首以待，角落里的博山炉熏着名贵的百和香。塌上，侍女递过支蹱，冯夫人缓缓坐下。还没等洪钰反应过来，身边的侍者便推了推洪钰。
“驿马弃道，吏逐不及……啬夫钰，何事？”冯夫人的声音虽如沉水，但仍有藏不住的焦急。
洪钰正要开口，身边的一切却仿佛蒙上一层纱。随即纱帐层层卷来，拂过洪钰的鼻尖，酥酥痒痒，让他忍不住皱起鼻子，打了个喷嚏。
忽然，洪钰睁开眼。他正站在悬泉驿书库最后一阶。手中的灯笼还没燃尽。映入眼帘的，是藏于四面壁龛内的简牍。
en:
The candle on the lowest step of the Celestial Spring Station library had just gone out. Hong Yu briefly adjusted to the darkness, then took out a tinderbox and lit the lantern in his hand. What met his eyes were the bamboo slips stored in niches on all four walls. Han-dynasty clerical script was clear, the leather cords still intact. 
These were bamboo slips left since Emperor Wu of Han waved his whip to expand the empire, records from when Celestial Spring Station was still called Celestial Spring Post. Hong Yu brushed his hand over the stacked documents, picked one roll, and gently untied the silk ribbon binding it. 
"Between the first day and the twenty‑ninth day of the second month in the second year of the Ganlu era, Yu, the stationmaster of Yuli Post, transferred a document to Xianquan Post, dispatching his assistant Guang with ten relay horses to support Madam Feng's carriage. He also allocated supplies: a total of 32.7 dan of hulled barley and 25 dan 2 jun of hay." 
Madam Feng? That was the maid of Princess Jieyou during the Western Han, an extraordinary woman who moved between the Wusun and the Great Han. Hong Yu had read the Book of Han and knew of this woman's courage. Had she also come to Celestial Spring Station? 
A gust of wind came from nowhere, stirring the dust on the documents. The lantern's dim light reflected on the dusty veil. Hong Yu's vision blurred, and he seemed to see a woman with dark hair and long skirt walking, then pausing, letting out a soft sigh in a guest room of Celestial Spring Post. 
The dim light before his eyes suffused the walls. Hong Yu found himself standing in the very guest room that had just been cleaned today. Attendants stood around with bowed heads. In the corner, a Boshan censer wafted precious blended incense. On the couch, a maid offered a footrest, and Madam Feng slowly sat down. Before Hong Yu could react, an attendant beside him nudged he. 
"The post horses strayed off the road, and the officials couldn't catch up... Administrator Yu, what is the matter?" Madam Feng's voice, though calm as still water, held an unmasked urgency. 
Just as Hong Yu was about to speak, everything around his seemed veiled in gauze. Then the gauze layers rolled in, brushing the tip of his nose, tickling and making him wrinkle his nose and sneeze. 
Suddenly, Hong Yu opened his eyes. He was standing on the lowest step of the Celestial Spring Station library. The lantern in his hand was not yet burnt out. What met his eyes were the bamboo slips stored in niches on all four walls.
Hey, can you teach me this?

但我们知道自己有太多不够成熟的地方：第一次面对全球玩家，对不同玩家喜好了解还不够深入……
我们就像初入江湖的新客，唯有对武侠开放世界的热爱。一腔热血，惴惴不安。
但万分幸运的是，你们回应了我们的声音。我们终于有幸得以与各位在风中相遇。
自游戏上线以来，我们一直密切关注着各位游侠的反馈和建议，并不断修复体验不佳之处。当然，还有诸多不够周全之处，请再给我们一些时间，我们会在你们的陪伴下不断地改进和进步。
行胜于言，对于游戏目前体验不佳之处，全体开发团队都在紧锣密鼓地调整和优化中，具体修复和优化内容请游侠前往官网或社区进行查看。
你的支持是我们前行路上最强大的动力，也是最好的鞭策。也再次感激每一位游侠一直以来的支持与反馈。
最后，谢谢你来玩Where Winds Meet。
我们相遇在风起之地，也希望有幸一起迈向更广阔的天地。我们定不辜负！
en:
It has always been thrilling for us to see you leave the bamboo abode and embark on your journey into the world of Jianghu in Where Winds Meet. 

Just like your first encounter with Jianghu, our initial attempt to connect with players around the globe has been both exciting and uncertain. But our passion and commitment to creating a living open world drive us forward, and your response and support to our efforts has been a tremendous encouragement, giving us the confidence to keep pushing ahead.

Since launch, we have been listening closely and working tirelessly to address the key areas where the experience has fallen short. We have made key progress in network connectivity and latency, localization and voiceovers, beginner tutorial, character customization, and more. We remain committed to ongoing improvements in essential areas such as localization, PS5 compatibility, and multi-character creation features in the near future.
Please check our official website or community posts for detailed updates and optimizations, and we welcome any further suggestions you may have.

While there is still much work to be done, we kindly ask for your patience as we continue to develop this world together with you. Thank you once again for supporting Where Winds Meet, we will not let you down!
No more slog, no more drag!

zh:
莫晓云七岁那年，爷娘又给她添了个妹妹。
那小娃娃粉雕玉琢，活泼可爱，莫晓云看着欢喜，只想把全世界的好东西都给妹妹。
爷娘给妹妹起名叫夕霓。
只是莫晓云很不喜欢这个名字。“稀泥，稀泥，妹妹才不能和稀泥呢！”
爷娘被逗得前仰后合，妹妹却伸出手抓着姐姐的手指不放。

于是，给妹妹改名字成了莫晓云的心病。
待妹妹长大一些，莫晓云认真地问妹妹。“小霓儿，你要不要阿姊给你改个名字？”
莫夕霓捧着自己的脸，仰着头看阿姊，一脸听不懂的样子。“小霓儿听阿姊的！阿姊说什么就是什么！”
“那阿姊给你想一个！”莫晓云立刻开始转动大脑。“莫大云？不好，莫……莫夕夕？也不好……”没读过几年书，莫晓云也想不出什么新鲜词。
最后，她决定，和妹妹一起改名……

晚上回来，爷娘喊姐妹两个吃饭。
莫晓云拉着妹妹，一脸骄傲地宣布。
“以后我们两个要改名字了！我叫莫大妮，她叫莫小妮……”
爷娘相视，不由笑出声来。
“你这孩子，莫不是总觉得'夕霓'二字不好听，所以才要改名?"
阿爷把莫晓云抱在怀里。“你们姐妹两个的名字可是阿爷阿娘求了好多私塾先生才得的。”
“把你们的名字连起来，是什么呀？”
“晓云……夕霓……”莫晓云念着，一头雾水。
“是晓夕云霓。”阿娘温柔地扑打妹妹裙摆上的灰尘。
“阿爷和阿娘只希望，你们这一生都如云霓自由，不论晓夕。”
姐妹两个似懂非懂地点点头，相视一笑，两只小手紧紧拉在一起。
en:
The year Mo Xiaoyun was seven, her parents gave her a little sister. 
The baby was pink and jade-like, lively and adorable. Mo Xiaoyun was delighted, wanting to give all the world's good things to her sister. 
Her parents named the little one Xini. 
But Mo Xiaoyun didn't like the name at all. "Xini, Xini—my sister can't be like mud!" 
Her parents were doubled over with laughter, but the little sister reached out and grabbed her big sister's finger, refusing to let go. 

Thus, changing her sister's name became Mo Xiaoyun's obsession. 
When her sister was a little older, Mo Xiaoyun seriously asked her, "Little Ni, do you want your big sister to give you a new name?" 
Mo Xini cupped her own face, looking up at her sister with an expression of incomprehension. "Big Sister, whatever you say, I will say yes!" 
"Great!" Mo Xiaoyun immediately started racking her brains. "Mo Dayun? No good. Mo... Mo Xixi? Not good either..." Having not studied much, she couldn't come up with anything fresh. 
Finally, she decided to change her own name along with her sister's... 

That evening when their parents called them for dinner, 
Mo Xiaoyun led her sister by the hand and announced proudly, 
"From now on, we're changing our names! I'm Mo Dani, and she's Mo Xiaoni..." 
Her parents looked at each other and couldn't help laughing. 
"Silly child, is it because you always thought 'Xini' didn't sound nice, so you wanted to change it?" 
Father picked Mo Xiaoyun up. "Your names were ones your mother and I asked many tutors to suggest." 
"What do your names make when put together?" 
"Xiaoyun... Xini..." Mo Xiaoyun recited, puzzled. 
"It's Morning Clouds and Evening Glories," Mother said gently, brushing dust from her younger daughter's skirt. 
"Your father and I only wish that your lives be as free as clouds and rainbows, whether at dawn or dusk." 
The sisters nodded, only half-understanding. They looked at each other, smiled, and their small hands clasped tightly together.

zh:
那是一次相约已久的棋局。对手也是十里有名的棋手。
那一天，烈阳高照。杜不弈早早来到相约的地点。也许是因为紧张，也许是因为周围热烈的氛围，杜不弈只觉口干舌燥。
一个少年抱着一只铜盒叫卖。“冰葡萄哟，凉津津的冰葡萄哟！”
听闻此言，杜不弈眼前一亮。
“快来快来，给我来……来三份！”
甜滋滋冰凉凉的葡萄在口舌间爆浆，滑入喉间，如清泉滋养干涸龟裂的土地。杜不弈发出满足的呼声。
”再给我来五份！不，我全要了！拿着钱！不必找了！“
杜不弈接过铜盒，在众人钦佩的眼光中就这么席地而坐，一口一口吃着冰葡萄，直到对手的到来。

分出先后手，杜不弈屏息以待——
突然，一阵咕噜声传来。杜不弈的肚子仿佛被倒入了刀片滚水，立刻疼得他直冒冷汗。
杜不弈深吸一口气，凝神，蓄力。可腹痛的抽痛不由人控制，杜不弈只觉得腿软，手中的棋子也失了力。
咬咬牙，杜不弈射出了自己的第一枚棋子——那棋子待着一往无前的常胜之勇，直直冲向棋盘边缘之外。
“哎哟——”不知是懊恼还是疼痛，杜不弈紧闭的牙关泄出一声惨叫。
众人只看到他落荒而逃，夹着步子跑走的身影。
此刻，杜不弈根本无暇顾及胜负——原来最难战胜的，是自己的身体……
en:
It was a long-awaited match. His opponent was also a player of renown from miles around. 
That day, the sun blazed down. Du Buyi arrived early at the agreed spot. Perhaps from nerves, perhaps from the heated atmosphere around him, his mouth felt parched and dry. 
A young boy hawked a copper box. "Ice-cold grapes! Sweet and chilled grapes!" 
Hearing this, Du Buyi's eyes lit up. 
"Over here! Quick, give me... three servings!" 
Sweet, icy grapes burst in his mouth, sliding down his throat like a clear spring nourishing cracked, dry earth. Du Buyi let out a satisfied sigh. 
"Five more! No, I'll take them all! Here's the money, keep the change!" 
Du Buyi took the copper box and, under the admiring eyes of the crowd, sat right on the ground, eating the frozen grapes one by one until his opponent arrived. 

They drew lots for first move. Du Buyi held his breath, waiting— 
Suddenly, a gurgling sound came. It was as if shards of glass and boiling water had been poured into his stomach. Pain made cold sweat break out instantly. 
Du Buyi took a deep breath, focused, gathered his strength. But the cramping wouldn't be controlled. His legs felt weak, the piece in his hand losing its force. 
Gritting his teeth, Du Buyi launched his first piece—carrying the momentum of past victories, it shot straight... off the edge of the board. 
"Oww—!" Whether from frustration or pain, a stifled cry escaped Du Buyi's clenched jaw. 
The crowd only saw him flee in panic, scurrying away with an awkward gait. 
At that moment, Du Buyi had no mind for victory or defeat—sometimes the hardest opponent to beat is your own body...
You want to kill him?

zh:
在“李代桃僵”之计刚完成的时候，冯如之的心中就生出过这个问题：郑鄂会不会回头？
她知道这个猜想乍听上去及其荒谬。毕竟从流寇暴乱的那个血夜开始，到朝生暮落之害、洪水袭城之灾…… 过去的十二年里，他已经经历、承受太多。可是在已故母亲朱鱼的口中，郑鄂从不是一个铁石心肠的人。那个只存在于描述中的“阿郑”又正直又善良，他与沈义伦情谊深厚，包括承恩镇民在内的开封百姓，都曾被囊括入他们的理想。
这种忧虑在愈臻功成之时愈发强烈，迫使冯如之不得不借口转运粮草，冒险坐小船经黑市过暗河，来到常平仓地下，去试探义兄的想法。可她到底不是个善于遮掩的人，少女的心思明明白白地写在脸上，还没出言相询，就已被人看穿。

“我不会动摇。”郑鄂答得直截了当。“恶人不除尽，好人如何活。”
“可是…… 如果有一天赵宋归还了田地，承恩镇的人也纷纷悔过……”
“我不会动摇。”他再一次强调。“恶人不会改过。就算野狼能够披上羊皮混入羊群，狼也永远是狼，狼终究要吃羊。”
“可是……”
冯如之还想说，然而这一次，郑鄂直接打断了她。
“如之！阿阮死了，朱鱼死了，大家都死了…… 咳咳咳。”
说完这句，郑鄂突然难以遏制地咳嗽起来。他好容易才平复呼吸，只是再开口时，吐出的每个字里好似都冒着森森的寒气。
“我的亲友所剩无几。他们应该活下去，他们必须活下去，所以…… 我不能动摇。”
郑鄂定定地注视着眼前人，冯如之猝不及防地被那道锐利的眼神狠狠刺中了一下。她不再说话了，有些惊讶于这短短几句话中渗透而出的绝望，无可挽回的悲哀和毫无退路的执念在沉默中慢慢生长。

“不要再来了。”郑鄂简短地结束了对话。“如果连你也感染了寒毒……，我无法向师父朱鱼交代。”
郑鄂有些艰难地起身，骨头如痹症病人那般，发出轻微的摩擦声响。可他却连眉头都没皱一下，只是沉默地推开沉重的铁门，头也不回地走向那条幽深的甬道。——他明明穿得是白色的大氅，可身影却很快便被那株巨大朝生暮落花所投下的阴影吞没了。
冯如之朝郑鄂消失的方向又瞧了许久，才缓缓收回视线。她又一次地想起那个母亲曾无数次地向她描述过的少年，心中生出许多不可言说的感慨。那个少年坚守着“天下常平”的志向，身边围绕着志同道合的朋友、爱他信他的亲人，心底里填满了纯粹的善意和希望。
“真遗憾呐。”冯如之心想，“如果他也能活下来该多好，我很想亲自认识他。”
en:
The moment the "sacrifice the plum for the peach" scheme was completed, Feng Ruzhi had already wondered: Would Zheng E turn back?
She knew how absurd this speculation sounded at first glance. After all, from that bloody night of the marauder uprising, to the "Dawn-to-Dusk Plague", and the catastrophic floods... over the past twelve years, he had endured far too much. Yet according to her late mother Zhu Yu's accounts, Zheng E had never been a heartless man. The "A'zheng" who existed only in stories was righteous and kind, a man who shared a deep bond with Shen Yilun. Their ideals had once embraced all of Kaifeng commoners, including the townsfolk of Gracetown.
As their mission neared success, her unease grew. Pretending to transport supplies, she risked taking a small boat through black markets and dark rivers to the underground Ever-Normal Granary, hoping to gauge her brother's resolve. But she was no good at hiding her feelings, and the worry on her face gave her away before she even spoke.

"I won't waver," Zheng E said bluntly. "No peace for the good until all evil is eliminated."
"But... what if the Song court returns the land, and Gracetown repents..."
"I won't waver," he repeated. "Evil doesn't repent. A wolf in sheep's clothing is still a wolf. It will always hunt sheep."
"But..."
Feng Ruzhi opened her mouth to speak again, but this time, Zheng E cut her off without hesitation.
"Ruzhi! A'ruan is dead, Zhu Yu is dead, everyone is dead... *coughs*..."
After saying this, Zheng E was suddenly seized by uncontrollable coughing. When he finally regained his breath and spoke again, each word seemed to carry a deathly chill.
"I have few loved ones left. They deserve to live. They must live. That's why I can't waver." Zheng E fixed his gaze upon her, and Feng Ruzhi flinched as if pierced by its sharpness. She fell silent, startled by the despair that had seeped into those few words. An irrevocable sorrow, and a resolve past the point of no return, quietly took root between them.

"Do not come again." His voice was curt, final. "If even you were to succumb to the cold poison... I could never face Master Zhu Yu again." With visible effort, Zheng E pushed himself upright, his bones emitting the faint, grating creak of a palsy patient. Yet not so much as a flicker of pain crossed his face. Wordlessly, he shouldered open the heavy iron gate and strode into the shadowed corridor beyond without a backward glance. He wore a white cloak, but the silhouette was swiftly devoured by the gloom cast from the massive Dawn-to-Dusk Blossom.
Feng Ruzhi stared long after he had vanished before finally lowering her eyes. Once more, she thought of the youth her mother had so often described, a boy who clung fiercely to his dream of "Ever-Normal for All", surrounded by comrades who shared his cause, by kin who loved and believed in him, his heart brimming with untainted hope.
"What a pity," she mused. "If only he could have lived. I would have liked to meet that version of him."

小时候，菜菜从草丛里捡回了它。那时的黑蛋糊满煤灰泥巴，黑不溜秋，路人都唤它“黑蛋儿”。直到菜菜坚持不懈地帮它舔毛，露出了原本的花色，大家才惊觉这竟是只漂亮的小花狗。为了养活黑蛋，菜菜省下了自己的一半小鱼干，硬是把黑蛋养得比自己还壮实。
如今，每当午后日暖，黑蛋便奔走在皇宫各处，给菜菜寻摸好吃的，再跑回小草窝，和菜菜头挨着头晒太阳。对黑蛋而言，狗生最快乐的事有两件：一是看见太阳，二是看见菜菜。
en:
Heidan is Veggie's best dog buddy. They live together in a secluded courtyard full of flowers and greenery.

When they were little, Veggie found it in the grass. Back then, Heidan was caked in soot and mud, black from head to toe, so passersby called it "Heidan."

Only after Veggie kept licking its fur clean did its real markings show through. That was when everyone realized it was actually a pretty little spotted dog.

To keep Heidan fed, Veggie saved half of its own dried fish and somehow raised Heidan to be even sturdier than itself.

Now, whenever the afternoon sun turns warm, Heidan races all over the palace to sniff out something tasty for Veggie, then runs back to their grass nest to bask in the sun with Veggie, heads resting together.

For Heidan, life has two greatest joys: seeing the sun, and seeing Veggie.

en: Fleshy, incredibly succulent, and sweet, this fruit has a warm nature. Its tree can grow several meters tall, wrapped in greyish-brown bark with narrow, alternating leaves. When spring arrives, it bursts into bloom. The five-petaled flowers resemble plum blossoms, painting the orchards in a romantic blur of pink and white. By late summer and early autumn, the fruits ripen into oval or near-spherical shapes, their skins dusted with a soft velvet fuzz. Beneath lies yellow or white flesh, encasing a hard pit that holds the seed kernel. Since ancient times, the resilient peach wood has been crafted into tools and spiritual wards. Truly, its blossoms, fruits, and timber are all treasures of utility.

zh:
活人医馆曾经收治过一位老妇人，说是家里人搬去了开封，病倒后无人照看。村民们只得将她送来活人医馆。老妇人觉着前来送药的豆豆长得真像她那小孙儿，便抓了一把饴糖塞进了他的手里。自那以后豆豆不知着了什么魔，天天都去陪那老妇人聊天逗趣。药药问他，他只说老妇人亲切，或许真是他失散的家人也说不准。药药知道豆豆是天不收捡来的孤儿，哪来的什么家人。可天不收从不让他在豆豆跟前提起这事，药药也只好摇头叹气，懒得再与豆豆争辩。
豆豆深信天不收是这天底下最厉害的神医，定能治好老妇人的病。可好景不长，不过一月时间，老妇人还是撒手人寰。

天不收找到豆豆时，他正一个人抱膝坐在塘边。天不收只道生老病死乃是定律，豆豆却无法理解。若生老病死真是定律，那要医者又有何用？天不收没有接话，从身后拿出一小包饴糖转交给豆豆。那老妇人自知时日无多，但有豆豆在一旁逗乐，倒是少了惊惧痛苦。这饴糖便是她给豆豆的谢礼。
豆豆拿着那包饴糖终究还是没忍住眼泪。
en:
There was once an elderly woman brought to the Evercare Clinic. Her children had long since moved to Kaifeng, and when illness struck, there was no one left to care for her. The villagers, helpless and unsure of what else to do, brought her to the clinic. When she saw Doudou—the boy who delivered her medicine—she smiled and pressed a handful of sweet candies into his palm. He reminded her of her grandson. No one knew why, but from that day on, Doudou visited her every day. He would sit by her side, chat with her, and make her laugh. When Yaoyao asked him why, Doudou simply replied, "She's kind. Maybe... maybe she's someone I lost—a relative, maybe." Yaoyao knew the truth: Doudou had no family. He was an orphan, taken in by Unfated Tian. But Unfated Tian had made it clear—never say that in front of the boy. So Yaoyao simply sighed and let it go.

Doudou believed that Unfated Tian could cure anyone. He was the greatest healer in the world, and surely he could make the elderly woman well again. But only a month later, she passed away.

Unfated Tian found Doudou sitting alone by the pond, his arms wrapped tightly around his knees. Unfated Tian sat beside him and spoke gently, "Birth, aging, illness, and death... they're all part of life's path." But Doudou didn't understand. If death came no matter what, then what was the point of being a healer? Unfated Tian didn't answer. Instead, he reached into his sleeve and pulled out a small paper-wrapped bundle—candies. "She knew her time was short," Unfated Tian said, "But you made her laugh. You made her less afraid. These were her way of saying thank you."Doudou took the bundle in his small hands, and for the first time since she'd gone, he cried.

zh:
那是多少年前的一桩旧事了？她已记不清了，就像她忘了名字，只记得自己的侠号是云中君。
那夜观天象，推测或有坠星，她便兴致勃勃地盼了起来。可最近秋凉，再加前些时日在外游学劳碌奔波，自己竟落了病，浑身发烫。老詹想劝她留在屋里好生休养，但她向来是出了名的执拗。坠星哪能错过？下回再遇上还不知是何日呢。
她就这么固执地在前头走着，老詹背着被褥子、汤婆子、药罐子在后头追。好容易到了地方，两人依偎在一起，倒也暖和。可恨暖得太安逸，她竟不知不觉昏沉睡去，再到醒来时，天已蒙蒙亮。老詹不知何时在一旁生了火，锅里的菜肉粥“咕嘟咕嘟”地滚着，香气暖融融地飘来。
“昨夜坠星来过吗？”
“来了，就是唤不醒你。”
她很是沮丧。
“但给你捡到了这个。你不是说，星坠至地，则石也？”
她看着老詹手里那枚晶莹剔透的怪石子，忍不住笑出了声。
“回头镶起来，好叫你时时戴着。往后伸手一拿就是坠星，不必再一个劲地往外跑了。”
en:
How many years ago was that old matter? She couldn't remember clearly, just like she had forgotten her name, only recalling her hero title, Lord of Clouds.
That night, observing the stars, she predicted a possible meteor shower and eagerly awaited it. But the autumn chill, combined with fatigue from recent travels and studies, had made her ill. She was burning with fever. Old Zhan wanted to persuade her to stay inside and rest, but she had always been notoriously stubborn. How could she miss a meteor shower? Who knew when the next one would come?
So she stubbornly led the way, with Old Zhan following behind, carrying bedding, a hot water bottle, and medicine pots. When they finally reached the spot, they huddled together for warmth. But it was so warm and comfortable that she unknowingly fell into a deep sleep. When she awoke, the sky was already light. Old Zhan had somehow started a fire, and a pot of meat and vegetable porridge was bubbling away, its warm fragrance wafting over.
"Did the meteor shower come last night?"
"It came, but we couldn't wake you."
She felt very dejected.
"But I picked this up for you. Didn't you say that when a star falls to earth, it becomes stone?"
She looked at the strange, crystal-clear stone in Old Zhan's hand and couldn't help but laugh.
"I'll have it set for you so you can wear it always. From now on, you can just reach for a fallen star instead of constantly running outside."

zh:
风雪夜，农户的草棚迎来了一队兵。
农户的手在发抖。不开门，马上丢命；开了门，早晚是死。他将缩在炕角的妻女塞进破衣柜，颤着手拨开了门闩。
为首之人说他叫张议潮，带的兵叫归义军。农户听不懂这些名头，只觉得这队蓝衣兵，与往常那些豺狼不太一样。
他们借草料，喂了战马；借枯柴，生了堆营火。农户邀他们进屋避寒，蓝衣兵摆手谢绝。这是农户的屋子，归义军不扰民。
天蒙蒙亮，草棚里谁都没合眼。将军问农户姓名，说借了东西定会归还。农户只当客套，能活命已是万幸，哪敢指望这些？
直到蓝衣兵再次出现。他们带着新田制、新户籍，还有那个名字——张议潮。兵卒照着名册，点到农户名字，免了他一年的柴草税。
农户望着蓝衣兵。原来这些大人物，真有说话算数的。至少这个张议潮，眼下还算数。
en:
On a snowy night, a group of soldiers arrived at a farmer's thatched shed. 
The farmer's hands trembled. If he didn't open the door, he would die immediately; if he did, he would still die. He stuffed his wife and daughter, huddled in the corner of the bed, into a tattered wardrobe and unlocked the door with shaking hands. 
The leader was Zhang Yichao, and his soldiers the Guiyi Army. The farmer didn't know those names, but he felt that this group of soldiers in blue robes was different from the usual jackals. 
They only borrowed forage to feed their war horses and dry firewood to build a campfire. The farmer invited them into the house to escape the cold, but the blue-robed soldiers declined. This was the farmer's house, and the Guiyi Army would not disturb the people. 
When dawn arrived, no one in the thatched shed had slept a wink. Zhang Yichao asked for the farmer's name and said he would definitely return what he had borrowed. The farmer thought it was just polite talk. The soldiers were merciful enough to leave him and his family alive. How could he dare to hope for anything else? 
That was until the blue-robed soldiers appeared again. With them came a new land system, a new household registration list, and that name, Zhang Yichao. A soldier called the farmer's name from the roster and exempted him from a year's firewood tax. 
The farmer looked at the blue-robed soldiers. Surprised that the powerful would keep their promises. At least this Zhang Yichao did, for now.

zh:
有墨者自北方来，称有救天下策。延广闻之，盛邀入府。
初，墨者入府，处事傲然，数进策于广。不纳，欲去。于是延广与墨者诺，能现古名匠德衡之百戏人偶，转十日而不息，则纳其言。墨者应之，月余即成。及转九日而未息，第十日，墨者请资费以备黄河之渠。延广大笑，乃引墨者入观，枢机错行，已溃。墨者疑，察之，乃一木榫与制不合。延广又诺，墨者于府中饮酒百坛，则纳其策。
愚哉笑尔！不知彼墨者尽饮百坛否？
延广真欲救天下尔？欲献技于上而复得宠也！
上欲救天下尔？称孙于契丹，不取利、妄起衅，搏名青史也！
墨者真欲救天下尔？以奇技淫巧能救天下，世所未闻也！
今且观之，皆搏名利之跳梁丑，而戏你我小民而已。国策？民策？天下策？于你何益？于我何益？如梦呓，作笑谈。
en:
A Mohist arrived from the North, claiming to possess a grand strategy to save the world. Hearing of this, Jing Yanguang lavishly invited him into his estate.

At first, the Mohist carried himself with arrogance, proposing several schemes to Guang. None were accepted, and he prepared to leave. Yanguang then made a wager: if the Mohist could recreate the legendary Deheng's Spectacle Puppet and have it run for ten days without stopping, his strategy would be adopted. The Mohist agreed and completed the work in a month. The mechanism ran for nine days without pause, but on the tenth day, when the Mohist asked for funds to repair the Yellow River canals, Yanguang laughed heartily. He led the Mohist to see the puppet; its gears had jammed, and the machine had collapsed. Bewildered, the Mohist inspected it, only to find a single wooden peg that did not fit the design. Yanguang made another wager: if the Mohist could drink a hundred jars of wine within the estate, his strategy would be accepted.

What a laughable farce! I wonder, did that Mohist manage to drain all one hundred jars?

Did Yanguang truly wish to save the world? He merely sought to present a novelty to the Emperor to regain royal favor!

Did the Emperor truly wish to save the world? Calling himself a "grandson" to the Khitans, gaining no real advantage yet recklessly provoking a war, all just to make a name in history!

Did the Mohist truly wish to save the world? The idea that clever trinkets and mechanics can save the world is unheard of!

Looking back, they were little more than liars driven by fame and profit, putting on an elaborate performance to deceive the commoners. National strategy? People's welfare? World salvation? What good does it do you? What good does it do me? It is all just a joke, like ramblings of a dream.

en:
Drunken Qiantang stands foremost among the taverns of Hangzhou city. Climbing high and gazing afar, one takes in the whole of the bustling streets and hearth-smoke below, along with its pavilions and towers. A thousand jars of fine wine are stored within, of more varieties than one could count; each day it serves the rare delicacies of Jiangnan, offering its guests a feast of freshness beyond compare. Aromas drift throughout the tower, and guests fill its halls without end. Some call their friends, raising cups and tapping chopsticks in merriment; others lean alone against the balustrade, inspired with sudden poetry. Once, a scholar from a distant land climbed this tower for the first time, and after several rounds of wine, wrote the words: "One cup, and I am drunk on Qiantang; another, and I forget my way home," then cast down his brush and departed. To this day, Drunken Qiantang still draws guests without cease, and the ink of that traveler long past still carries the fierce scent of wine.
The stranger of yesteryear has become today's man of the drunken land. When the wine runs deep and joy runs its course, one no longer knows what night this is.

多亏这小巴郎子，这群猫儿真还围着个人呢，以为是泉眼呢嘛。都说沙漠里猫儿鼻子灵，月亮味道的地方喜欢着呢。你身上一定是月亮沾着了。鬼机灵的！花花草草全都给你叼来了，把你当成神仙了嘛，连咱队骆驼干粮也想叼着呢！

前方的难路啊，像沙丘一样数不清！商队骆驼带不了你，朋友自己保重着！像沙柳一样扎稳咯！
要是缘分大雁一样回来了，咱们就长安再见嘛！
en:
Hey! Friend!
You awake yet?
Strange things are happening! The young lad in our caravan said he saw spirits in the moonlight—popping up out of nowhere! He eats too much naan and talks nonsense with sand in his mouth! But when I looked, there was a whole group of cats under the moonlight, their fur shining brighter than gems, flickering like spirits!
Thanks to that kid, we found these cats gathered around you, thinking you were an oasis. They say desert cats have sharp noses—they love the scent of the moon. You must be drenched in moonlight, you sly ghost! They’ve been bringing you flowers and grass, treating you like a deity—even tried to steal our caravan’s camel feed!
Keep the little trinket I sent. Our caravan’s money bag is as dry as the Gobi, but when friends meet, we help however we can.
The road ahead is tough, endless as the dunes! The caravan’s camels can’t carry you, so stay strong, friend! Stand firm like a desert willow!
If fate brings you back like a migrating goose, we’ll meet again in Chang’an!
Qianbei Wan

玄金短甲静静躺在库房角落，随行来取料的年轻弟子经过，忍不住为它的流光所惊叹。
鹏只多看了一眼。

无用的死物，倒唤醒了些许无用的旧忆。
当年有人被她顺手救下，成了一名穷奇师。有一天他突然送上了这玄金甲，言称是亲手在山中采的玄金，将其锻甲，以谢救命之恩。
她早已不记得那人名姓样貌，也懒得细想当日为何出手。
这些旁枝末节就和甲上的金光一样，最易惑人耳目，可进了火炉，也不过一滩铁水罢了。
为天下司南者，心不可为外物所移。
不为多余的事哀嗟，不被无用之器所累。行走在正确的道路上，献祭掉这些微不足道的情感，这已是，最微末的牺牲。
en:
The Golden Short Armor lay quietly in a corner of the warehouse. Young disciples passing by to collect materials couldn't help but marvel at its luster.
Peng only gave it a single glance.
"A useless scrap, nothing more."
A useless, dead object, yet it awakened some useless old memories.
Years ago, she had saved someone on a whim, and he became a Qiongqi Artificer. One day he suddenly presented this dark gold armor, claiming he had mined the metal in the mountains and forged it himself to repay her for saving his life.
She had long forgotten the man's name and face, and didn't care to think why she had intervened that day.
These trivial details were like the golden light on the armor: easy to deceive the eye, but once in the furnace, they were nothing but molten iron.
For the one who acts as the Lodestar for the world, the heart must not be moved by external things.
Do not mourn for the redundant, nor be burdened by useless tools. Walk the correct path and sacrifice these insignificant emotions. This is but the smallest of sacrifices.

zh:
北魏晚期至东魏时期的鎏金铜佛像，高35.2厘米，宽22.5厘米，重2.729千克，现藏陕西历史博物馆。主尊佛立于莲台上，手施无畏与愿印，背光饰火焰纹。台座两侧有龙形饰件承托菩萨。
佛像铸造时期可追溯至北魏，为一佛二菩萨组合。北魏孝文帝推行改革后，佛教艺术造像走向了汉家士大夫所推崇的秀骨清像、褒衣博带的风格，该佛像也是目前所知具有青州风格的唯一的金铜造像。
en: A gilt-bronze Buddha statue from the late Northern Wei to Eastern Wei period, now housed in the Shaanxi History Museum. It measures 35.2 cm high, 22.5 cm wide, and weighs 2.729 kg. The principal Buddha stands on a lotus pedestal, with the gestures of fearlessness and wish-granting, backed by a flame-pattern halo. Dragon-shaped ornaments on either side support two bodhisattvas, forming a one-Buddha, two-bodhisattva composition. Following Emperor Xiaowen's reforms, Buddhist sculpture took on the slender figures and flowing robes favored by Han literati. This statue is the only known gilt-bronze example in the Qingzhou style.

zh:
①本局游戏为多轮循环模式，每轮开局重新发牌。
②每轮随机确定一个安全数字，每人固定发放5张手牌。出牌阶段可打出1~3 张牌，万能牌可替代任意牌型。
③若认为他人出牌不属于安全牌型，可发起质疑：质疑成功，对方罚酒一次；质疑失败，自己罚酒一次。
④单轮只要有玩家被罚酒，该轮即刻结束；场上仅剩最后一名玩家时，本局游戏结束。
⑤出牌倒计时结束，会自动随机出牌；若全场只剩一名未打完牌的玩家，其回合将自动发起质疑。
en:
1. Each game is played in multiple rounds. At the start of every round, a new hand of cards is dealt.
2. At the start of every round, a random Safe Number is chosen, and every player receives 5 cards. During your turn, you may play 1 to 3 cards. Wild Cards can substitute for any number.
3. You can challenge a player if you think they played cards that don't meet the Safe Number. If your challenge succeeds, the other player takes a drink. If it fails, you take a drink.
4. A round ends as soon as someone takes a drink. When only one player remains in the game, the match ends.
5. If you don't play your cards before the timer runs out, random cards will be played for you. If only one player still has cards left, their turn will automatically trigger a challenge.

zh:
【离娄章句上】

孟子曰：离娄之明，公输子之巧，不以规矩，不能成方员；师旷之聪，不以六律，不能正五音。尧舜之道，不以仁政，不能平治天下。今有仁心仁闻，而民不被其泽，不可法于后世者，不行先王之道也。故曰：徒善不足以为政，徒法不能以自行。诗云：不愆不忘，率由旧章。遵先王之法而过者，未之有也。圣人既竭目力焉，继之以规矩准绳，以为方员平直，不可胜用也；既竭耳力焉，继之以六律正五音，不可胜用也；既竭心思焉，继之以不忍人之政，而仁覆天下矣。故曰：为高必因丘陵，为下必因川泽，为政不因先王之道，可谓智乎？是以惟仁者宜在高位，不仁而在高位，是播其恶于众也。上无道揆也，下无法守也，朝不信道，工不信度，君子犯义，小人犯刑，国之所存者幸也。故曰：城郭不完，兵甲不多，非国之灾也；田野不辟，货财不聚，非国之害也。上无礼，下无学，贼民兴，丧无日矣。诗曰：天之方蹶，无然泄泄。泄泄，犹沓沓也。事君无义，进退无礼，言则非先王之道者，犹沓沓也。故曰：责难于君谓之恭，陈善闭邪谓之敬，吾君不能谓之贼。
孟子曰：规矩，方员之至也；圣人，人伦之至也。欲为君，尽君道；欲为臣，尽臣道，二者皆法尧舜而已矣。不以舜之所以事尧事君，不敬其君者也；不以尧之所以治民治民，贼其民者也。孔子曰：道二，仁与不仁而已矣。暴其民甚，则身弑国亡；不甚，则身危国削。名之曰幽、厉，虽孝子慈孙，百世不能改也。诗云：殷鉴不远，在夏后之世，此之谓也。
孟子曰：三代之得天下也以仁，其失天下也以不仁。国之所以废兴存亡者亦然。天子不仁，不保四海；诸侯不仁，不保社稷；卿大夫不仁，不保宗庙；士庶人不仁，不保四体。今恶死亡而乐不仁，是由恶醉而强酒。
孟子曰：爱人不亲，反其仁；治人不治，反其智；礼人不答，反其敬。行有不得者，皆反求诸己，其身正而天下归之。诗云：永言配命，自求多福。
孟子曰：人有恒言，皆曰天下国家。天下之本在国，国之本在家，家之本在身。
孟子曰：为政不难，不得罪于巨室。巨室之所慕，一国慕之。一国之所慕，天下慕之。故沛然德教溢乎四海。
孟子曰：天下有道，小德役大德，小贤役大贤。天下无道，小役大，弱役强。斯二者，天也。顺天者存，逆天者亡。齐景公曰：既不能令，又不受命，是绝物也，涕出而女于吴。今也小国师大国而耻受命焉，是犹弟子而耻受命于先师也。如耻之，莫若师文王。师文王，大国五年，小国七年，必为政于天下矣。诗云：商之孙子，其丽不亿。上帝既命，侯于周服。侯服于周，天命靡常。殷士肤敏，祼将于京。孔子曰：仁不可为众也。夫国君好仁，天下无敌。今也欲无敌于天下而不以仁，是犹执热而不以濯也。诗云：谁能执热，逝不以濯？
孟子曰：不仁者可与言哉！安其危而利其菑，乐其所以亡者。不仁而可与言，则何亡国败家之有？有孺子歌曰：沧浪之水清兮，可以濯我缨；沧浪之水浊兮，可以濯我足。孔子曰：小子听之，清斯濯缨，浊斯濯足矣，自取之也。夫人必自侮，然后人侮之；家必自毁，然后人毁之；国必自伐，然后人伐之。大甲曰：天作孽，犹可违；自作孽，不可活，此之谓也。
孟子曰：桀、纣之失天下也，失其民也，失其民者，失其心也。得天下有道，得其民，斯得天下矣。得其民有道，得其心，斯得民矣。得其心有道，所欲与之聚之，所恶勿施尔也。民之归仁也，犹水之就下，兽之走圹也。故为渊欧鱼者，獭也；为丛欧爵者，鹯也；为汤、武欧民者，桀与纣也。今天下之君有好仁者，则诸侯皆为之欧矣，虽欲无王，不可得已。今之欲王者，犹七年之病求三年之艾也。苟为不畜，终身不得；苟不志于仁，终身忧辱，以陷于死亡。诗云：其何能淑？载胥及溺。此之谓也。
孟子曰：自暴者不可与有言也，自弃者不可与有为也。言非礼义，谓之自暴也；吾身不能居仁由义，谓之自弃也。仁，人之安宅也；义，人之正路也。旷安宅而弗居，舍正路而不由，哀哉！
孟子曰：道在迩而求诸远，事在易而求之难。人人亲其亲，长其长，而天下平。
……
en:
【Lilou Chapter I】

Mencius said: "Even with the sharp eyes of Lilou and the skill of Gongshu Zi, one cannot draw perfect circles and squares without compasses and squares. Even with the keen hearing of Shi Kuang, one cannot tune the five notes without the six pitch pipes. Even the ways of Yao and Shun cannot bring peace and order to the world without benevolent governance. If a ruler has a benevolent heart and a reputation for benevolence, yet the people do not benefit from his kindness, and he cannot serve as a model for future generations, it is because he does not follow the ways of the ancient kings. Thus, it is said: 'Benevolence alone is insufficient for governance; laws alone cannot enforce themselves.' The Book of Songs says: 'Do not err, do not forget, but follow the old statutes.' Those who follow the laws of the ancient kings and still err are unheard of. When sages exhaust their visual acuity, they use compasses, squares, and rulers to create circles, squares, and straight lines, which can be used endlessly. When they exhaust their auditory acuity, they use the six pitch pipes to tune the five notes, which can be used endlessly. When they exhaust their mental faculties, they implement governance rooted in compassion, and benevolence spreads across the world. Thus, it is said: 'To build high, one must rely on hills; to dig deep, one must rely on rivers and marshes. Can one be called wise if one governs without relying on the ways of the ancient kings?' Therefore, only the benevolent are fit for high positions. If the unworthy occupy high positions, they spread their wickedness among the masses. When those above lack moral principles and those below lack laws to abide by, when the court does not trust the Way and artisans do not trust measurements, when gentlemen violate righteousness and petty people violate the law, the survival of the state is merely a matter of luck. Thus, it is said: 'Incomplete city walls and insufficient armor are not the disasters of a state; unopened fields and unaccumulated wealth are not the harms of a state. When those above lack propriety and those below lack learning, rebels arise, and ruin is imminent.' The Book of Songs says: 'When Heaven is about to overturn, do not be so complacent.' 'Complacent' means negligent. Serving one's ruler without righteousness, advancing or retreating without propriety, and speaking against the ways of the ancient kings are all forms of negligence. Thus, it is said: 'To hold one's ruler to high standards is called reverence; to present goodness and suppress evil is called respect; to say one's ruler is incapable is called treachery.'
Mencius said: "Compasses and squares are the ultimate tools for creating circles and squares; sages are the ultimate models for human relationships. If one wishes to be a ruler, one must fulfill the duties of a ruler; if one wishes to be a minister, one must fulfill the duties of a minister. Both must emulate Yao and Shun. To not serve one's ruler as Shun served Yao is to disrespect one's ruler; to not govern the people as Yao governed the people is to harm the people. Confucius said: 'There are only two paths: benevolence and its absence.' If a ruler oppresses his people severely, he will be killed and his state will perish; if less severely, he will be endangered and his state will weaken. Once labeled 'Dark' or 'Cruel,' even filial sons and kind grandsons cannot change this reputation for a hundred generations. The Book of Songs says: 'The mirror of Yin is not far; it lies in the age of the Xia.' This is what it means.
Mencius said: "The Three Dynasties gained the world through benevolence and lost it through its absence. The rise and fall, survival and demise of states follow the same principle. If the Son of Heaven is not benevolent, he cannot protect the four seas; if feudal lords are not benevolent, they cannot protect their altars of soil and grain; if high ministers are not benevolent, they cannot protect their ancestral temples; if scholars and commoners are not benevolent, they cannot protect their own bodies. To fear death yet delight in cruelty is like hating drunkenness yet forcing oneself to drink.
Mencius said: "If you love others but they do not reciprocate, reflect on your own benevolence; if you govern others but they are not orderly, reflect on your own wisdom; if you treat others with propriety but they do not respond, reflect on your own respect. When actions do not yield the desired results, always seek the cause within yourself. When one's own character is upright, the world will submit. The Book of Songs says: 'Always in accord with the Mandate, seek abundant blessings for yourself.'
Mencius said: "People often say, 'The world, the state, and the family.' The foundation of the world lies in the state; the foundation of the state lies in the family; the foundation of the family lies in the individual.
Mencius said: "Governing is not difficult; it is about not offending the great families. What the great families admire, the whole state admires; what the whole state admires, the world admires. Thus, virtuous teachings overflow abundantly across the four seas.
Mencius said: "When the world follows the Way, the less virtuous serve the more virtuous, and the less worthy serve the more worthy. When the world does not follow the Way, the small serve the large, and the weak serve the strong. Both are decreed by Heaven. Those who follow Heaven survive; those who defy it perish. Duke Jing of Qi said: 'If one can neither command nor accept commands, one is cut off from all things.' He wept as he gave his daughter to Wu. Now, small states emulate large states but are ashamed to accept their commands. This is like a disciple being ashamed to accept the commands of his master. If ashamed, they should emulate King Wen. By emulating King Wen, large states will achieve governance over the world in five years, and small states in seven. The Book of Songs says: 'The descendants of Shang are countless, but Heaven has commanded them to submit to Zhou. Submitting to Zhou shows the Mandate is not constant. The nobles of Yin, dignified and quick, assist at the capital.' Confucius said: 'Benevolence cannot be measured by numbers.' If a ruler loves benevolence, he will be invincible in the world. To seek invincibility without benevolence is like holding something hot without washing it. The Book of Songs says: 'Who can hold something hot without washing it?'
Mencius said: "Can one reason with the cruel? They find security in danger and profit in disaster, delighting in what leads to their ruin. If one could reason with the cruel, how could states perish and families be ruined? There is a children's song: 'When the Canglang's waters are clear, I can wash my hat strings; when the Canglang's waters are muddy, I can wash my feet.' Confucius said: 'Listen, my disciples: clear waters wash hat strings; muddy waters wash feet. It is determined by the water itself.' A person must first insult themselves before others insult them; a family must first destroy itself before others destroy it; a state must first attack itself before others attack it. Tai Jia said: 'Heaven-sent calamities can be avoided; self-inflicted calamities cannot be survived.' This is what it means.
Mencius said: "Jie and Zhou lost the world because they lost the people. To lose the people is to lose their hearts. There is a way to gain the world: gain the people, and you gain the world. There is a way to gain the people: gain their hearts, and you gain the people. There is a way to gain their hearts: gather what they desire and avoid imposing what they detest. The people's turn to benevolence is like water flowing downward or beasts fleeing to the wilderness. Thus, the otter drives fish into the deep; the sparrowhawk drives sparrows into the thicket; Jie and Zhou drove the people to Tang and Wu. If there is a ruler in the world who loves benevolence, all feudal lords will drive the people to him. Even if he does not wish to become king, he cannot avoid it. Those who now wish to become kings are like someone with a seven-year illness seeking a three-year-old mugwort. If not stored in advance, they will never obtain it; if not committed to benevolence, they will live in worry and disgrace, descending into death and ruin. The Book of Songs says: 'How can they be good? They will all drown together.' This is what it means.
Mencius said: "One cannot speak with those who harm themselves; one cannot act with those who abandon themselves. Speaking against propriety and righteousness is self-harm; being unable to dwell in benevolence and follow righteousness is self-abandonment. Benevolence is humanity's peaceful abode; righteousness is humanity's proper path. How lamentable to leave the peaceful abode empty and abandon the proper path!
Mencius said: "The Way is near, yet people seek it far away; affairs are easy, yet people make them difficult. If everyone loves their parents and respects their elders, the world will be at peace.

zh:
【百花·二】

【海棠】

海棠
贾岛

纵使许昌持健笔，可怜终古愧幽姿。

海棠
郑谷
春风用意匀颜色，销得携觞与赋诗。
秾丽最宜新著雨，娇饶全在欲开时。
莫愁粉黛临窗懒，梁广丹青点笔迟。
朝醉暮吟看不足，羡他蝴蝶宿深枝。

【牡丹】

牡丹
李商隐
锦帏初卷卫夫人，绣被犹堆越鄂君。
垂手乱翻雕玉佩，招腰争舞郁金裙。
石家蜡烛何曾剪，荀令香炉可待熏。
我是梦中传彩笔，欲书花叶寄朝云。

红牡丹
王维
绿艳闲且静，红衣浅复深。
花心愁欲断，春色岂知心。

【荷花】

莲花坞
王维
日日采莲去，洲长多暮归。
弄篙莫溅水，畏湿红莲衣。

夏日南亭怀辛大
孟浩然
山光忽西落，池月渐东上。
散发乘夕凉，开轩卧闲敞。
荷风送香气，竹露滴清响。
欲取鸣琴弹，恨无知音赏。
感此怀故人，中宵劳梦想。

采莲曲
李白
若耶溪傍采莲女，笑隔荷花共人语。
日照新妆水底明，风飘香袂空中举。
岸上谁家游冶郎，三三五五映垂杨。
紫骝嘶入落花去，见此踟蹰空断肠。

【芙蓉】

临湖亭
王维
轻舸迎上客，悠悠湖上来。
当轩对尊酒，四面芙蓉开。

秋兴八首·其六
杜甫
瞿唐峡口曲江头，万里风烟接素秋。
花萼夹城通御气，芙蓉小苑入边愁。
朱帘绣柱围黄鹤，锦缆牙樯起白鸥。
回首可怜歌舞地，秦中自古帝王州。

木芙蓉
韩愈
新开寒露丛，远比水间红。
艳色宁相妒，嘉名偶自同。
采江官渡晚，搴木古祠空。
愿得勤来看，无令便逐风。
en:
【Hundred Flowers - II】

【Crabapple】

Crabapple
Jia Dao
Long have I heard travelers praise your fragrance,
By Brocade-Washing River, countless branches sway.
Even if a master's brush in Xuchang were to trace your image,
Alas, it would forever fall short of your graceful, secluded display.

Crabapple
Zheng Gu
The spring breeze, with intent, evens out your hues,
Inspiring one to bring wine and compose verse anew.
Your richest beauty shows best after a fresh rain,
Your full charm lies in the moment just before you bloom.
No need to worry over rouge by the window, languid and vain,
Nor the painter's brush, delayed, to capture your perfume.
From dawn's intoxication to dusk's chants, never enough to see,
I envy the butterfly that rests upon your deepest bough in glee.

【Peony】

Peony
Li Shangyin
Like Lady Wei when first her brocade screen is rolled,
Or Prince of E on piled embroidery, a sight to behold.
With pendent hands they toss carved jade pendants in disarray,
At the waist they vie to dance in skirts of golden hue array.
Never trimmed, the Shi family's candles burn so bright,
Ready to be perfumed, the Xun's incense burner's light.
I am he who in dreams received the colorful brush's might,
Wishing to write on petals and leaves to Morning Cloud in flight.

Red Peony
Wang Wei
Green leaves, serene and still, a tranquil delight,
Red petals, pale then deep, a shifting hue.
The flower's heart, with sorrow, seems to break outright,
But does the spring's color know the feelings it drew?

【Lotus】

Lotus Cove
Wang Wei
Day after day I go to gather lotus seed,
The long isle often sees me return at dusk's lead.
Pole the boat gently, do not splash water with speed,
Fearful of wetting my robe of red lotus, indeed.

Thinking of Xin the Elder on a Summer Day in the South Pavilion
Meng Haoran
The mountain light suddenly fades in the west,
Over the pond, the moon slowly climbs from its rest.
With hair unbound, I enjoy the evening's cool air,
Opening the window, I lounge with ease and no care.
The breeze carries the lotus fragrance, sweet and fair,
Bamboo dew drips, a clear, ringing sound everywhere.
I wish to take my lute and play a melody rare,
But regret no kindred soul is here the tune to share.
Touched by this, I think of my old friend with despair,
All night long, in dreams, my thoughts for him I bear.

Song of Gathering Lotuses
Li Bai
By the Ruoye Stream, lotus-gathering girls in sight,
Laughing behind lotus blooms, they chat with delight.
The sun shines on their fresh makeup, clear in water's light,
The wind lifts their fragrant sleeves, soaring in flight.
On the shore, which young gallant strolls, debonair and bright?
In threes and fives, they linger 'neath willows, a pleasing sight.
A purple steed neighs and vanishes among fallen blooms in flight,
Seeing this, I hesitate, my heart filled with longing's blight.

【Hibiscus】

Lakeside Pavilion
Wang Wei
A light boat welcomes honored guests with grace,
Leisurely it comes across the lake's wide space.
Facing the pavilion, with wine in hand we face,
On all four sides, hibiscus flowers embrace.

Autumn Meditations - VI
Du Fu
From Qutang Gorge's mouth to Qujiang's bend,
Ten thousand miles of wind and mist with pale autumn blend.
Flower-Calyx Path led royal air to town's end,
 Hibiscus Garden brought frontier woes to descend.
Vermilion blinds, embroidered pillars round yellow cranes wend,
Brocade cables, ivory masts start white gulls to ascend.
Looking back, pitiable the land of song and dance, my friend,
Since ancient times, the Qin region, where royal powers tend.

Cotton Rose Hibiscus
Han Yu
Newly opened in cold dew clusters, they stand,
Far redder than those by the water, so grand.
Should dazzling colors harbor envy's demand?
A fine name they share, yet by chance, not planned.
Gathering by the river ferry, late, hand in hand,
Plucking by the ancient shrine, empty, the strand.
I wish to come often and see, as you understand,
Lest they be swept away by the wind, across the land.

zh:
阳光正好，梨花又飘。午后的天光从竹叶罅隙中漏下，洒做碎金。暖洋洋的风像猫狸子，轻轻挠抓搔你的脸。十六岁离家后，你鲜少回到这里。檐下的蛛网结成画，屋子的主人去了天涯。你坐在昔日他坐着的长椅上，想起曾经自己的童言稚语，缓缓入睡。
恍惚间，你睁开眼，竟看到江叔牵着一匹马，向你走来。印象中的江叔背脊永远这般笔直，宽阔的肩膀如山如岗，为你挡下风雨。可如今你却发现他的衣摆有些脏了，脸上似乎也有了微不可察的疲惫。
此刻你有千言万语想说，但还未及开口，他便抬手止住。他似是猜到你所想，只微颔首，开口询问：
即便如此，你也想入江湖？
看着他的眼睛，你脱口而出——
#Y再想想。不知道要去哪儿，不知道该怎么办，不知道是留下还是离开。你什么都不想了，你只想多和他待着，待着就好。#E
听见你的回答，江叔点点头。他的眼神并没有什么波动，仿佛你的回答正如他所预料。在他的面前，你可以畅所欲言。因为你知道，不管你的选择是什么，他永远都站在你的身后。曾经，你是他怀中熟睡的婴孩，是他与这个世界的纽系。未来，你会成为他的骄傲，或是牵挂吗。
你起身奔向江叔，想要问问他去了哪里，问问他过得好不好。倏忽间，你的腿抽动了一下，撞在了桌角——疼痛让你睁开了眼。
阳光依然好，梨花还在飘。天光撒做碎金。风里没有故人的消息，但又处处是他，和他们的消息。
en:
The sun shines bright, and pear blossoms drift down once more. Afternoon light filters through the bamboo leaves, scattering like flecks of gold. A warm breeze, soft as a cat's paw, gently teases your cheek. You have seldom returned since leaving home at sixteen. Cobwebs beneath the eaves have woven into intricate paintings, while the master of the house has wandered to the ends of the earth. Sitting on the long bench where he once sat, you recall your childish prattle from long ago and slowly drift off to sleep.
In a daze, you open your eyes, only to see Uncle Jiang leading a horse toward you. In your memory, Uncle Jiang's back is forever straight, his broad shoulders like a sturdy mountain sheltering you from the wind and rain. Yet now, you notice his hem is slightly soiled, and a barely perceptible weariness lingers on his face.
Thousands of words rush to your lips, but before you can even speak, he raises a hand to stop you. As if guessing your thoughts, he gives a slight nod and asks:
"Even so, do you still wish to wander in the jianghu?"

Meeting his gaze, you blurt out...
#YGive it some more thought. You do not know where to go, what to do, or whether to stay or leave. You let go of all other thoughts. All you want is to linger by his side a little longer. Just being there is enough.#E
Hearing your answer, Uncle Jiang nods. His gaze remains steady, as if your response is exactly as he expected. Before him, you can always speak your mind. For you know that no matter your choice, he will always stand behind you. Once, you were a sleeping infant in his arms, his tether to this world. In the future, will you become his pride, or his lingering worry?
You rise and run toward Uncle Jiang, curious about where he has been and whether he has been well. Suddenly, your leg twitches, striking the corner of the table. The pain jolts your eyes open.
The sun remains bright, and the pear blossoms keep drifting down. The daylight scatters like flecks of gold. The wind carries no news of old friends, yet traces of him, and of them all, can be found everywhere.
<a long sigh>

zh:
“哎呦，小东家，别钻架子了！哪里还不满意，你说一声就行。”周叔一把拎起蹦跳的孩子，放到一旁竹荫下。
小孩勉强安生，转而叽咕着嫌灯笼太瘦，转眼又蹿到米叔背上折腾他手上的木椅，末了还蹲在田姑身边，一本正经点评被套上的鸭鹅图案不好。总之，给这小人盖的新房子这里不好，那里也不好。
众人实在没辙，拿眼睛瞧他们的东家，等着她开口。这已经是小东家说不好的第三个房子了。前两个可都是拆了重建的。

“给我过来。”寒香寻看着满场地乱窜的孩子，攥紧了手里的算盘。
孩子逐渐大了，要有自己的起居室。为了这件大事土木动工，不羡仙关门了小半年。可这位小东家一天一个主意——昨日要窄门配胖家具，今儿又改口瘦家具配宽门。
寒香寻问过几次，到底想要什么样的，小孩也说不出个所以然。只能依着，日日改，拖了三月有余。寒香寻原想纵着，可眼看第三次新房子落成在即，孩子仍闹个不停，又说不好。
“最后一次！最后改一次。”寒香寻甩开假装干嚎的孩子，头也没回地走了——今夜，活人医馆的“客人”还等她定期的复诊。

半夜，寒香寻望着圆月，想起孩子白日的“哭闹”，晚上误打误撞又被吓着的模样，终是叹了口气。
她坐在小床边，回忆起家乡的童谣，哼了起来。
被窝里，卷成一团的小孩正迷糊糊地抽噎着。
星移月落，她轻抚孩子安睡的脸，掖紧被角。
“……不要新房子，不长大，不分开……”
寒香寻忍不住回：“说胡话，你会长大，我会——”
似乎想到了什么，寒香寻凑近了孩子的脸。“要是那天来了，你一个人，也要好好的。”

更轻微的一声传来。
“娘……”
准备起身的女人差点没忍住，要落下泪来。
再折腾几个月吧，再多纵着这孩子一点。
在终将分离的那天来临前，在必定来临的那天前。
en:
"Oh, little master, mind the scaffolding! If anything is not to your liking, just give the word." Uncle Zhou scooped up the boisterous child and set him down beneath the bamboo shade.
Settling only briefly, the boy grumbled about the lanterns being too thin and then scrambled onto Uncle Mi's back to fuss over a wooden chair. Finally, he squatted by Autie Tian, gravely critiquing the embroidered ducks and geese on the linens. In short, nothing in this new house was quite right for the little master.
At their wits' end, the workers cast their eyes toward their Mistress, waiting for her to intervene. This was the third house the little master had rejected. The first two had already been razed and rebuilt.
"Come here." Han Xiangxun watched the boy dashing about the yard, her grip tightening on her abacus.
The boy was growing up; it was time he had his own quarters. For this grand endeavor, the Blissful Retreat had been shuttered for nearly half a year. Yet the little master's whims changed with the tide, one day demanding narrow doors with stout furniture, the next, slender pieces with broad entryways.
Han Xiangxun had asked many times what he truly desired, but the child could offer no clear answer. So they indulged him, revising day by day, until three months had slipped away. She had meant to be patient, but with the third house nearing completion, the boy continued his fussing, still unsatisfied.
"The last time! One final change, and no more." Han Xiangxun shrugged off the boy's feigned wailing and walked away. That night, a "guest" at the Evercare Clinic awaited her routine rounds.
At midnight, beneath the full moon, she thought of the boy's daytime antics and how he had been frightened later that evening. She sighed at last.
Sitting by his bedside, she hummed a nursery rhyme from her distant home.
Beneath the quilt, the child lay curled in a ball, sobbing in his drowsy state.
As stars drifted and the moon paled, she caressed his sleeping face and tucked the corners of his blanket tight.
"...No new house... I don't want to grow up... I don't want to be apart..."
"Foolish child," she whispered. "You will grow up, and I shall..."
As if a thought struck her, she leaned closer. "When that day comes, even if you are left alone, you must fare well."
A softer murmur drifted up.
"Mother..."
As she moved to rise, the woman nearly lost her composure to tears.
Let him fuss for a few more months. Let her indulge him just a little while longer.
Before the day of parting, before that day which must inevitably come.
Ever-Normal Granary · Zheng the Frostwing

Shi Mian ended up staying in Gracetown longer than anywhere else he'd ever been. 
He'd say it was because the Plainfield was close by and the wheat here was especially fragrant, perfect for making great noodles. 
He'd say it was because Kaifeng wasn't far, and there were plenty of skilled cooks there to learn from. 
But what he never said was that every day, when he set up his stall by the theater stage, she would set up hers right next to his. Sometimes they'd chat a little, sometimes just share a smile. That's the real reason he stayed. 
Noodles might not have feelings, but the people who make them always do.

会同九年十二月十九
汉宠功臣，聿著带河之誓；周尊元老，遂分表海之邦。久闻墨山道长老鸦，德劭功高。今畴其褒赏，即以礼，金银器物锦冠鞍马等，具如别录。

会同九年十二月二十
长老鸦心迹与余人不同，谦德机敏，宽厚体仁。曾领众山民入桃源安居，尽瘁乃事。此行高山仰止，朕素有向慕。当有升擢，特授墨山道巨子，赐铁券。山中百务，任尔便宜行事。望率我化，从我教。其益懋于远图，以钦承于休命。
……

会同九年十二月廿八
敕墨山道鸦：朕临御北关，削平四海，但推诚而待物，期率土以咸宁。惟彼墨门，自亏恩赏，曲尽绥怀之道，终藏奸诈之心。锋镝之下，玉石难分，明开转福之门，当体好生之意。惟尔通晤，知我诚怀，故兹示谕，想宜知悉。
en:
Beneath the uneven leg of the table lies a stack of ten tattered silk edicts. They read:

19th Day of the Twelfth Month, 946 CE
The Han honored meritorious ministers, swearing oaths as enduring as the Yellow River. The Zhou esteemed their elder statesmen, granting them lands by the sea. It has long been known that Elder Raven of Mohist Hill is a man of great virtue and high merit. We therefore bestow rewards in his honor, namely gold, silver, vessels, brocade crowns, saddled horses, and the like, all as listed separately.

20th Day of the Twelfth Month, 946 CE
Elder Raven's heart and conduct are unlike those of ordinary men. Modest in virtue, keen in mind, broad in generosity, and rooted in benevolence, he once led the mountain folk into Haven and settled them there in peace, spending himself utterly in their service. Such conduct inspires reverence like a lofty peak, and We have long held him in admiration. He is hereby specially raised to the rank of Grandmaster of Mohist Hill and granted an iron charter. All affairs within the mountain are entrusted to his discretion. We hope that you will accept Our transforming influence and follow Our teachings, and that you will labor all the more for the sake of Our far-reaching designs, in reverent obedience to this gracious command.
...

28th Day of the Twelfth Month, 946 CE
Edict to Raven of Mohist Hill: We have come to govern the northern marches and bring peace to the four seas, ever dealing with others in sincerity, in hopes that all under Heaven may know peace. Yet the Mohists, for all the favor and rewards bestowed upon them, and for all the pains taken to win them over, still conceal hearts full of treachery. Once arrows fly, the worthy and the worthless are not easily told apart. Yet the gate of renewed fortune still stands open, and the will to spare life ought to be understood. You alone have spoken with Us and know the sincerity of Our intentions. Thus We issue this edict, trusting that you will understand.

zh:
自公主千金悬《凉州十景》诗榜，众人为得青眼，纷纷献诗。
初时酸儒们揣度上意，以为金枝玉叶必喜琼琚之辞，遂极尽辞藻堆砌之能事，恨不得字字引经，句句据典，艰深晦涩，佶屈聱牙。
不料公主朱批：此等酸腐馊饭，混着书虫蛀粉，臭不可闻！
反观牧羊儿戏作《白雪无垢》诗："无垢高塔戳破天，大雪盖它三层棉。神仙路过要缩脖，怕把玉帝帽子掀。"，倒引得公主击节，选作榜首。
昔曹子建七步成诗，今凉州百姓七步成趣，此方谓'清水出芙蓉'真谛。

那牧羊儿本是窣利商队遗落凉州的羯鼓手，一心想要去往遥远的撒马尔罕——那是他梦中的福地，他想去看看那里的树上是不是真的结着传说中的金色桃子。
得了公主的赏金，牧羊儿买下一匹白马，便出发了。

数年后，牧羊儿再回凉州，听闻公主已殁，便牵着当年的那匹马，前往拜祭。
白马成了老马，牧羊儿也成了老叟。老马驮着老叟走到望帝乡前，呼出最后一口气后，便双双死去了。

是夜，望帝乡前月明如水，有人说看到了公主的魂魄，依旧是初见牧羊儿时的模样。
见到了金色桃子的牧羊儿将白马回赠给了一生困于凉州的公主。年轻的白马驮着远行的大唐女儿，踩着月光铺就的大道，一步一步走回了长安。
en:
After the princess offered a huge reward for poems about "Liangzhou's Ten Scenery Spots," people scrambled to present their works, hoping to gain her favor. 
At first, pedantic scholars tried to guess her preferences, thinking the imperial princess must favor elegant, obscure verses. They piled up flowery words, quoting classics in every line, making their poems incomprehensibly rigid. 
Unexpectedly, the princess wrote a red comment, "Such stale, pedantic nonsense, mixed with bookworm dust, utterly stinking!" 
In contrast, a shepherd boy's playful poem "Snowy Purity" won her enthusiastic praise and was ranked first, "A pure tower pierces the sky, covered in three layers of snow like cotton. Immortals passing by huddle their necks, afraid of knocking off the Jade Emperor's hat." 
Once, Cao Zijian composed a poem in seven steps. Today, the common people of Liangzhou create charm in seven steps, this is the true meaning of "natural beauty like lotus emerging from clear water." 

That shepherd boy was originally a Suli merchant caravan's drummer left behind in Liangzhou. He yearned to go to distant Samarkand, his dreamland of bliss. He wanted to see if trees there truly bore the legendary golden peaches. 
Having received the princess's reward, the shepherd boy bought a white horse and set off. 

Several years later, the shepherd boy returned to Liangzhou. Hearing the princess had passed away, he led that same horse to pay respects. 
The white horse became an old horse and the shepherd boy became an old man. The old horse carried the old man before imperial capital. After exhaling its last breath, both died together. 

That night, the moon before imperial capital was bright as water. Some said they saw the princess's spirit, still looking as she did when she first met the shepherd boy. 
The shepherd boy who had seen the golden peaches gifted the white horse back to the princess who had spent her life confined to Liangzhou. The young white horse carried the far-traveling Tang daughter, treading the moonlit-paved road, step by step back to Chang'an.

en: Completed during the Liang dynasty of the Southern Dynasties. Emperor Wu of Liang commissioned the scholar Zhou Xingsi to compile a text by tracing the surviving calligraphy of the great master Wang Xizhi. Zhou selected exactly one thousand non-repeating characters and wove them into a masterpiece. The entire text is composed of four-character lines, totaling two hundred and fifty verses, rhyming flawlessly from beginning to end. It covers everything from astronomy, geography, and history to ethics, agriculture, and daily life. From the Tang dynasty onward, it served as an essential primer for children. Later, it joined Hundred Family Surnames and Three Character Classic to form the famous "Three, Hundred, Thousand" series of early education.

家家户户飘起了肉香，福宝已经坐在这里等了很久，可主人还是没有回来。
福宝时常觉得主人在家时，一天过得很快。仿佛只是跟主人玩儿了会儿球，太阳就从东边到了西边。可是，主人离开了，福宝一动不动地蹲坐在门口发呆，也不知道过了多久，天才黑下来。
主人留下的吃食还有很多，福宝却觉得自己不能再这样等下去了。
最近天气越来越凉，万一主人在外面冻坏了可怎么办，一向胆小的它迈出了家门。
它嗅着主人的味道，走过繁华，也路过寂静，和流浪狗抢吃食，喝着以前从未尝过的脏水。有人拿着香喷喷的肉想收养它，福宝叼起了肉，撒腿就跑。
终于，主人的味道越来越浓烈，福宝汪汪叫着窜到了主人的面前。看着主人欣喜又惊讶，它发出了委屈的呜咽声。
福宝知道，它才不是没有家的小狗。
en:
The aroma of meat wafts from every home. Fortune Treasure sits waiting for a long, long time, but its owner still doesn't return.
Fortune Treasure often feels that when his owner is home, the day passes quickly. A few games of fetch, and the sun moves from east to west. But now, with his owner gone, Fortune Treasure just crouches by the door, staring blankly. He doesn't know how long it has been before the sky darkens.
There is plenty of food left, but Fortune Treasure feels he cannot wait any longer.
It grows colder each day. What if his owner freezes out there? Timid as he is, he steps out the door.
He follows his owner's scent through busy streets and quiet paths. He fights stray dogs for food. He drinks dirty water he has never tasted before. Someone tries to adopt him with fragrant meat, but Fortune Treasure snatches it and runs.
Finally, his owner's scent grows stronger. Fortune Treasure bounds forward, barking wildly, and appears before him. Seeing his owner's joy and surprise, he whines pitifully.
Fortune Treasure knows that he is not a dog without a home.

zh:
游侠，见字如面。
前些时日，老朽随府尹大人巡查蒙学，见学堂里的娃娃们一个个正襟危坐，埋首书卷，连我等走近了都未曾察觉。
老朽心下好奇，是何等妙文，能让这些上蹿下跳的娃娃们如此专心？一问才知，他们手中所读，竟是你前些时日所赠。
老朽又问，这些书好在何处？娃娃们七嘴八舌，老朽这才知道，原来你竟为每个孩子都择了不同的书，实在是费心了。而听闻老朽与你相熟，他们都央着我，定要代他们向你道声谢。
只是，真要问他们想说什么，这群小家伙却面露羞赧，讷讷而止了。最后，老朽想了个法子，让他们把想说的话都诉诸笔端，一并封在信里了。至于写了什么，老朽绝未偷看！
对了，娃娃们还托我转交几幅画作，说是读了书卷后的有感而发。他们都说，游侠你是他们见过最有眼光的人，定能欣赏他们的大作。
哈哈，看来往后若再有与孩子们打交道的差事，找游侠准是没错了。

en:
Dear Wanderer,

The other day, I accompanied the Prefect on an inspection of the village school. The children sat straight at their desks, noses buried in scrolls, so absorbed they didn't even notice us draw near.
Curious what could hold their attention so completely, I asked. Turns out, they were reading the very books you gifted them not long ago.
I inquired further: what made these books so special? The little ones burst into chatter, and that's when I learned you had chosen a different book for each child. What thoughtfulness.
When they heard I knew you, they begged me to pass along their thanks.
But when I asked what they wanted to say, shyness took over, and words failed them. So I suggested they write it down instead. Their letters are enclosed. And no, I did not peek!
Oh, and they also asked me to send you a few drawings. Inspired, they said, by your books. They all agreed you're the most discerning person they've ever met, and that you'd surely appreciate their masterpieces.
Seems to me, whenever there's a task involving children, you're the one to call.

zh:
笨笨是真的很笨。
教它握手，它只会歪过脑袋傻傻地看着你；教它名字，也要喊上三四遍才能慢吞吞地抬头；不管谁来喂它，它都会尾巴摇得像小桨，没心没肺地埋头苦吃，甚至一脑袋栽进食盆里，好像天生少根弦。
那是一个赶集的日子，笨笨追着蝴蝶，深一脚浅一脚地跑到了人群最密的地方，等它回过神来时，蝴蝶早没了影，四下都是陌生的气味，来时的路也被踩得一塌糊涂。
笨笨很笨，连家的方向在哪里都分不清，只能用最笨的办法试错，走错，再退回，再走错，再退回。日头从高高的耸翠楼下沉到湖山一线，笨笨慢吞吞地走过卖花的船舶、走过从没见过的石桥，走过来往的人群。
入夜，主人家的门忽然被拱开，一团脏兮兮的小毛团冲了进来，扑到主人身上，尾巴摇得飞快。
en:
Bumble really is a bumbler.
Teach him to shake and he only tilts his head and stares at you. Teach him his name and it takes three or four tries before he slowly looks up. No matter who comes to feed him, he wags his tail like a little oar, then buries his face in his food without a care in the world, sometimes tipping headfirst into the bowl. As though he'd been born a little slow.
It was market day. Chasing a butterfly, Bumble stumbled his way into the thick of the crowd. By the time he came to his senses, the butterfly was long gone, every smell around him was strange, and the way back had been trampled over by too many feet.
Bumble was dumb. He couldn't even tell which way home was, so he tried it the dumbest way: wrong turn, double back, another wrong turn, double back again. The sun sank from high above the Verdant Tavern to the line where the lake met the hills. Bumble plodded past the flower boats, past a stone bridge he had never seen, past the crowds coming and going.
After dark, the door of his owner's house was suddenly nudged open. A filthy little ball of fur came barreling in and threw itself at him, tail wagging faster than ever before.

江流天地外，山色有无中。孙愿曾见《嘉陵江三百里风光图》，观后登高，一时畅快，挥扇泼墨间，似见青山共执笔墨，势如山水，招招不可阻挡，可回神后，再也无法施展此中扇招。

en:
Rivers flow beyond the realm of earth, and mountain hues shimmer between presence and absence. Sun Yuan once gazed upon the Scenic Scroll of the Three Hundred Miles of Jialing River. Inspired, he climbed to a high peak. In a moment of exhilaration, he wielded his fan with the flourish of splattered ink, as if painting with the mountains themselves, each stroke unstoppable, like a living landscape. But once the trance faded, he could never use that fan technique again.
Ten years passed. A bell chimed in the clouds. And in that instant, Sun Yuan recalled the feeling, and the Inkwell Fan resurfaced in the jianghu once more.

zh: 把子肉据说与古代公祭有关——古人公祭后将祭祀用的肉切成长方块，扎上青蒲草或马蔺草形成扎把，分送给参祭的人拿回家用酱炖着吃，于是渐渐就有了把子肉这道特色美食。民间还有将把子肉的起源推到东汉末年刘关张拜把子，张飞屠猪煮肉的说法。但桃园结义之事并不见于正史，此说多半是后人附会，虽不足信，却也颇有趣味，聊备一格。
en: Meat Stew is said to have originated from ancient sacrificial rites. After the rites, the sacrificial meat will be cut into rectangular chunks, tied with cattail or rush grass into bundles, and distributed to the participants to take home and braise in soy sauce, gradually evolving into the dish known today. Another folk tale traces its origins to the Oath of the Peach Garden at the end of the Eastern Han Dynasty. After Liu Bei, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei took an oath of fraternity in the Peach Garden, Zhang made a dish of stewed pork. Though the story is not recorded in official history and is likely a later embellishment, it adds a colorful layer to the dish's legacy.
