zh:
父兄怯敌畏战的罪名传来时，丁笑稍有恍神，却多少也信了几分。
只因他想起幼时曾偷看父亲教兄长练刀。
父亲将刀横转，说明刀与剑不同——刀重在守，人，应在刀背之后。
你们兄弟二人，一个练刀，一个握笔，一守一攻。正好。
彼时，丁笑不懂，为何持刀者要藏，自己手中的笔，却算得上武器。
后来城破，家散，他被牵连入狱。想来皆因父兄太怯，藏得太深。
狱中寒夜，丁笑无故挨打，蜷身在地，只见月光淌过地面，清透似霜粉。
令他想起不久前还吃过的甜糕，他忍不住抬手轻触，却只得指尖冰凉——人生至此，只剩苦味。
这种苦味，让他下定决心，要换一种有别父兄的活法。

出狱后，他先学会了笑。
再学会了见人先躬身，说话三分敬。
更往后，他学会了如何把字写得圆融。笔真成了武器，尽管不愿承认，但或许父亲也不全错。
如此一来，很快窄路渐宽。有人送钱、有人称兄、而自己，更能在军帐中有个座位。
他又过回了比常人还要富裕的日子，每天都要去买半包甜糕，细细嚼。
直至那个叫做孟宽的人出现，带来父兄之死的真相。只短短四字：援军未至。
原来父兄并非藏于刀后。他们是被人，当成了刀。

得知真相后，丁笑也曾试过再为杜砌银提笔。
或因心神犹疑，墨迹总在纸上晕开。
这些年来，自己何尝不是一把刀呢？藏于躬身的笑脸后、藏于恭顺的笔墨间。
可人藏于刀背，为先作格挡，再谋良机，反击劈砍，攻其不备。
原来父亲，真是对的。
他懂得太晚，也已藏得够久。若要再起攻势……就是现在了。

那夜，窗外无月。
却是丁笑自父兄死后第一次尝出甜糕的甜味。
或许等事毕之后，这份曾经任谁来要也不给的甜，也能分给别人了。
en:
When word came that his father and brother had been condemned for fearing the enemy and shirking battle, Ding Xiao was briefly stunned.
But part of him believed it.

He thought back to when he was young and once secretly watched his father teaching his elder brother how to use a blade.
His father turned the blade sideways and said a blade was not like a sword. A blade was for guarding. The person should stay behind the blade.

"You two brothers, one takes the blade, one takes the brush. One guards, one attacks. That works out just right."

Back then, Ding Xiao did not understand why the one holding the blade had to hide, while the brush in his own hand was supposed to count as a weapon.
Later the city fell, the family was torn apart, and he too was dragged into prison.

Looking back, he thought it was all because his father and brother had been too timid, hiding themselves too well.

On cold nights in prison, he would be beaten for no reason at all. Curled up on the ground, he watched moonlight spill across the floor, pale and clear like powdered frost.
It reminded him of the sweet cakes he had eaten not long before. He could not help reaching out to touch it, only to feel cold at his fingertips.

By then, life seemed to hold nothing but bitterness.
And that bitterness made him decide he would live a different kind of life from his father and brother.

After he got out of prison, the first thing he learned was how to smile.
Then he learned to bow before speaking to people, and to lace every word with just the right amount of respect.
Later on, he learned how to round out his handwriting until it looked smooth and agreeable.

The brush really did become a weapon. Much as he hated to admit it, maybe his father had not been entirely wrong.
And once he learned all that, the narrow road in front of him quickly began to widen.
Some sent him money. Some called him brother. And he himself won a seat in the command tent.
He went back to living better than most people. Every day he bought half a packet of sweet cakes and ate them slowly, bite by bite.

That lasted until the man named Meng Kuan appeared and brought him the truth of how his father and brother had died.

Just three words:

Reinforcements never came.

So his father and brother had not hidden behind the blade after all.
They had been used as one.

After learning the truth, Ding Xiao tried once more to write for Du Qiyin.
But perhaps because his mind would not settle, the ink kept spreading across the page.

All these years, had he himself not also been a blade?
Hidden behind a smiling bow. Hidden inside obedient brushstrokes.
But when a person stays behind the blade, it is to block first, wait for the right opening, and then strike back when the moment comes.

So his father had been right.
He had only understood it too late, and he had hidden long enough.
If he was going to strike now, it had to be now.

That night, there was no moon outside the window.
And yet for the first time since his father and brother died, Ding Xiao could taste the sweetness in the cakes again.

Perhaps when all this was over, he could finally share that sweetness, the sweetness he had never been willing to give anyone before.

en:
Submitted by: Pan'er, Registry Director
Subject: Post-New Year staffing shortfalls across the Six Offices

After the New Year, many palace attendants are expected to be released from service, while newly recruited attendants are not yet fully trained. All Offices are short-handed. I respectfully request Your Ladyship's instructions.

I. Registry Office
Current situation: Despite coordinating the Six Offices, the Registry Office is struggling to keep up. Paperwork is severely backlogged.
Staffing:
- Herald Chief: Previously staffed by 1; that person has left the palace. Only 1 female clerk remains. She carries edicts between the Secretariat and the inner palace 12 times a day, and her feet are badly swollen, making it difficult to walk. Request: assign 2 nimble new attendants to assist.
- Records Chief: During the release period, the Records Chief must verify the departure rolls day and night to avoid errors or omissions. She has gone three days without proper sleep, and files are piling up.

II. Etiquette Office
Current situation: Ritual and music duties are heavy but still manageable. The main shortfall is general support.
Staffing:
- Rites Chief (Shuyu): Overextended. She must oversee court-assembly protocols and teach 3 new attendants to read musical notation. Rehearsals for next month's new piece have not yet begun.
- Archives Chief (Du Ruo): With clear weather, book airing was scheduled to finish in 3 days. With no laborers available to move the books, Du Ruo must move several hundred volumes alone. Completion may be delayed to 10 days.

III. Wardrobe Office
Current situation: Seasonal garment-making and ornament production overlap. Manpower is insufficient.
Staffing:
- Robes Chief: Winter garments must be rushed. Skilled embroiderers have resigned and returned home. The supervisor is cutting patterns herself, while new attendants are assigned to sewing. Their stitching is rough and may not meet standards.
- Adornment Chief: At Mao hour, 6 staff must be assigned to Baoci Palace to assist with dressing and hair, leaving the gold-and-jade workshop unmanned. Orders from the various palaces cannot be delivered on time. Request: an extension.

IV. Culinary Office
Current situation: Meals are critical. Staff loss is the most severe here, creating significant risks.
Staffing:
- Provisions Chief: The head cooks remain, but most workers for washing vegetables and tending fires have left. All staff have had rest days suspended and must begin ingredient prep at Yin hour daily. Without new staff, discontent is likely.
- Wine Chief: Due to shortages, 1 female clerk must watch over 3 cellars, with no night relief. Continued operation poses a theft risk.

V. Bedchamber Office
Current situation: Night duty is the most exhausting. Fatigue is widespread, and breakage has increased.
Staffing:
- Lamp Chief: Night-watch attendants have dropped sharply. Remaining staff must take consecutive night shifts and sleep only about 6 hours by day. She is already impaired by fatigue and has broken 1 glass lamp.
- Furnishings Chief: Thanks to frugality measures across the palaces, replacement frequency for bed hangings and carpets has decreased. Senior attendants can manage for now.

VI. Crafts Office
Current situation: Repairs are numerous and varied. Only the most urgent work can be handled first.
Staffing:
- Tailoring Chief: Several of His Majesty's old garments require delicate mending, which is time-consuming. All other clothing sent from the various palaces will be postponed until next month.
- Gardens Chief: Expansion areas are unattended and overgrown. With no dedicated staff available, Bedchamber Office cleaning attendants have been temporarily assigned pruning and watering duties as well.

en: The garments sold in the secondhand clothing trade came from all sorts of places: forfeited pawnshop items, cast-offs sold by commoners, cheaply made new clothes, and even stolen goods. 唐·刘禹锡

孔子云：“何陋之有？”
en:
Inscription on a Humble Abode
By Liu Yuxi, Tang Dynasty

A mountain needn't be high; 
It is famous so long as there is a deity on it.
A lake needn't be deep; 
It has supernatural power so long as there is a dragon in it. 
My home is humble, 
But it enjoys the fame of virtue so long as I am living in it.
The moss creeping onto the doorsteps turns them green. 
The color of the grass reflected through the bamboo curtains turns the room blue. 
Erudite scholars come in good spirits to talk with me, 
And among my guests there is no unlearned common man. 
In this humble room, I can enjoy playing my plainly decorated qin, or read the Buddhist Scriptures quietly,
Without the disturbance of the noisy that jar on the ears, or the solemn burden of reading official documents. 
My humble home is like the thatched hut of Zhuge Liang of Nanyang, or the Pavilion Ziyun of Xishu.
Confucius once said, "How could we call a room humble as long as there is a virtuous man in it?”
Jiang Dong Hui

zh: 云母岩质薄如蝉翼，层叠如书页，光莹若水镜，色或白若霜雪，或黑如玄墨，或间青紫，触之滑腻，叩之有声。可剥为片，片片透光，故古称“光明石”。其性耐火，烈焰炙之而不毁。贵族常以云母片制作屏风，李商隐诗《嫦娥》云“云母屏风烛影深”。光影斑驳，半透朦胧，美不胜收。
en: Mica rock is as sheer as a cicada's wing, layered like the pages of a book, and glistening like a clear water mirror. Its colors vary significantly: some are white as frost and snow, some black as dark ink, and others interwoven with cyan and purple. It is smooth to the touch and produces a resonant sound when struck. Because it can be peeled into translucent flakes, the ancients called it the "Luminous Stone." It is highly fire-resistant and remains intact even when scorched by roaring flames. Nobles frequently use these mica flakes to craft ornamental folding screens. As the poet Li Shangyin wrote in his poem Chang'e, "Candlelight casts deep shadows across the mica screen." The mottled light and shadows create a hazy, semi-transparent beauty that is truly breathtaking.

zh: 百工坊，旧名西坊。建隆元年，朝廷于此筑修造案官署，广纳四方能工巧匠。百姓多得财而去，此地更名百工坊，民间仍习称西坊。尝闻荥阳郑氏于此有别院一间，两年前，修造案以郑氏没落、此地亦空置良久为由，拆除别院，于密室中得珍玩甚众，故就地筑奇物监以藏之。坊内非止木工、铁器之坊，亦有瓷窑、染坊、造纸坊、造船务，日夜炉火不息。开封漕运关隘亦在此地，名曰天京渡。然则漕运诸事皆为青蛟堂帮众所司，不知何故。
en: The Imperial Artisan Court, formerly known as West Market. In the 1st year of the Jianlong Reign (960 CE), the imperial court built the Imperial Works Bureau here, recruiting skilled artisans from across the land. As commoners prospered through trade, the area was renamed the Imperial Artisan Court—though locals still call it West Ward. It's said the Xingyang Zheng family once had a villa here. Two years ago, the Imperial Works Bureau demolished it, citing the Zheng clan's decline and long vacancy, then built the Artifacts Bureau on-site after unearthing countless rare curios in a hidden chamber. The district hosts not just carpentry and blacksmith workshops, but also porcelain kiln, dye works, paper workshops, and Shipyard Bureau—forges burn day and night. Kaifeng's canal checkpoint, Tianjing Dock, is also located here, strangely overseen by the Jade Serpent Hall.

zh:
书接上回，这天泉的陈尧自打被那九流门的恶徒骗走了帮派发派的钱财，受了堂主的指摘，便郁郁在胸，誓要报酬雪恨。他日日盘桓在开封城内，欲凭那恶徒身上扯下来的面具，寻得那人的踪迹，可九流门神出鬼没，面具种类又多，连查了十数日，竟是一无所获。
这一日，陈尧又喝空了酒葫芦，坐在灰坑边上打盹，却忽然被争执声吵醒，原是一群无忧帮的恶徒，正欺负一个小姑娘。正愁心烦无处发泄，他冷笑一声，掰掰手指，扭扭脖子，便扛刀走了上去。未到半柱香功夫，方才气势汹汹的大汉便屁滚尿流地伏了一地磕头求饶，陈尧甩了甩头发，也不理他们，只向那倒在地上的姑娘伸出手去，可视线一对上，他便愣住了。
什么小姑娘……分明是那骗了自己的恶徒！
“好你个恶徒，以为换身女装我便不认得你了……”陈尧破口大骂，可话还没说完，他便两眼一黑，软倒了下去。
再醒来时，他竟发现自己躺在一张华丽的绣床上，满屋缭绕着旖旎香气，他欲起身，却发现自己被点了穴，连话也说不出来，他急得哼哼，却见一只削葱般的玉指抵在了他的唇上，正是那恶……正是那恶徒穿着一身醉花阴的衣裙，半伏在他的身上，狡黠地对他一笑：
“好恩人，本想先处置你，可门派有急事儿，抱歉啊，借你一用。”
en:
Picking up where we left off—
Ever since Chen Yao of the Well of Heaven Sect was duped by a rogue from Nine Mortal Ways, losing the sect's funds and drawing a harsh rebuke from his hall master, he had brooded bitterly, swearing to avenge his humiliation. Day after day, he lurked in the streets of Kaifeng, hoping to track down the thief by the mask he ripped off from his face. But Nine Mortal Ways were as elusive as ghosts, and masks were a dime a dozen. After ten fruitless days, he had nothing to show for his efforts.

One day, after draining his wine gourd dry, Chen Yao dozed off by the Ash Pit, only to be roused by the sounds of a scuffle. A gang of Unbound Cavern thugs were bullying a little girl. Already in a foul mood, Chen Yao cracked his knuckles, rolled his neck, and walked over with a blade in hand. In no time, the once ferocious brawny men were groveling on the ground, sobbing and begging for mercy. Chen Yao tossed his hair disdainfully, ignoring them. He reached out a hand to the girl lying crumpled on the ground, only to freeze.

A girl? No, it was the rogue who had tricked him!

"You wretched swindler! Think I wouldn't recognize you in a dress?" he bellowed. But before the words finished leaving his mouth, darkness closed over him, and he collapsed.

When he awoke, he found himself lying atop a lavishly embroidered bed, the air thick with intoxicating fragrance. He tried to get up, but realized his pressure points had been sealed, he couldn't even speak. Panicked, he began to groan softly. Until a slender, delicate finger pressed against his lips. It was that rogue again, this time clad in a gauzy Velvet Shades dress, leaning coyly over him, flashing a mischievous smile:

"Dear benefactor," she purred, "I had such plans for you, but something urgent has arisen in the sect. Forgive me, I'll just be borrowing you for a little while."
